Independent input evidence. Tamil urupu/uruvu, Malayalam uruvam and Telugu uruvu/uravu share a vowel-first shape-word family. DEDR explicitly queries derivation from Sanskrit rūpa.

Direction. Under inherited analysis the attested regional order is u–r; under borrowing analysis it could arise from prothesis/adaptation of initial rū-. Neither should be silently treated as established.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional uru-v gives Telugu uruvu and related forms without metathesis. A loan route rūpa > *urūpa > urupu/uruvu requires prothesis, shortening and labial weakening; evidence here does not select that chain over inherited morphology.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a direction-sensitive loan control: treating Tamil urupu as necessarily conservative could reverse the history. Badaga bathing compound urugaṭṭu may have another ancestry; use the simplex uru only as a form witness.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 657, explicit ? < Skt. rūpa-

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uruku/urukku, Malayalam urukuka/urukku and Kannada urku independently support a u-vowel velar formation. The steel noun and melt verb have related but distinct morphological histories.

Direction. Southern and Gondi vowel-first forms support older u–r; eastern rūg/rūy is displaced under the melt comparison. Telugu ukku retains the initial vowel and loses medial r.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ur-ukk > *urkk > ukku gives the Telugu steel noun by syncope/assimilation. *ur-uk > *rūg gives Konda/Kui melt stems through displacement/contraction and voicing. Kui ūra/ūrka retains initial vowel with a long root, whereas rūga displaces it in the velar formation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kui is genuinely mixed within one source, so its retained forms cannot be coded missing or assigned to a separate outcome-defined root. Kuvi uku/ukku steel may be a regional technical loan or parallel medial assimilation; either way it is not the same displaced melt formation as rūy. d656 burn is a plausible parent-root relation, to be collapsed in sensitivity counts.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 661 p.64 directly checked

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam uruvu and Kannada urcu independently support vowel-first rhotic. Tulu urumbuni supplies a nasal-labial formation beside rummuni.

Direction. Independent full forms favor u–r; Telugu uccu can arise by medial cluster assimilation, while Tulu rummuni is compatible with a local initial-loss history.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ur-c > ucc yields Telugu uccu, Kannada uccu and Parji ucc, preserving initial vowel. Tulu urumbuni > rummuni would combine initial-vowel loss with nasal/labial assimilation; a literal u/r swap is not distinguishable with identical u vowels. Kuvi uh/ust reflects another medial cluster development.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not infer hidden initial metathesis from the absence of r in Telugu: the independent Kannada urcu : uccu comparison supports medial assimilation directly. Kurux hurnā/huṛnā has an added initial h but retains the root vowel before r. Shared ucc forms could also diffuse; no precise shared-innovation date follows.

Mechanism scope. Medial cluster assimilation; Tulu initial loss or displacement not uniquely resolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR 663 p.64 directly checked

d664: roll, round object, wheel, egg

PropertyAnnotation

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uruḷ/uruṇṭai, Malayalam uruḷ/uruṇṭa and Kannada uruḷ/uraḷu/uraṇṭu independently establish r before later lateral/nasal-stop material. Original DEDR p.64 restores Telugu uralu/urlu/oralu, mislabeled Kodagu in the database.

Direction. Broad r-before-lateral agreement supports earlier urVḷ. Telugu uṇḍa loses/assimilates medial r in a round-object formation; Pengo rōnḍa/Manda runḍa promote r under the proposed egg-from-round comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. Telugu *ur-aḷ > uralu > urlu retains initial order; *uruṇṭ > *urṇḍ > uṇḍa loses r medially. *urṇḍ > uṇḍr could instead underlie uṇḍramu/uṇḍrālu, but suffixal r or analogy is not excluded. Pengo *ur-aṇḍ > *rōṇḍ and Manda *ur-uṇḍ > runḍ are conditional different-vowel paths; neither exact egg input is independently fixed.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The existence of Kannada both u and a does not license choosing whichever vowel produces the eastern outcome. Pengo egg is long rōnḍa, explicitly corrected by DEN1; Manda is short runḍa. Irula ruḷḷu/ruṭṭu may reflect local aphaeresis and strengthening. Sanskrit round-lump words are contact comparisons. Modern Telugu round-cake derivatives count once, and their possible medial r transposition is separate from initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 664 p.64 directly checked; DEN1 p.401 Pengo correction

d665 — rub, grind, touchstone; pestle

d665: rub, grind, touchstone; pestle

PropertyAnnotation

Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil urai, Malayalam urayuka and Kannada ore establish a low-ay formation; Kannada urdu/uddu/ujju independently supplies the medial dental cluster relevant to Telugu ruddu. Labial rubbing formations occur in Tamil/Malayalam, but their precise vowel varies.

Direction. Multiple independent full roots support earlier u–r. Telugu orayu retains the low-ay formation while ruddu/rubbu promotes r in other formations; this is not a reversal of the same fully specified stem in every derivative.

Derivation and relative chronology. K61 p.55 derives ruddu from *ur-d and rubbu from *ur-upp: *ur-d > *ru-dd, and *ur-upp > *ru-pp > rubbu with displacement and strengthening/voicing. *ur-ay > *or-ay > orayu retains order. Kannada urdu > uddu/ujju instead assimilates r medially. Konda rōs can reflect a low-a derivative; Kui rūsa and Kuvi rub require distinct high-vowel/consonantal formations.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu rō̃kali is explicitly questioned and compared alternatively with d672 ulakkai pestle; its r/l ancestry is not solved by the rub root. Kannada rubbu may be inherited displacement or a Telugu loan; Kannada ruddu and Telugu ruttu are explicitly queried in the original source. Kolami/Naikri/Gondi pestle names are explicitly Telugu loans and are excluded from independent innovations. Telugu retained low-a forms remain genuine counterexamples to obligatory application.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 665 p.64 directly checked; K61 p.55 §1.131 inspected in Google Books; alternative d672

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Kannada urbu/urvu beside ubbu, Tulu urkuni beside ukkuni and Konda/Kui urp independently support medial rhotic-plus-stop clusters. Root quantity alternates and is not fixed by a single proto-head.

Direction. Independent retained clusters favor r after u; assimilated labial/velar forms do not require initial promotion of r.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ur-p > *urb > ubb gives Telugu ubbu and related forms; *ur-k > ukk produces local boil-over forms. Telugu ūru keeps a long rhotic root. ubuku may reflect a labial root plus velar extension rather than direct r-to-b conversion, so its full derivation is separate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a widespread negative for initial displacement and a positive for medial assimilation. Exact Proto-Dravidian quantity and whether all swelling/boiling words descend from one root remain uncertain. Tamil upparam is explicitly Telugu-borrowed. A Manda label was swallowed into a Pengo record; do not count the duplicate Pengo-looking stem as an independent language without source correction.

Mechanism scope. Medial rhotic assimilation, not initial displacement.

Independent input evidence. Tamil ulakkai, Malayalam ulakka, Kannada olake and Kodagu oḷake establish vowel-first lateral plus velar tool name. The linked Indo-Aryan mortar words form a separate comparison, not many independent Dravidian witnesses.

Direction. Vowel-first order is supported within the southern comparison. The relationship to Indo-Aryan ulūkhala and Telugu rō̃kali (queried under d665) does not establish a uniquely recoverable pan-Dravidian input.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ulakkay > olake/oḷake includes lowering and daughter-language suffix changes; Kannada onake/onike has lateral-to-nasal variation. Kota elk has syncope. Toda vas̱k requires initial glide and lateral/velar developments; no initial promotion of l is visible.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No Telugu record is linked here. Deriving Telugu rō̃kali from this rather than rub d665 would require an independently justified l/r correspondence and nasal origin; preserve both hypotheses. Kuruba alke is wrongly labeled Malayalam in the corpus. Do not count either the large Indo-Aryan contact fan-out or pestle derivatives as independent Dravidian etyma.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 672; compare d665, d651; Indo-Aryan CDIAL 2360

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Malayalam uẓiyuka/uẓivu establishes vowel-first ẓ in the stroke family; Kannada ūḍu preserves vowel-first retroflex with long quantity. DEDR separates a stroke/scrape series from a long ū-s anoint series.

Direction. Earlier u–ẓ is plausible for the stroke comparison, reinforced by comb d689. Whether the ū-s series reflects earlier ẓ loss or an independent root is not settled by combining the source’s two subentries.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *uẓ-v > *ẓuvv > ḍuvv > duvvu gives Telugu stroke, sharing the comb formation in d689. *uẓ-u-s > *ẓūs could yield eastern ṛūs; an alternative *ūẓ-s > ūs accounts for vowel-first anoint forms by medial assimilation. ṛūs > ūs through later initial-r loss is another testable concealed-metathesis hypothesis, but requires independent evidence of that initial loss.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not assign all ū-s forms a definite retained or concealed-metathesized status: the contrast may predate the proposed event. The exact V2 of Telugu duvvu cannot be inferred from modern u alone. Pengo ṛoh and Kui ṛōsa have an additional vowel-quality problem. Shared Telugu duvvu stroke/comb means d686+d689 form one primary counting family.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 686(a,b) p.67 directly checked; compare 689

d688: plough, root up soil

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd688
Comparative input*uẓ-u; *uẓ-n- verb and *uẓ-kk- noun

Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencehigh
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam uẓu, Kannada uẓ and Central Dravidian ur/uṛ independently support vowel-first approximant root. K03 pp.152–153 distinguishes Telugu nasal plough verb and velar tillage noun from the eastern vowel-final formation.

Direction. Independent southern/central order favors u–ẓ. Eastern ṛū and Telugu dunnu/dukki are displaced under the shared root comparison; initial ẓ then has its separate daughter-language reflexes.

Derivation and relative chronology. K03 derives *uẓ-n > *ẓun(n) > ḍunn > dunnu, and *uẓ-kk > *ẓukk > ḍukk > dukki. Eastern *uẓ-u > *ẓū > ṛū contracts matching vowels. These are distinct independently discussed formations; Telugu short u need not be a shortened reflex of eastern long ū.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kui ūṛa root up retains vowel first beside ṛūva plough; its semantic/formation split must remain mixed. Gondi lum/lumm root/gore may be displaced but requires approximant-to-l and suffix history, and the gore comparison is explicitly queried. Tulu dappuni/aḍapuni has dialectal initial-vowel loss and a different vowel/root history; source corrections restore those forms from mistaken Kodagu labels. Tamil tunnu and Parji ḍukki are explicit Telugu loans. Agriculture-contact possibilities do not by themselves negate the deep comparative root.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.152–153 example 86; PSS83 p.235 example 781; DEDR 688 p.67 directly checked

d689 — comb, arrange hair

d689: comb, arrange hair

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd686+d689
Comparative input*uẓ-u/v; consonantal labial expansion
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantityu / short
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu/zero
Root/formation shapeVC-u / VC-v
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceLabial expansion independently preserved in Parji/Gadaba; comb-tool suffix not counted as another root.
Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uẓu, Parji uṛ/uṛv and Gadaba uḍuv/uṛv independently support earlier vowel–approximant order and a labial extension. Gondi uṛ/ūs corroborates the root; Tamil uḷar is explicitly queried.

Direction. Agreement of SD I and Central Dravidian supports u–ẓ independently of Telugu. Telugu duvvu and eastern ḍūs/ṛūc are innovative under the hair-arranging comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uẓ-v > *ẓuvv > ḍuvv > duvvu, with labial strengthening and later initial ḍ>d, gives Telugu comb. Konda ḍūs and Kuvi ṛūc reflect different coronal extensions and possibly vowel contraction. Kodagu ū-k and Naiki ū instead lose the medial approximant while keeping the vowel first.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The identical Telugu stroke duvvu in d686 is counted in the same primary family. Gondi Koya dus might be borrowed from a neighboring displaced language or reflect a local innovation; root and suffix history do not decide it yet. Tulu dūbina is a possible Telugu-area loan or local displacement, while urvaṇe retains order. Tamil uḷar does not establish a second lateral root without further evidence.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 689 p.67 directly checked; comparison with stroke d686

d690 — black gram

d690: black gram

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd690
Comparative input*uẓ-unt- / *uẓ-untu
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantityu / short
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu
Root/formation shapeVC-u-NT
Grammatical categorynoun
Boundary evidenceNasal-stop crop-name formation independently matched.
Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uẓuntu, Malayalam uẓunnu and Kolami urunde preserve vowel–approximant–vowel–nasal-stop order. Kannada urdu/uddu supplies the intermediate medial cluster and its assimilated outcome.

Direction. Independent full southern and central forms favor an earlier initial vowel; Telugu uddulu lacks the medial approximant because of cluster reduction, not initial promotion.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uẓ-unt > *ur-nd > *ur-d > udd, with nasal/stop simplification and assimilation, is a schematic route to Telugu uddulu. Exact sequencing of nasal loss and r assimilation may differ; Kannada urdu : uddu directly supports the latter step.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This same-u comparison retains the initial vowel despite the shared approximant found in displaced comb/tiger. Crop-name borrowing can spread either full or reduced forms, so branch distribution cannot by itself date each sound change. Marathi/Prakrit urad names are contact comparisons, not independent evidence for Dravidian metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Medial approximant/cluster assimilation, with contact chronology unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR 690 p.67 directly checked; K03 *uẓ-untu reconstruction

d692 — tiger, panther

d692: tiger, panther

PropertyAnnotation

Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D

Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uẓuvai supplies a vowel-first approximant plus labial big-cat name. Gondi ḍuvval/ḍūāl and Telugu duvvu support the related labial formation but are not additional unshifted witnesses.

Direction. Vowel-first ancestry is supported by the established comparative approximant correspondence and the Tamil form, but only one unshifted lexical witness survives here; direction confidence is lower than in comb/plough.

Derivation and relative chronology. K03 p.162 gives *uẓ-(u)-w > *ẓu-ww > ḍuww > duvvu. Kolami/Parji ḍū can preserve an older borrowed ḍ-initial stem with later labial loss/contraction. Gondi quantity and labial variation needs separate dialect history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. K03 and PSS83 explicitly diagnose Kolami/Parji Telugu loans; their retained ḍ is evidence about relative borrowing chronology, not independent metathesis. Gondi ḍuhkyā/ḍuhkiak and Gadaba ḍuccā wolf are queried in DEDR and need separate cognacy. The identical Tamil fish name d693 is not merged on homophony alone.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 p.162; PSS83 p.235 example 782; DEDR 692 p.68 directly checked

Independent input evidence. Tamil uẓuvai/uḷuvai and Malayalam uẓuva support vowel-first approximant/lateral plus labial fish name. Telugu uṇuju has both nasal and palatal consonants in place of the expected sequence.

Direction. Southern vowel-first order is secure regionally; Telugu cognacy is not independently secured by the generic fish gloss.

Derivation and relative chronology. A path *uẓuvay > uṇuju would require ẓ > ṇ and v/y > j with additional vowel changes. No independently established conditions for those steps are supplied here. Initial vowel retention is observed, but a full inherited derivation remains unproved.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This superficially matches the input of tiger d692 and retains the initial vowel, yet cannot be advertised as a decisive sound-law falsifier until its nasal/palatal correspondence is explained. Better species identification, historical Telugu spellings and nearby fish names could distinguish changed cognacy from irregular sound change.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Parji uṛup independently supplies vowel-first approximant with high u and final labial. Tamil uẓai and Tulu ure/uḷe supply shorter related deer names; they do not themselves prove the labial suffix.

Direction. Parji’s full labial form and southern vowel-first shorter forms support earlier u–ẓ. Telugu duppi and Konda ḍupi are displaced under the independently supported labial comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uẓ-up(p) > *ẓup(p) > ḍupp > duppi, or matching-vowel contraction followed by shortening before pp; the short output alone does not decide between these timing alternatives. Gondi luppi/lūpi involves a lateral approximant reflex plus dialectal length/strength variation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kannada duppi, Kolami ḍuppi and Gadaba duppi may be regional loans; their donor histories are not established just by matching Telugu. Keep them uncertain in innovation counts. Parji uṛup is a valuable inherited-order control in the same family. Distinct animal suffixes and dialect variants are not extra etyma.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 694 p.68 directly checked; K03 *uẓ-u-pp reconstruction

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Telugu ūḍucu, Konda ūṛs and Gadaba ūrs support a long-vowel series; Kolami/Naikri uṛp and Gondi uṛp support short-vowel labial formations. No unshifted SD I comparator occurs in this entry.

Direction. Widespread vowel before apical establishes regional V–C order, but exact deeper approximant and root quantity are less secure. Source-corrected Kui ḍupka is the consonant-first comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. Long *ūẓ-s > ūṛs/ūḍcu retains initial order. Conditional short *uẓ-k-p > *ẓukp > ḍupk gives Kui ḍupka with a separate, morphologically explicit k-p > p-k exchange. Kui rūṭpa is queried and has extra dental/quantity changes.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This does not prove metathesis of an inherited long *ūẓ root: the Kui velar derivative may have a short stem allomorph, but that must be independently demonstrated. Until then its initial development is uncertain. The original source assigns ūṛs to Konda and both ḍupka/rūṭpa to Kui, not Gondi; that correction materially changes the geography.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 695 p.68 directly checked

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Kannada urcu and Tulu urcuni/uḷc preserve a medial liquid before a palatal; Gondi uṛk preserves a retroflex rhotic before a velar. The shared liquid identity and exact suffix relationship remain less certain than vowel-first order.

Direction. The full medial clusters support r/liquid before the final stop. Telugu ucca is compatible with medial assimilation, not movement of the liquid to onset.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ur-c > *ucc > Telugu ucca and Kannada uccu/ucce; Gondi *uṛ-k retains the liquid, while Kota uc and Toda ūc have local consonant/quantity histories.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not count medial liquid loss as hidden metathesis when an unchanged initial vowel and retained cluster comparanda provide a simpler account. Urine, purge and diarrhoea may share a root but distinct noun/verb derivations are not independent examples. The r/ẓ reconstruction should remain uncertain until more correspondences settle it.

Mechanism scope. Medial liquid assimilation, not initial displacement.

Scholarly references. DEDR 696 p.68 directly checked

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil and Malayalam uḷ, Kannada uḷ/oḷ and Kota oḷ independently support short vowel before lateral. The existential nasal-stop formation is explicitly reconstructed *uḷ-nt- by K03.

Direction. The full southern paradigms establish earlier u–ḷ without treating Telugu uṇḍu as an unchanged root. Its initial vowel survives an independently motivated medial cluster assimilation.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uḷ-nt > *uṇṭ > Telugu uṇḍu; related nasal causative unucu/uncu and existence noun uniki preserve the initial vowel. Toda viḷd-/vɨḍ- includes prothesis and internal strengthening. Kolami an-/Naikri anḍ require separate root-vowel history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kui lohpa and Kuvi loy/lōi are explicitly questioned in the source comparison; exact formative vowels and cognacy are unresolved. Their l-first appearance alone does not prove metathesis. Brahui anning has a suppletive-looking present uṭ/us/un/ure/ur in the source; full paradigm history is needed. Potential semantic connection with inside d698 is a sensitivity merge, not evidence for one homogeneous input.

Mechanism scope. Medial assimilation; uncertain eastern lexical comparisons.

Scholarly references. DEDR 697 p.68 directly checked; K03 *uḷ-nt reconstruction

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uḷ locative and Kannada oḷ/oḷa support the vowel-first singleton locative independently. The source-cited Old Telugu oḷana reading is now uncertain: DHARMA00099 and Sastri1969 p.285 n.1 read ēḷan ruling in the candidate inscription instead. Tamil/Malayalam uḷḷam independently establish a geminate mind formation.

Direction. Southern and Central Dravidian vowel-first locatives favor u/o–ḷ before Telugu lōna; the alleged earlier Old Telugu oḷana is not presently secure chronological evidence. The mind noun ullamu is not a same-input counterexample: its geminate is independently matched outside Telugu.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uḷ-a-n > *oḷan > *ḷōn > lōn gives Telugu lōna/lōnu and comparable Gondi lōn/rōn, with final suffix history differing by language. *uḷḷ-am > ullamu retains order. Konda olbi and Kuvi oṛp/onp thought verbs preserve initial V with internal consonant development.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. DEDR dates oḷana to the seventh century and ḷōna to the ninth–tenth; a corpus lōna record incorrectly inherits the seventh-century date. These are source dating claims. The candidate seventh-century witness at Inpuḻōli has oḷana only in an older edition: Sastri1969 p.285 n.1 and DHARMA00099 read ēḷan ruling. Unless another inscription is identified, do not use oḷana to establish retention in seventh-century Telugu. Kui lai cannot be explained by the same o outcome without another vowel/formation history. Telugu submit loŋgu/loggu series is queried; Central Dravidian lopal may be Telugu loans. Brahui house urā and heart ust have explicit alternative etymologies; exclude them from secure core counts. An existence/inside common ancestor is plausible but not settled.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 698 p.68 directly checked; K03 *uḷḷ-am and *oḷ-an records

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam uḷu and uḷuppu independently establish vowel-first lateral and high u. Telugu lūta and Kui lupenji are explicitly queried by DEDR.

Direction. The southern woodworm family has secure vowel-first order, but that cannot settle whether the two ant names are its cognates. Imported *ḷup- should not override this evidential uncertainty.

Derivation and relative chronology. If cognate, *uḷ-u > *ḷū would explain Telugu lū-, but the extra -ta is not independently matched. Kui lu-penji would also need suffix analysis and an explanation of quantity. Alternative comparison with nuḷampu d3715 admits an earlier initial nasal.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep Telugu and Kui uncertain rather than using their output to invent *-ta or claim an exceptionless high-u class. Species identification, historical ant forms, and analysis of -penji would distinguish a displaced derivative from questionable cognacy.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Malayalam uḷukka/uḷuppu, Kannada ulaku and Telugu uluku/ulku support a lateral family; Tamil uṭku has a stop before k. Medial vowel quality varies independently.

Direction. Every witness is vowel first. Tamil ṭk could arise from *ḷk cluster hardening rather than representing a proto-singleton ṭ followed by a vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *uḷ-k > Tamil uṭk, with Telugu ulk ~ uluk and Malayalam uḷukk. This distinguishes syncope/epenthesis and cluster assimilation from movement of the apical to initial position.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Which branch retained a medial vowel is unresolved. Do not manufacture a uniform *uluk input merely from Telugu or take Tamil ṭ to prove the same environment as open *uṭV animal names. Kannada low a also remains to be historically explained.

Mechanism scope. Retention with internal syncope/epenthesis and possible assimilation.

Scholarly references. DEDR 703 p.69 directly checked

Independent input evidence. Tamil, Malayalam and Kannada independently preserve geminate ḷḷ. K03 reconstructs *uḷḷi; the alternative singleton database reconstruction conflicts with those witnesses.

Direction. Widespread u before lateral supports original vowel-first order; singleton daughter reflexes can result from degemination. It is not legitimate to reclassify their ancestors as singleton solely to enlarge the eligible denominator.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uḷḷi > Telugu ulli; Central/Eastern uli and Pengo ūṛi involve degemination and apical/quantity developments. Toda u·ḷy also changes vowel quantity. Garlic compounds with white/water modifiers retain the root internally.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The plant term has Indo-Aryan comparisons (Sanskrit ūlī, Oriya uli); the contact direction is not settled here. Four corpus Manda forms are actually Kuvi F./S./Su.; source-corrected. Compound garlic forms and repetitions across sources add no independent etyma.

Mechanism scope. Retention with medial/quantity changes and unresolved plant-name diffusion.

Scholarly references. DEDR 705 p.69 directly checked; K03 *uḷḷi reconstruction

Independent input evidence. Konda uṟ with fortis uRt, Kuvi ur, Pengo uz/ust and Parji ud independently support u before an alveolar apical. Kui ubga instead has a velar/labial formation whose exact relationship to the apical root is less certain.

Direction. All clear apical cognates retain initial u. Kuvi ūrhali adds quantity, not reversed order. Kui ubga provides independently explicit g-b > b-g locally, but no initial apical metathesis.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ > uṟ/ur/uz/ud retains order with apical reflex changes. Kui ug-b > ubg is suffix-cluster exchange; root apical-to-g history is not established here.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No Telugu linked attestation. Bare and consonantal stems provide an eastern nonmetathesizing comparison; do not infer a required a formative from their infinitival citation endings. Kui ubga occurs also under happen d710; it cannot create two independent cluster-metathesis votes without disambiguating the lexeme and morphology.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟaŋku, Malayalam uṟaŋŋuka and Kannada oṟaŋgu/oṟagu independently establish vowel-first alveolar and a low-a expansion. K03 reconstructs *oṯ-a-nku at Proto-South Dravidian level.

Direction. The southern full formations and Parji org agree on V before alveolar, with internal syncope in the latter. Telugu oṟagu retains this order; modern Tamil is not the sole basis for direction.

Derivation and relative chronology. *oṯ-a-nk > oṟaŋg > oṟag gives Telugu recline, with nasal loss separately required. *oṟ-g > ogg is a possible route to Telugu oggu yield. Irula roŋgu can arise by initial-vowel loss; its exact vowel development does not uniquely select literal exchange. Gondi urh/uhr has a distinct medial consonant reversal.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a clear independently low-a retained Telugu formation, despite its broad segmental eligibility. The semantic specialization bend/recline versus sleep may matter lexically but is not a deterministic sound condition. Toda v- and Gondi var- are compatible with prothesis, not promotion of the medial alveolar. The offered/given sense of oggu requires semantic history; it is not proof of hidden initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 707 p.69 directly checked; K03 *oṯ-a-nku reconstruction

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada uṟi and Konda uRi establish a vowel-first alveolar with high i. Kannada also has uṭṭi/oṭṭi, independently matching the strengthened Telugu form.

Direction. The high-i full forms support older V–alveolar. Telugu ṭṭ is an internal strengthened reflex, not an initial segment that later acquired an epenthetic vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *uṯ-t-i or strengthened *uṯṯ-i > uṭṭi gives the Telugu sling; exact strengthening morphology is unresolved. Parji ut/utip/utka preserves a consonantal base and derivational suffixes, without initial exchange.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not use Telugu ṭṭ alone to classify the proto-root as obligatorily geminate: singleton and strengthened formations coexist independently in Kannada. Gadaba uṭṭi is explicitly compared with Telugu but not unambiguously marked borrowed; contact is uncertain. The d570 ukkam comparison is queried and cannot establish a regular velar alternation.

Mechanism scope. Retention with internal strengthening.

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟi/uṟiñcu and Malayalam uṛiñcuka independently support u before apical and a high-i formation. Pengo uj reinforces the initial-vowel order with its own apical reflex.

Direction. Several branches favor u-apical before Kuvi jū. Simple deletion of the first vowel of uṟi would yield ṟi, not jū, so vowel interaction/transfer or a different high-u formation is needed.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ-i > *ṯu-i > *ṯū > jū is a plausible displacement/contraction chain, with the apical-to-j stage potentially preceding displacement. Pengo uj retains u before j. Tulu ujumbu has added nasal/labial formation without initial exchange.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A clear eastern-only order contrast, though the exact segment-exchange mechanism and relative j development remain inferred. Telugu and Kui are absent from this linked set. Kolami ūmburseng explicitly includes ūmb from d2621 and cannot be treated as an ordinary unsuffixed uṟ reflex; Badaga ūtu kudi has distinct compound morphology. Kannada queried uṟita preserves the source’s cognacy doubt.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 709 p.70 directly checked

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟu, Malayalam uṟuka and Kannada uṟu independently establish short u followed by alveolar and high u. Kannada urt/utt alternation documents internal cluster assimilation.

Direction. Southern vowel-first agreement supports earlier u–ṯ; Telugu uṟu directly preserves this order. The unrelated shark reconstruction in the database is excluded.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ-u > Telugu uṟu/uru retains order. *uṯ-n > *unn > ūn is a possible route to ūnu/ūncu with medial assimilation and later quantity change; the exact stages need historical forms. Kannada uppu and Tulu uppuni/untuni similarly invite consonantal-formation assimilation. Kui ug-b > ubg is a separate morphologically explicit stop reversal.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not treat every u-initial derivative as evidence for one invariant suffix. Kui ubga also occurs under butt d706 with a different gloss; its root-level relationship to uṟu is less secure than the local g/b exchange. Koraga ujji has a palatal medial development, not initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Retention and internal assimilation; Kui stop-cluster metathesis is orthogonal.

Scholarly references. DEDR 710 p.70 directly checked; compare 706 p.69

Homophonous uṟu happen d710 and force d719 are potential semantic-family relationships, not automatic independent roots or automatic mergers. Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟu and historical Kannada uṟade negative independently establish vowel-first alveolar with both positive high-u and negative low-a formations.

Direction. Tamil and Kannada agreement supports earlier vowel first; Telugu Kittel examples are specifically negative and retain this order.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ-a-ka > Telugu uṟaka not minding, and *uṯ-a-person ending > uṟãḍu he does not care, as given inside the lexical record. No initial displacement is required. Exact segmentation of the personal ending remains a grammatical rather than lexical comparison.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Negative forms form an independently motivated grammatical class, but one or several retained roots do not establish a universal negative blocking rule. Compare negative-only uraka d648 and the early destroy paradigm; the exact inherited stem grades must be checked before generalizing. Brahui hunning is only a cross-reference to d727, not an attestation in this entry.

Mechanism scope. Retention in negative formations.

Scholarly references. DEDR 712 p.70 directly checked; cited BDCG §3.16 n.11 concerns alternative Brahui comparison

Direction. Full Tamil/Telugu and syncopated Konda/Kuvi all keep initial vowel before alveolar, supporting V-first root without a consonant-initial comparator.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ-ukk > Telugu uṟuk(u), Konda uRk and Kuvi urk, with medial-vowel loss and suffix-strength changes. Animal *uṯ-tt-ay yields Tamil uṟuttai and Telugu uṟuta after simplification; the exact cluster prehistory remains to be established.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The velar is later than the first singleton apical and does not exclude the root from phonological eligibility. The associated squirrel d590 may be the same family with a strengthened/retroflex root variant; show sensitivity collapse rather than counting two independent animal counterexamples.

Mechanism scope. Retention with internal syncope/cluster changes.

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟu with uṟuv/uṟṟ and Malayalam uṟuttuka support a short-u apical root and high-u formation; independently long Tamil ūṟu is a separate nominal grade.

Direction. Southern u-before-apical establishes the direction toward Kui jūga. The exact vowel before its velar suffix is not independently fixed by the bare high-u root alone.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṯ-u > *ṯū > jū, then velar/intransitive or causative formation, gives a plausible chain; the relative age of velar suffix and contraction is not proved. Kui jūk-p > jūp-k is independently established by the source’s jūkt past.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No Telugu attestation in this group. The high-u base supports long contraction but should not be counted as direct attestation of every intermediate in the Kui velar formation. Related happen/obtain uṟu d710 may share a deeper root; keep a family-sensitivity link rather than assuming either total independence or identity.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṟumu, Malayalam uṟumpuka and Central Dravidian urum support initial u before rhotic and high-u labial formation. Kannada oṟalu independently matches Telugu oṟalu lament with low a and a lateral extension.

Direction. Independent full forms favor V-first inputs in each formation. The long ṟōlu lament series is innovative under comparison with oṟalu; the uṟumu thunder series itself retains order in Telugu.

Derivation and relative chronology. *uṟ-um > Telugu uṟumu retains order, while conditional *oṟ-al > *ṟōl > ṟōlu/rōlu gives a displaced lament derivative. Kui *uṟ-um > *ṟūm > rūma/rūmba combines initial displacement/contraction with labial formation. Telugu roppu/rollu requires consonantal-suffix reconstruction or later shortening, not simply one uniform vowel input.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Expressive sound words can converge independently; do not use their semantic resemblance as decisive cognacy. Kui ṛunja is explicitly queried and has an unexplained nasal-palatal formation. Kannada ṟoppu could be an independent development or a regional loan; Brahui hūrra has an explicit Balochi comparison. Keep these separate from secure retained thunder forms and probable displaced lament forms.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 718 p.70 directly checked

Independent input evidence. Kannada uṟubu independently supplies vowel-first alveolar with high u and labial expansion. Telugu uravaḍi retains a related low-a speed formation; Konda uṟmi supports a vowel-first nasal throwing derivative.

Direction. Kannada and Konda agreement gives evidence for earlier V–alveolar beyond Telugu alone. Telugu ṟuvvu/ruvvu is consonant first under that comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *uṯ-v > *ṯuvv > ṟuvvu, or *uṯ-uv > *ṯūv with later strengthening/shortening, accounts for Telugu throw; ṟūvu supports investigating a long stage but does not uniquely establish it. Tulu rummuni/rumbu is compatible with initial-vowel loss plus medial assimilation; Konda uṟmi retains initial order.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The exact correspondence between Kannada -ub and Telugu -vv is plausible but does not prove an identical syllabification before change. Kolami ruv may be an early Telugu loan or an independent related displacement; rusi is explicitly ruv+si give and is not a second etymon. Sound-symbolic/semantic relation to abundance d711 and roar d718 deserves sensitivity treatment, not automatic merging.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 719; DED(N) 617 p.401 for Tulu

Direction. Southern forms and Kurux ordnā all put the vowel before the apical, supporting V-first ancestry. No initial displaced reflex occurs among reviewed forms.

Mechanism scope. Retention with vowel/suffix developments.

Direction. The southern low-vowel forms establish earlier u–ṯ; Telugu oṟṟa retains the initial vowel, and vaṟṟa has an additional v rather than the apical moving first.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This remains a structural-history uncertainty, not a conveniently defined geminate exception. Historical Telugu and related pungency derivatives would distinguish inherited strengthened stem from later local reinforcement. The o/a alternation is not consonant/vowel exchange.

Direction. Agreement across southern languages establishes earlier V–alveolar; Telugu oṟa/oṟṟa retains this initial order with variable medial strengthening.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A useful low-a noun control: the short-vowel singleton history is independently supported and cannot be ruled out just because one Telugu source spells ṟṟ. The two Telugu spellings are source variants, not independent roots. Borrowed Central Dravidian forms cannot count as inherited retention evidence.

Mechanism scope. Retention with medial strengthening; Central Dravidian loans.

Eligibility / caveatnorthern-medial-reduction-comparison

Independent input evidence. Kurux eṛetʰ and Malto eṛtu establish initial vowel before the rhotic, but only one full-vowel comparison supports medial e. Database *eṛt is a northern reconstruction, not a Proto-Dravidian input.

Direction. Both database languages keep initial V-r. The external Kunha iṛtū can arise from a medial-cluster formation without exchanging the initial vowel and rhotic. Kurux full form versus Malto/ Kunha clusters does not by itself decide syncope versus Kurux anaptyxis.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *eṛetʰ > *eṛt > Malto eṛtu, Kunha iṛtū, with initial raising and final vowel formation/length in Kunha. Alternatively inherited *eṛt plus Kurux medial e insertion. Either account preserves the target initial order. The archer derivative eṛtyo adds morphology without an extra metathesis event.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kujur and Dash2025 p.119 calls the Kurux/Kunha comparison metathesis, but the changed vowel quality and final quantity require additional assumptions; the segment sequence is equally compatible with syncope and final vocalism. No Telugu attestation and no southern cognate establish a shared Telugu event. Northern morphology, older Kurux forms and stress data would distinguish the alternatives.

Mechanism scope. No target initial displacement; medial syncope versus anaptyxis remains unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR789; Kujur and Dash2025 p.119

Independent input evidence. Gondi ersk preserves vowel-r order alongside rēsk. DEDR explicitly reconstructs *eṟiñc for corrected Konda ṟīnz, while Tulu edde and Malto eswe/espro supply reduced/changed coronal cognates, not the exact same full suffix.

Direction. The retained Gondi order and independent morphological comparanda favor an earlier V-apical sequence over the displayed *ǯīnǯ head as a family-wide proto-form. Konda source explicitly corrects r to ṟ, significant for the subsequent j correspondence.

Derivation and relative chronology. *e/iṟ-iñc > *ṟī/ĭnj > Konda ṟīnz, Kui jīnja and short Kuvi/Pengo/Manda jinj is a proposed displacement family. Gondi *er-sk > rēsk has a separate suffix and quantity history. Initial ṟ>j and later palatal/affricate developments are not interchangeable with inherited initial j.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Exact V1/V2 and length are not independently uniform; short versus long eastern forms cannot all be predicted by a single reconstructed *eṟiñc without additional vowel history. Tulu geminate dd might result from earlier apical/suffix assimilation, and Malto has suffix consonant variation. Telugu is genuinely unattested in this group, not retained. Source Konda correction is duplicated into long/short parser variants; do not count both as independent historical stages.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR800 p.79 directly read; DEN1 1972 pp.401,407 entries686,2127

Eligibility / caveatnonapical-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil eytu, Malayalam eytuka, Kannada aydu and historical eydu independently establish a glide root with dental extension. Pengo ika plus ipka < ik-pa identifies a separate velar-plus-labial intensive boundary.

Direction. Vowel-first order is preserved across branches; this root has no independently original medial nonnasal apical in the relevant first position. Pengo k-p direction is independently given by the simplex ika and intensive formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ey-t > eydu/ēdu or ett through glide/dental changes, not apical metathesis. Gondi ev/av, Kui epa and Konda ī have their own lenition/contraction histories. Pengo ik-pa > ipka is genuine local stop-cluster exchange after intensive suffixation; initial-vowel order remains unchanged.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This extends the local k-p process beyond Kui without pretending it establishes one family-wide innovation. The labial construction is intensive in Pengo rather than automatically the identical causative function of every Kui example. Kui epa/eppa contains no velar to exchange and is an appropriate distinct input control. Kuvi ne and Manda neyka require initial nasal/morphological history; they do not prove nasal metathesis. Brahui hining is an infinitive citation of in-, not an original h-i-n-root unanalysed whole. Tulu labels restored from source; Kuvi motion-base/personal-object tags are shifted in the parser.

Mechanism scope. Initial retention; independent Pengo stop-cluster exchange.

Scholarly references. DEDR809 p.79 directly read; MBE1962 pp.63–64 cited there

Eligibility / caveatcompound-process-separate

Independent input evidence. Kannada eral/eraḷ/elar/elal and Telugu compound temm-eral independently establish an initial vowel before the first liquid; exact liquid order is variable within Kannada.

Direction. Telugu temm-eral and the cited Tamil nir̤ali comparison favor r before l, but restricted distribution and alternative elar prevent a certain ancestral order between the two liquids.

Derivation and relative chronology. *er-al > Kannada eral and Telugu temm-eral retains initial order; Kannada elar can be an internal r/l exchange, elal assimilation, and Telugu temm-era final-l loss. payy-ara has its own compound vowel history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is not initial metathesis. Treat Kannada internal exchange as a separate medium-confidence process. Source temm-eral is attested in Kumārasambhava and an inscription reference via Sastri p.99, but no date is assigned until those references are localized. Badaga Eranda dog name has uncertain relationship and contributes no secure wind evidence.

Mechanism scope. Initial order retained; internal liquid exchange possible.

Scholarly references. DEDR810; DEN1 1972 p.416 S96

d811 — burn, blaze, smart, pungency

d811: burn, blaze, smart, pungency

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd811
Comparative input*er-i; related high/low and long derivatives
Initial consonantzero
V1 quality / quantitye / short
C2 identity / structurer / singleton
Following voweli/a/u
Root/formation shapeVC-i / VC-V-C / VVC
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceHigh-i burn versus long causative and other-vowel derivatives; no automatic reverse inference from Kui ī.
Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh for e-r core; low for Kui earlier vowel
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil eri, Malayalam eriyuka, Telugu eriyu and Konda er independently establish e-r with a high-i burn formation. Long causatives/nouns and wildfire compounds have different morphology.

Direction. The broad full-form comparison favors initial e before r. Kui rīva has reversed order but i rather than e, so it cannot simply be treated as the expected result of transferring the first vowel e.

Derivation and relative chronology. Telugu eriyu retains order; high-vowel loss and compensatory quantity can give ērcu/ērpu without metathesis. Kui rīva could reflect an older *ir-i grade plus contraction, or aphaeresis of *eri with separate lengthening/formative change. Kui ēṛ/ērpa causative retains initial e and needs a distinct formation history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A strong Telugu short-vowel/high-i retained control. Kui exact mechanism and input vowel remain uncertain despite the r-initial form; no invented *iri should count as independently verified conditioning. The relation to n-initial fire d2929 is a possible prothesis/loss connection, not a license to merge all fire formations. Toda row/sitting and Kota scooping senses reflect polysemy/homonym alignment issues; only the cited brightness meanings support this comparison. Badaga scattering senses need separate semantic review.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 811; DEN1 1972 p.401 entry694; comparison DEDR 2929

PropertyAnnotation

Initial consonantØ

Input classshort-vowel-initial-singleton-apical

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil eru/eruku, Malayalam eru/erukuka and central/northern erŋg/erx independently place e before r. High u is supported in the southern velar formation; nasal extensions are distinct.

Direction. Southern, central and northern agreement favors vowel-first order independently of Telugu eruvu/ērugu.

Derivation and relative chronology. *er-uK > Telugu ērugu involves unexplained or morphological lengthening but preserves V-r order. *er-uV > eruvu is retained. Kannada ekku allows medial r/velar assimilation; Gondi ērg adds quantity and syncope, not initial reversal.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The long Telugu velar stem must not be used to reconstruct a universally long proto-root: Tamil eruku is short. Different noun/verb derivatives and existing Kannada ēru suggest a quantitative grade, but its conditioning is not established. Medial r loss in Kannada is opaque for detailed chronology, not automatically hidden initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam erutu, Tulu eru and Kannada eṛ̆tu establish older vowel-r order with a stop extension independently of Telugu eddu. Whether all branches inherited a vowel or a cluster at the relevant date is not fixed.

Direction. Shared fuller er-u-t and r-t show r before the dental rather than a primitive initial r. Medial assimilation readily yields eddu/ettu in several languages.

Derivation and relative chronology. *erut > *ert > ett/edd gives Kannada eddu/ettu, Telugu eddu and central eḍ. Telugu compound gaŋgi-reddu could contain inserted/linking r after an already assimilated eddu, or a separately displaced/shortened formation; neither chronology is established by the compound alone.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not count gaŋgi-reddu as certain inherited metathesis. Original DEDR writes -reddu, explicitly bound, beside gaṅg-eddu; parser removes the initial hyphen and creates an apparent free word. Short e and geminate dd require explanations under any *erut>rēt route. Toda eṭ in song is explicitly a Badaga loan; inherited ešt/eśt remains separate. Telugu eddu is an opaque apical-loss development, not a clean retained-r example.

Mechanism scope. Medial assimilation; compound r origin unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR815; original SQL rows9924–9927; PSS83 pp.393–394 medial-r loss

Independent input evidence. Tamil erumai, Malayalam eruma and Badaga erume independently support e-r-u-m; Tulu and historical Kannada erme and Gondi ermi preserve the rhotic before a nasal after syncope.

Direction. Broad full and syncopated comparisons favor earlier r before m. Telugu enumu can result from r nasalization before m, independently compared with inumu iron by PSS83 p.394.

Derivation and relative chronology. *erum > Telugu enumu involves r>n before a nasal, not movement of r. Kannada/Kodagu emme follows medial syncope and assimilation of rm; Kota im loses r, Toda ɨr loses final nasal material. Each reduces a different part of the full form.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a candidate interaction that could remove the target before initial metathesis, but the relative date of nasal assimilation and metathesis is not independently established. No surviving mr/nr onset licenses a concealed-displacement claim. Badaga has both erume and emme; retain those as variation, not a dated sequence. Historical Kannada erme supplies relative support for later assimilation in that language.

Mechanism scope. Nasalization/assimilation and segment loss, no proven initial metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR816; PSS83 p.394 *r>n before nasal

Independent input evidence. Tamil eruvai blood, Kannada ere colour, Parji iric netta and Gondi erom/erm dog compounds independently establish vowel-first order. Exact -Vc and -Vm formations are distinct.

Direction. The matching Parji iric dog formation strengthens the comparison with Telugu rēcu beyond using colour semantics alone. Gondi rasi/rac dog stems reverse initial order relative to full erm/erom variants but differ in suffix.

Derivation and relative chronology. *er-Vc > *rēc > Telugu rēcu is plausible displacement with contraction; Parji iric supplies a full high-i formation but does not uniquely justify e versus i in the shared input. Gondi rac/rasi and Gadaba rēs may share or borrow the displaced dog adjective. Kolami resn a·te reflects compound boundary res#na·te, not root-final n.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Agricultural/hunting vocabulary may diffuse between Telugu, Gondi and central languages; identical compound meaning is compatible with inherited formation or calquing/borrowing. Do not label every central r form an independent innovation. Gondi ce is an editorial cross-reference to red1931, not a dog root. Badaga red-fruit comparison supports colour association only, not the precise dog suffix.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR817; DEN1 1972 p.402 entry700

Independent input evidence. Kannada ere black soil supplies an independent vowel-r comparison for Telugu compound rē-gaḍa/rē-gaḍi. Only these two languages establish the narrow set, so deeper reconstruction is tentative.

Direction. Full Kannada ere and the transparent Telugu clod second member favor vowel-r before Telugu rē, but loan adaptation or a separate long regional noun remains possible.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *ere#kaḍḍa > *rē#gaḍa yields the Telugu compound through displacement/contraction plus independent compound consonant changes. An original V2 e cannot be equated with inherited a or i without additional comparison.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Count as medium-confidence regional displacement, outside strict V2 prediction tests. The DEDR entry was split from oldDED700, shared with the red/dog material now817; a common colour/soil root is plausible but not proven and should be a sensitivity merge. Root-gaḍa is not the source of the moved r.

Direction. Agreement across southern and Gondi branches favors V-r order; Telugu eṟṟa is a strengthened variant rather than evidence that every input was geminate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A low-a nominal retention counterexample to unrestricted application; do not exclude it simply because it lacks a metathesized variant. Independent input evidence. Kota irg places r before a velar, while Kannada ege/eŋkli, Tulu eggɛ/eggelɯ and Koraga eŋkili motivate other cluster formations. There is no independently agreed full *ir-Vv input for Telugu rivva.

Direction. Kota can support a vowel-initial rhotic input, but lateral/nasal/velar comparisons do not uniquely establish the same root or exact derivative as Telugu rivva/rivaṭa.

Derivation and relative chronology. If related, *ir-Vk/w > *ri-kk/vv could involve displacement and velar-labial development, but each step needs independent evidence. Alternatively the Telugu twig noun is a separate root; DEDR explicitly prefixes its comparison with a question mark.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The parser suppresses the source question mark before Telugu, creating spurious certainty. Keep Telugu A, not a short-vowel metathesis counterexample or positive. Needed: early Telugu spelling, velar/labial correspondence and fuller cognates; Kota irg alone cannot justify the whole proposed chain.

Mechanism scope. Unresolved cognacy and cluster history.

Independent input evidence. Kota ed, Toda eθy, Kannada ede/edde/erde, Tulu ede and Telugu eda establish initial e followed by a coronal. Kannada r-containing variant alone cannot establish an original r for the entire set.

Direction. Vowel-before-coronal order is stable; Telugu eda/eḍæda and Konda eduṟam do not move an apical to the initial position.

Derivation and relative chronology. *edV > eda/ede and strengthened edda/eḍḍa retain order. Konda eduṟam and Parji edram/edrom may contain an r-formation; Kannada erde could preserve a cluster or add r, with no unique direction yet.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Coronal identity and singleton/cluster reconstruction remain uncertain; this is a retained-order comparison but not a decisive test of a specifically *ṭ or *r law. Telugu eḍæda shows additional syllabic material; do not count its repeated coronal as a second root. No plausible initial metathesis in this set.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam eli and Kannada/Tulu eli/ili establish a high-i root; Telugu elika/eluka and Konda/Kolami elka share a velar extension, with high vowel versus syncope.

Direction. Broad southern and central vowel-first evidence establishes e/i before l independently of Telugu. Brahui hal keeps the vowel before l after initial h addition and vowel change.

Derivation and relative chronology. *eli > eli/ili retains order. *el-i-k > elika/eluka or elka via medial syncope retains V-l; Gondi elli/allī and Naiki elli add strength/quantity history. Toda is̱y and Kota eyj reflect local lateral changes. Gadaba sirel is small+rat, not a root-initial s-l displacement.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A high-vowel noun control with extensive independent comparison. Geminate Gondi/Naiki cannot be projected onto all branches when singleton southern evidence is broad. No Kui/Kuvi attestation occurs in this group, so absence of a eastern metathesized rat form is missing data, not retention. Brahui hal requires prothesis/vowel history but no initial liquid transfer.

Independent input evidence. Telugu elũgu/elĩgincu and independently Parji iluŋg establish vowel-l-high-vowel-nasal-velar order. Parji was incorrectly labeled Telugu in the corpus and is restored from DEDR p.81.

Direction. Independent central Parji full form prevents reasoning solely from Telugu. Gondi lēng/lēŋgi and Konda līŋ reverse initial order relative to the shared full formation; differing ē/ī needs its own vocalism analysis.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *el-iŋ > *lēŋ or *il-iŋ > *līŋ gives eastern displacement/contraction; source variable i/e/u prevents a single secure V2-quality prediction. Gadaba lēng may be borrowed from a displaced Gondi-like form.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The high-vowel suffix is independently attested but exactly matching first-vowel grade is not. Do not use long ē to invent low a. Koraga elkiri weep is explicitly queried and absent from parsed lexical evidence; no independent voice vote is assigned to it. Gondi dialect duplicates remain one family observation.

Independent input evidence. Parji elub, Gadaba elub/elb and Gondi elum/allum independently establish vowel-l-u-labial order, while eastern līm/līmbu is reduced. The displayed *līm head does not establish the earlier family-wide input.

Direction. Several central and Gondi full forms support vowel-first order before the lateral; eastern initial l/ḍ is secondary under the parsimonious comparison. Geminate Gondi/Gadaba variants cannot be imposed on singleton elub/elum.

Derivation and relative chronology. *el-u-m/b > līm/līmbu is a displacement-family development, but the exact change e-u > ī is unresolved. Kuvi lēmpu beside līmpu/līmbu and short limbu reveals real vowel/quantity variation. Kui initial ḍ follows the lateral-to-stop correspondence; it does not imply original *ṭ.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This challenges a mechanical output rule based on the directly attested full e-u sequence. An earlier *il-im could explain ī but is not independently attested here and is not adopted to save the rule. Alternative vowel assimilation, extension reshaping or borrowing among eastern languages needs source/dialect evidence. Compound ant terms piṛku/dār/pete are not additional roots. Telugu is missing, not retained.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil elumpu, Malayalam elumpu/eluŋku, Kodagu elɨmbɨ and Kannada elubu/elugu independently establish e-l with high-u nasal/labial or velar extensions.

Direction. The lateral precedes the nasal/labial in fuller forms; Tamil eṉpu and Telugu emmu show medial assimilation rather than evidence for an original initial m.

Derivation and relative chronology. *elump > *elmp > emmu and extended emuka/emmuka plausibly involve medial syncope/assimilation plus velar nominal material. Kannada emike/emake provides an independent parallel. Telugu makkelu bones may involve resegmentation/analogy, aphaeresis or internal rearrangement of an extended plural; its exact input is not fixed.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not label makkelu a secure initial-l metathesis: its initial m is not the reconstructed l and an l persists later. Recovering *emukalu or *elmukalu and dated intermediate forms would distinguish aphaeresis plus analogy from consonant transposition. Toda complex spellings preserve local lateral fricative/allophonic notation, not differing metathesis events. Sanskrit/BHS monument terms are contact comparisons, not roots for this denominator.

Mechanism scope. Medial assimilation and possible plural restructuring; initial displacement not established.

Eligibility / caveatgeminate-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil ellām, Malayalam ellām, Kannada ella, Kodagu ella· and Telugu ella independently support geminate l. Kota/Toda final el cannot independently diagnose historical singleton intervocalic l.

Direction. Initial vowel before the lateral is shared throughout; the Tulu additive enclitic -la has a different morphological position and needs separate grammaticalization history.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ell-am > ellām/ella involves final quantity and nasal history, not initial metathesis. Conditional *ella > -la would require clitic reduction/aphaeresis, possibly degemination, rather than evidence for the ordinary initial root rule.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Tulu source writes -la (? -lā) and compares its function with *-um; the parser drops the hyphen and turns the editorial reconstruction *-um into a lexical record. The clitic cannot be counted as a secure metathesized lexical all root. Personal suffixes and compounds remain nested observations.

Mechanism scope. Geminate retention; Tulu clitic reduction unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR844 p.82 directly read; MBE1974a pp.107–108 cited there, not directly read

Independent input evidence. Tulu elle and Telugu elli independently agree on short e and geminate l; Markodi elle/yelle supports the same regional shape.

Direction. All witnesses place the vowel before the geminate. Initial y in Markodi is prothesis or a separate local onset, not a moved root liquid.

Derivation and relative chronology. *elli/e > elli/elle retains order. Telugu elluṇḍi and Tulu ellañji are different day-after-tomorrow formations whose endings require separate reconstruction.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a regional control, not proof of a Proto-Dravidian time adverb. K03 p.407 includes Brahui elli in a broader distribution statement, but the database group and DEDR entry lack a Brahui attestation; that published claim remains source-only and unverified here. Potential relation to light/day829, all844 or limit846 should be tested as family sensitivity, not assumed from ell alone.

Mechanism scope. Geminate retention.

Scholarly references. DEDR845 p.82 directly read; K03 adverbial discussion

Independent input evidence. Tamil ellai, Malayalam ella, Kannada elle and Telugu ella independently establish a geminate low-vowel formation. Malayalam eluka instead has a singleton lateral and different velar expansion.

Direction. The initial vowel precedes lateral in all forms; single final Toda l does not prove a singleton intervocalic ancestor.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ell-ay > ellai/elle/ella retains order; Toda ely follows its own final sequence reduction. Malayalam eluka may be a separately expanded grade, not metathesis or evidence against the geminate reconstruction of the main formation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Classify the common ell-ay formation as geminate and the Malayalam singleton separately. Boundary place names repeat the same root. A possible connection with all844 or day845 is a deeper lexical hypothesis; shared spelling alone is insufficient.

Mechanism scope. Original initial order retained.

Scholarly references. DEDR846 p.82 directly read

d851 — rise, lift; awake, caution

d851: rise, lift; awake, caution

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd851
Comparative input*eẓ-u; *eẓ-c/ar, nasal/velar/labial extensions
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantitye / short/long by formation
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu/a/unknown
Root/formation shapeVC-u / VC-C / VC-ar
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceCaution -car, rise/lift and ladder derivatives separately reconstructed.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh root order; low exact eastern V2
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil eṛ̆u, Malayalam eṛ̆uka, Kannada eṛ̆ and Kota eṛv establish vowel-approximant order. Kannada eṛ̆caṟ independently supports the medial approximant before the caution suffix, even though many caution forms assimilate it.

Direction. Southern full forms precede eastern initial ḍ in lifting/standing variants. The caution r after cc belongs to an extension, not a moved first apical. The database *enǯ alternative and imported *eẓ-c head refer to particular formations and must not replace the whole complex root.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *eẓ-Vk/ñj > *ẓēk/ñj > Kui ḍēk/ḍēnja and Manda/Kuvi ḍēk gives initial displacement and apical stopping, but exact V2 and length are not independently fixed. Gondi ḍiŋ has a different vowel. *eẓ-car > eccar through medial assimilation yields Telugu eccarika etc.; no earlier initial displacement is required. Tulu eḷañci > leñci/eñci permits aphaeresis and medial loss in a ladder noun.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Separate lifting, waking/caution and ladder formations. Telugu is represented only by caution derivatives in this entry; ordinary lēcu is assigned to d916 in DEDR and cannot be silently imported here. Brahui harfing/hēfing involves a morphologically complex infinitive and medial consonant loss/grade, not initial r transfer. Long southern ēẓ variants are independently attested and prevent a single uniform short quantity for all formations. Tulu short leñci may be aphaeresis, not the eastern long-vowel process.

Mechanism scope. Eastern displacement; southern medial assimilation and local ladder aphaeresis alternatives.

Scholarly references. DEDR851 p.82 directly read; compare separately DEDR916

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil eḷi/eḷimai and Malayalam eḷi/eḷima establish high-i singleton formation, alongside independently low-a iḷamai/iḷama and strong eḷḷu.

Direction. Southern forms and historical Kannada iḷi agree on vowel-first order. Telugu ellidamu retains the vowel and a strengthened lateral; the strengthening is a local or borrowed formation, not evidence of universal original gemination.

Derivation and relative chronology. *eḷ-i > eḷi/iḷi retains order; *eḷḷ > Tamil eḷḷu and Telugu ellidamu-like strength has a separate history. Tamil eṇmai follows l/n assimilation in a nominal suffix environment.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu is a retained-order observation but exact input strength and inheritance of ellidamu are uncertain. Do not classify all weak/light words as geminate merely from Telugu. Possible relation to young513 and poor911 or contempt776 is semantic/derivational and must be tested, not used to manufacture one regular class.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Input confidencehigh for order; medium for full root

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil iḷai/uḷiyam/elu, Malayalam uḷiyam, Parji ili and Gondi eṛj establish vowel-first lateral/apical forms with several extensions. Konda olzu/oṛzu independently supports apical before z.

Direction. The distribution supports an earlier vowel preceding the apical; the displayed alternative *joḷǯ- is a separate reconstruction and cannot override the comparative onset evidence without an initial-y account.

Derivation and relative chronology. *eḷ-Vñc > Gondi eṛj and Konda olzu/oṛzu involves syncope and palatal/nasal changes while retaining vowel-first order. Kui oli/oḍi and Kuvi oṛi reflect apical merger/stop development. Tamil eṇku and Malto eju have medial cluster reductions. Telugu elūgu is unusual in its long second vowel and needs separate suffix history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No positive initial displacement is attested despite several eastern languages. Exact ancestral vowel/formative varies and is not inferred from modern outcomes. Konda north/west rhotic versus south/east lateral is useful dialect correspondence, not necessarily metathesis variation. Animal-name diffusion remains possible but does not explain away the retained forms.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR857; K03 reconstruction *eḷ-V-ñc

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd859
Comparative input*e/iṟ-i/u; long *ēṟ; labial extensions
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantitye/i / short/long by formation
C2 identity / structureṟ / singleton
Following voweli/u/a
Root/formation shapeVC-i / VC-C / VVC
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceShort labial verb and independent long noun differentiated; no suffix recovered solely from output.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh root order; low exact Telugu mm suffix
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil eṟi/iṟu, Malayalam eṟiyuka, Kannada iṟi and Konda iṟ independently establish vowel-first alveolar order. Long ēṟu/ēṭu blow is independently attested and not shortened to fit the short branch.

Direction. Broad southern and Konda/Kuvi vowel-first reflexes precede Telugu ṟimmu and Gondi rē/rēh under a displacement account. Exact labial formative of ṟimmu is less certain than root order.

Derivation and relative chronology. *iṟ-(V)mm > *ṟimm gives Telugu ṟimmu if that strong labial derivative is established; a high-vowel root is independent, but mm must not be invented from the outcome. Gondi rē/rēh likely displaces a vowel-first stem while other dialects retain ērīstānā/ertānā. Kannada ṟeppu is an initial-loss/displaced-looking labial form with unexplained e. Kui ig-b > ibg is separately supported local cluster exchange.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Quantity and suffix predictions remain conditional: independent iṟi does not establish the exact mm derivative. Kannada initial ṟeppu may be local development or contact, not a family-wide exceptionless process. Kui ig root versus ṟ needs an allomorphic/correspondence explanation, while Kuvi ir remains unchanged. Toda mediative-causative eṯ is morphologically distinct from the throwing root and not an independent ordinary verb vote.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR859

d860 — pull, drag, pluck

d860: pull, drag, pluck

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd860
Comparative inputregional *ṟel / *er-i / *ar-i; deeper order uncertain
Initial consonantØ/r
V1 quality / quantitye/a / short
C2 identity / structurer/ṟ/l / singleton
Following voweli/unknown
Root/formation shapeVC-i versus CVC
Grammatical categoryverb
Boundary evidenceFinal-l and labial derivatives require independent reconstruction.
Input classuncertain-initial-order
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencelow for common full input
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlookalike-unresolved

Independent input evidence. Gondi ari/eri full forms coexist with Konda ṟel, Kui jel and Pengo jel. Telugu remmu has a labial formation, not the same medial/final consonants as all the eastern stems.

Direction. Gondi may preserve an earlier vowel-first root, but the broad regional ṟel/jel series and its final l cannot be derived by a bare reversal of ari. The displayed *Rel is a regional reconstruction, not independently settled deeper order.

Derivation and relative chronology. A conditional *eṟ-Vl > *ṟel could account for the Konda/Kui/Pengo series, with later ṟ>j, but no full identical -Vl formation is attested here. Telugu *eṟ-(V)mm > remmu requires a different derivative. Alternatively the Gondi ari material and eastern ṟel stems are distinct or only distantly related.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep the entire displacement claim uncertain rather than inventing *erel/*erimm to explain each result. Needed: older Gondi/Konda paradigms, independent final-l derivative, and regular correspondences linking Telugu mm to the same root. The several Gondi bringing/taking compounds do not add independent lexical votes.

Mechanism scope. Competing cognacy and displacement hypotheses.

Scholarly references. DEDR860; DEN1 1972 p.415 entry4243

d865: red

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd865
Comparative input*eṯ-V; *eṯ-a/*eṯ-up

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Konda eṟa/eṟani and Tamil eṟuṛ̆am red-flowered tree independently support short initial e before an alveolar; Telugu eṟupa and historical Eṟama have singleton evidence beside modern eṟṟa.

Direction. The independent Konda form and singleton variants favor a vowel-first root, not a primitive initial r. Gemination in Telugu is not uniformly ancestral.

Derivation and relative chronology. *eṯ-a > eṟa and strengthened eṟṟa retain initial order; *eṯ-up > eṟupa has a different noun expansion. Gondi erra is explicitly borrowed from Telugu and must not become an independent inherited retention.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The source dates Eṟama as an eighth-century name and Eṟṟana as the fourteenth-century author; these are lexicographic date claims pending inscription verification. Tamil botanical semantic link is less direct than Konda colour, and Kolami eroṛi/erroḍī may be regional loans. Possible relationship to red/dog817 and clay820 requires a cognacy argument, not automatic merging of colour roots.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR865; K03 regional *eṯ-V
