d868 — say, quotative; literary contracted grammatical forms

d868: say, quotative; literary contracted grammatical forms

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd868
Comparative inputregional *an/en/in; proposed deeper *aHn; grammatical *an-an, *an-ā-baḍu etc.
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantitya/e/i / short regional roots; long northern grade and grammatical contractions
C2 identity / structuren / nasal with tense-conditioned cluster variants
Following vowela/ā/u/zero
Root/formation shapeVC+infinitive/passive/negative morphology
Grammatical categoryverb/quotative
Boundary evidenceFull and reduced infinitive, passive, post-action and negative paradigms explicitly paired in source.
Input classnasal-quotative-morphology
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for local an+suffix order; medium for phonetic mechanism
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatnasal-grammatical-displacement

Independent input evidence. Tamil eṉ, Kannada an/ennu, Tulu anpini/inpini and Telugu anu independently establish vowel before n; Old Telugu envānṟu preserves an e variant. K03 proposed *aHn explains wider vowel alternation but is not needed to establish local segment order.

Direction. Sastri1969 p.72 explicitly aligns full anu derivatives with literary n-initial variants, independently of the modern base alone. Kota in:n also shows initial-vowel absence but need not share the Telugu mechanism.

Derivation and relative chronology. Telugu *an-an > nān and *an-ā-baḍu > nābaḍu can involve displacement/contraction; negative *an-aka > nāka requires merger/loss of one a. The source also gives anaru:naru with short a, so one unqualified long-output rule does not cover the whole paradigm. Analogical stem extension and phonological reduction compete; passage-by-passage morphology is needed.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. These are literary grammatical formations, not evidence that ordinary nasal roots joined the classical nonnasal apical rule. Nasal augmentation in negayu<egayu and nuṇḍi<uṇḍi is a different process. Tamil/central tense alternants n:nt/t/c/s reflect inherited morphology and assimilation, not initial movement. Kota n could be simple aphaeresis. Kurux long ā and the deep laryngeal reconstruction remain separate vowel-history questions. No exact date of the individual literary forms is established by Sastri’s period label.

Mechanism scope. Literary grammatical nasal displacement/contraction or analogical allomorphy; distinct from the classical nonnasal apical domain.

Scholarly references. DEDR868; Sastri1969 p.72 visually checked; K03 comparative reconstruction records

d869: sunshine, dry in sun

PropertyAnnotation

Following vowelu/a

Input classnasal-or-nasal-cluster-input

Eligibility / caveatroot-cluster-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil eṉṟu and Telugu eṇḍa/eṇḍu independently establish a nasal-apical cluster. Gondi eddi/addī and Naiki edde can reflect medial assimilation of that cluster.

Direction. Nasal and apical follow the initial vowel in the independent southern witnesses. Parji nendi/nenḍi adds an initial nasal whose origin cannot simply be called initial apical displacement.

Derivation and relative chronology. *enṯ > eṉṟ/eṇḍ retains cluster order; *enṯ > edd is assimilation and possible denasalization. Parji nendi could reflect nasal prothesis, analogy with day words or a different extension; the medial nasal remains, so simple swapping of the sole n is inadequate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A root-cluster control, not an exception invented from its retained result. Toda eṟ in a song is explicitly labeled probably spurious by the newer dictionary, so it contributes no secure singleton evidence. Connection to el shine829 or eṟi861 is a lexical hypothesis; no automatic collapse until the lateral/nasal/stop derivation is supported.

Mechanism scope. Cluster retention/assimilation; Parji prothesis/analogy unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR869; Toda2025 p.15 entry20 explicitly doubtful

d910 — seven, seventy

d910: seven, seventy

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd910
Comparative inputshort *eẓ-u-pat- tens versus long *ēẓ-u numeral
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantitye / mixed by formation
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu/zero
Root/formation shapeVC-u + ten / VVC-u
Grammatical categorynumeral
Boundary evidenceShort attributive/tens grade and long independent numeral are independently attested in several languages.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam eẓu-patu seventy and short attributive eẓu- independently establish the short root beside ēẓu seven. Tulu eḷpa and Kodagu əḷu-vadɨ independently retain a short tens formation.

Direction. Southern short attributive/tens forms support e before ẓ. Telugu ḍebbadi promotes the apical, whereas ēḍu preserves the independent long root in numeral and person formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. *eẓ-(u)-pat > *ẓe-ppat > ḍebbadi is schematic: vowel loss, displacement, labial strengthening/voicing and the Telugu tens suffix require separate chronology. Later ḍebbʰai/ḍabbʰai adds suffix contraction, aspiration and e/a variation. Long *ēẓ-u > ēḍu retains order; no ad hoc shortening of modern ēḍu is required to feed seventy.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The compound boundary supplies independent conditioning information, but exact prehistoric weakening of u and voicing of p cannot be inferred merely from a compound label. The original ḍ in seventy remains distinct from later d elsewhere; orthography/source traditions need checking before claiming one universal merger date. K03 p.264 diagnoses Kolami seven forms as Telugu loans. Kui oḍgi is itself queried and has separate vowel/suffix history, not initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 p.264 §6.5.7; PSS83 p.235; DEDR 910

d915 — separate, winnow, sift

d915: separate, winnow, sift

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd915
Comparative input*ēṟ- / shorter extended *eṟ-l-; possible *cēṟ connection
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantityē/e / long and independently short extended forms
C2 identity / structureṟ / singleton
Following vowelzero/i/unknown
Root/formation shapeVVC-C / VC-l-is
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceplausible formative boundary; not independently dated
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for mixed quantity; low for immediate displaced input
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlong-short-formation-challenge

Independent input evidence. Telugu ēṟu and widespread Gondi ēri/ēr, Konda ēṟ and Kui/Kuvi ē- establish long vowel-first formations. Konda eṟlis and Kuvi erl independently supply shorter extended formations, but not the complete prehistory of ṟēs/jēc.

Direction. Widespread vowel-first order versus Konda ṟēs and Pengo jēc supports displacement-family comparison. It does not establish long ē as the immediate input of those precise derivatives, given the independently present short eṟl formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. Retained *ēṟ-s/p gives Gondi ērst-, Kuvi ērs/ērsp/ēhp and Konda ēṟp. Konda ṟēs and Pengo jēc could reflect long-input displacement or a lost short extended *eṟ-V-s/c; the latter is not directly attested. Kui ēspa/ēja and Kuvi ēhp show consonant developments without initial displacement. Konda nēspa requires additional prothesis or morphological history, not movement of an inherited initial n from this root.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A genuine quantity challenge remains: do not classify ṟēs/jēc as verified short-input outcomes because their outputs are long. Conversely, the full set is not proof that all long roots were eligible. Malayalam ekaṟuka has extra k and cannot simply be treated as the identical unextended stem. DEDR queries relation to cēṟ/cēṭṭai2019; initial c loss, cognacy and formation must be argued separately. Konda nēspa is preserved as an unresolved variant; it could show secondary n as in other Telugu-region verbs, but no source diagnosis is asserted.

Mechanism scope. Displacement-family comparison; direct long exchange versus unattested short derivative unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR915 p.88; DEDR source cross-reference2019

d916 — rise, ascend, rouse; dawn; water-lift

d916: rise, ascend, rouse; dawn; water-lift

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd916
Comparative input*ēṟ / *ēl; displaced regional rē/lē derivatives; alternative *sal?
Initial consonantØ
V1 quality / quantityē / long independently attested; immediate displaced input unresolved
C2 identity / structureṟ/l / singleton
Following vowelu/zero/unknown
Root/formation shapeVVC / VVC-V; disputed earlier short derivatives
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceDifferent rise, dawn, imperative and water-lift formations; no unverified short grade treated as established.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for comparative long root; low for immediate displaced derivative
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlong-input-challenge

Independent input evidence. Tamil ēṟu/ēl, Malayalam ēṟuka/ēlkka, Kannada ēṟu, Kota ēṯ/ēr and Toda long-apical forms independently establish long root quantity and vowel-before-apical order. No independently full short *er-V derivative matching Telugu rēgu/lēcu is supplied by the present set.

Direction. Widespread southern long V-apical order contrasts with Telugu rē-/lē- in the same broad rise/rouse meanings. This supports displacement-family comparison, but does not by itself prove that a long vowel was the immediate input: an independently documented earlier short grade or different root would change that conclusion.

Derivation and relative chronology. A direct *ēṟ > rē or *ēl > lē reverses a long vowel and apical, outside the short-input rule. Alternatively an earlier short extended *er/el-V could yield the long displaced forms, but that intermediate is currently unsupported. Telugu reccu needs its own shortening/strong derivative history. Water-lift ētamu preserves V-apical order after strong dental development. Konda ēṟasi versus defective le/leˀ e/ledu shows formation/morphological contrast, not a simple dated sound-change sequence.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep this as a genuine challenge in the long-input class, with immediate prehistory uncertain, rather than silently moving it to short input. The alternative *sal? reconstruction is connected to Brahui saling and requires a separate initial-s and vowel history; Brahui alone does not demonstrate a common *sal that explains every southern form. The unrelated *ñāl dog head is a database linkage error. Kannada rēgu and Tulu rēgiyuni could be shared regional developments or Telugu loans; no donor proof is available here. Central les/lēp also requires contact evaluation. Gondi cooking forms and Kuvi re'nai are explicitly questioned in DEDR; the Kuvi source disagrees ascend versus descend. Relation to short *eẓ rise851 could involve conflation or analogy but is not assumed; ẓ versus ṟ/l needs independent justification.

Mechanism scope. Displacement-family comparison supported; direct long-vowel metathesis versus lost short grade or etymological conflation unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR916 p.88 directly read; contrast DEDR851 p.82

Eligibility / caveatlong-input-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil ēṟu/ēṟṟai, Malayalam ēṟu/ēṟan and Kota/Toda ēṟ establish long ē before apical. Strong Tamil ṟṟ/ṭṭ supports an alveolar/dental-stop reconstruction rather than treating every r as primary rhotic.

Direction. Several independent southern branches have the same vowel-first order; Brahui arē also retains a vowel before r but has its own vocalism.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ēṯ-u > Tamil ēṟu, Malayalam ēṟu and southern ēṟ; reinforced ēṟṟai/ēṭṭai. Brahui arē/arisk could involve suffixation and vowel redistribution but does not show root-apical promotion to word onset.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kota tirēr/tir e·r is a compound, not a doubled metathesis result. Brahui arē comparison requires explicit vowel and plural analysis; do not count final ē as proof of a swap because r remains preceded by a. Badaga ēgaru has extra g and an alternative calf cross-reference, so its cognacy is less secure than ēru. DEDR questions connection with sēṟi2820; initial-s history remains outside this control.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR917 p.88; Krishnamurti reconstruction in database

Eligibility / caveatnonapical-kp-domain

Independent input evidence. Konda and Pengo ok-, Parji okp:okt and Kui past okt establish velar before labial in the transitive stem independently of the Kui present opka.

Direction. The base ok and retained Parji okp directly support k-p as earlier than Kui p-k. This is not an apical input.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ok-p-a > opka in Kui, while past *ok-t yields okt. Parji preserves okp:okt; Konda okis is a different causative formative. Pengo bare ok supplies a root control, not the same -p formation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The red *kem head is a database linkage error and is excluded. Gadaba oskap has additional s and cannot independently establish a simple identical stem. Gondi akanā may reflect vowel lowering or different formation/cognacy. The source compares Tamil oy984, but the relationship k:y needs separate reconstruction. This supplies one additional Kui k-p formation, not a Telugu metathesis case.

Mechanism scope. Consonant-cluster k-p > p-k, separate from initial apical displacement.

Scholarly references. DEDR931 p.90 directly read

Direction. The two regional witnesses both have o-ḍ-a; Telugu is not the sole order witness.

Independent input evidence. Tamil uṭaṉ and uṭam-paṭu, Malayalam uṭan/uṭam-peṭuka and Kannada oḍan/oḍam-baḍu independently establish a full comitative base and compound boundary.

Direction. The matching full compound in several southern languages supports initial-vowel loss in Tulu dambaḍ-; Telugu also preserves the full compound, but is not the sole order witness.

Derivation and relative chronology. *oḍam#baḍ- > Tulu oḍam-baḍipuni beside dambaḍipuni by aphaeresis plus retroflex simplification; medial a remains and no output long vowel is required. Telugu oḍam/oḍã-baḍu has nasalization/loss at the boundary without initial apical movement. Grammatical -oṭu/-ōṭu and Toda -vɨṛ require their own clitic/prosodic history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Tulu initial d is therefore not automatic evidence for the Telugu contraction process. Loss of initial o alone plus ḍ>d accounts for the observed segment sequence; a literal exchange would additionally need vowel fusion/loss and offers no independent advantage here. Badaga ōṭalu hotel with a following postposition gloss is a parser conflation, not a cognate comitative word. Morphological compounds and suffix allomorphs are not independent roots.

Mechanism scope. Tulu aphaeresis and stop simplification; no unique evidence for literal vowel-apical exchange.

Scholarly references. DEDR945 p.90 directly read

Independent input evidence. Tamil oṭi/uṭai, Malayalam oṭiyuka/uṭayuka and Kannada oḍi establish short retroflex roots with distinct i/ay formations; long hole/burst forms recur independently in SD I, CD and eastern languages.

Direction. Numerous vowel-first roots across branches support original V-ṭ. Long Telugu ōḍu is not evidence that a short metathesized stage occurred because the apical remains after the vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. Short *oṭ-i/ay yields oḍi/oḍe and related strong derivatives; separately long ōṭ/ōḍ produces ōr/ōh/ōj in eastern languages. Toda vaṛ and Gondi vōṛ have initial glide development, while r/ṛ remains postvocalic. Tamil noṭi has secondary n, not root-apical promotion.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu defeat forms are explicitly questioned against run-away1041; retain them as uncertain cognacy, not extra exceptions. Gondi urung/oruŋ may instead belong with snap662, and the database ruŋ is only that cross-reference, not an attested Gondi displacement in946. Original source separates Kodagu oḍe/oḍa paradigms that the database misassigns Kannada. Kui ohpa length is queried in DEDR; keep short source and proposed ōhpa distinct. No deterministic reconstruction of every long form from the short root has been established.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR946 p.91 directly read; alternative1041/662

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Exact origin of va is unresolved without dialect/historical evidence; it may parallel rounded-vowel breaking elsewhere but that is not asserted as a dated Telugu rule. Both forms are one compound family, and the lump element gaḍḍa is not an extra root reflex.

Eligibility / caveatcore-vowel-history-variable

Independent input evidence. Tamil oṭuŋku/oṭukku, Malayalam oṭuŋŋuka/oṭukkuka, Kannada uḍugu/uḍagu and Kurux oṛᵒgnā establish vowel-first retroflex and nasal/strong formations. High u is independently present, though Kannada also has a.

Direction. SD I and North Dravidian full forms establish V-ṭ before Telugu/ Kui initial ḍ. This does not establish a unique o versus u at every regional stage.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *uṭ-uŋ > *ḍuuŋ > ḍūŋ with subsequent shortening before ŋk yields Telugu ḍuŋku; *oṭ-uŋ may instead yield short ḍoŋku directly under the different-vowel account. Long dō̃ku preserves another quantity/nasal variant. Kui ḍūmba/ḍūppa requires a labial formative distinct from Telugu velar; high u can support long u+u contraction if the prior regional root was u. No single intermediate is proven across all formations.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu uḍugu/uḍuvu retain the original order in quit/cease meanings; semantic/formative differentiation is real but not yet a deterministic phonological rule. uḍupu may belong to1009, and Kolami ūḍp/ūrp is explicitly queried. Badaga okku may reflect medial assimilation rather than concealed metathesis. A connection to compressed aṭ roots63/80 or oṭṭ960 requires independent vowel and semantic history, not an automatic merge.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR954 p.91 directly read; contrast1009/960

Independent input evidence. Tamil oṭṭu, Malayalam oṭṭam and Kannada oṭṭu/oḍḍu establish a strong medial stop independently of Telugu. Eastern singletons may reflect simplification or borrowing.

Direction. All selected forms keep vowel before the stop; the source does not require initial-stop metathesis.

Derivation and relative chronology. *oṭṭ > Telugu oṭṭu oath and oḍḍu wager; Kui oḍa and Kuvi oṭu/ottinai show regional strength variation. Kuvi ōtali has lengthening with vowel first, not a metathesis long-vowel product.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Indo-Aryan hōḍḍa/hoḍḍa and modern hoṛ forms require contact analysis; their initial h is not evidence for a Dravidian word-initial apical. CDIAL explicitly labels Sinhala oṭṭu as Tamil loan, which is not an independent Dravidian vote. Shared origin with adhere958/place962 remains a family sensitivity question.

Independent input evidence. Tamil oli/ulampu, Malayalam oli and Kannada uli independently support vowel-before-lateral. Kurux olx and Malto olg give an independently matching northern velar extension for comparison with Brahui hōɣ.

Direction. The northern full lateral-plus-velar forms are particularly strong evidence for order and for loss of lateral in Brahui; a Telugu metathesis model is unnecessary.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ol-k > Kurux olx, Malto olg and, with lateral loss plus initial h/vowel history, Brahui hōɣ. Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 proposes this cluster-loss analysis and compares other lost preconsonantal laterals. Telugu uliyu/ulivu retains order; Tamil ōl/ōlam involves separate quantity formation. No root-lateral promotion is established.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Bray instead proposed imitative hō plus hiatus-bridging ɣ; Emeneau argues the comparative velar extension favors inheritance but leaves imperative/prohibitive ɣ absence unresolved. The source does not supply every intermediate explaining Brahui length and h. Keep that uncertainty visible; neither competing account is initial liquid metathesis. Tamil/Malayalam ulapp versus ulamp is nasal/strength variation. Potential relationship to strong oll expressives985 is not assumed.

Mechanism scope. Brahui cluster-member loss; competing imitative origin, not initial apical metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR996; Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 §§2.2–3 directly read; https://www.jstor.org/stable/619537

Independent input evidence. Tamil kakku, Malayalam kakkuka, Gondi kakk/kokk, Konda kak and the Pengo/Manda kak bases independently support the nonapical root. Kannada kaṛ̆ku (=kaẓku) supplies a real apical-bearing variant beside kakku, so an apical input cannot simply be rejected because the headword is kak.

Direction. A regional *kaẓ-k could give Kannada kaẓku and Telugu krakku, but the many nonapical forms do not uniquely establish whether the apical is inherited, secondary or belongs to a different convergent formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. Two alternatives remain: (1) *kaẓ-k > *kẓak > krakku, with separate k strengthening, while other branches assimilate ẓk to kk; (2) inherited *kak > kakku, with secondary r in Telugu on the literary Cr pattern and a separately remodeled Kannada variant. Pengo kak + intensive-ba > kabga has a distinct velar–labial alternation, independently supported by its simple stem.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu krakku is not counted as a secure classical displacement positive. Kannada kaẓku is the evidence that could favor that analysis, but its age and wider correspondences need checking. Cough/vomit vocabulary also permits expressive expansion. DEDR comparison1477 kāl is not accepted without independent semantic/phonological review. Badaga proper names and repeated God Šiva stories do not add lexical roots. The Kondh intensive and Telugu initial-r problem are separate processes in one family.

Mechanism scope. Ambiguous earlier apical versus secondary r in Telugu; separate Kondh morphological velar/labial alternation.

Scholarly references. DEDR1079; Garrett and Blevins2009 p.538 ex.20b; panel-030

Eligibility / caveatmixed-vowel-regional-apical

Independent input evidence. Tamil kaṭavu/kaṭāri, Kannada kaḍasu and Kurux kaḍrū independently establish medial retroflex and full order; they do not establish one common ending for every cattle term.

Direction. Full southern and northern forms favor k-V-apical before Konda gṛālu and Kui grāḍu. Kota kēv has only a conjectured earlier cluster in DEDR.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kaṭ-al > *kṛāl > gṛālu and Kui grāḍu adds regional stop/rhotic and final-lateral changes; Kuvi ḍālu can follow C1 loss from a cluster. Telugu krēpu has unexplained ē/p under this comparison and alternatively belongs to1594.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep Telugu krēpu ambiguous in both entries, never two positive votes. Kui gāṛo retains postvocalic apical while ḍrāḍu alters C1; livestock age/sex labels and possible diffusion need separate lexical history. IA cattle comparanda are contact evidence, not extra Dravidian votes.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 1123; current comparative cluster panel; DEDR alternative1594; no merged root asserted

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil karu/karuku, Kannada karaku/karñ-type formations and Gondi kar support short kar independently, beside widespread long kār. Exact Telugu -aŋ formation is not supplied by bare karu.

Direction. Full kar order across branches favors displacement in Telugu krā̃gu and Kui krumu/grīpa; their vowel differences require distinct formation histories.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kar-aŋ > *krāŋ > krā̃gu; kaggu/kaŋgu may follow lost r or direct medial assimilation. Kui *kar-um > krum could preserve the formative u by syncope/assimilation, whereas grīpa needs high-vowel formation or other quality change.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Long kāru is a separate retained formation, not proof every member had long input. Kui ī and Telugu inferred a remain unresolved. Kannada/Toda dark and charcoal derivatives contain internal assimilation/glide changes, not initial promotion. Personal/place names are not independent etyma.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Telugu short versus Kui long follows different formations; the contrast does not prove contraction followed by shortening in Telugu. Kannada gajiga/gajjuga can be medial loss/palatalization without initial exchange; Tulu gajigɛ may be contact. Composite malformed Tamil row preserved as source evidence, not several independent records.

Independent input evidence. Tamil kaẓumu gives full apical and labial formation; Kui garja keeps a postvocalic rhotic but has a different palatal extension.

Direction. Tamil full order and Kui medial apical make Telugu krammu/kraccu plausibly innovative.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kaẓ-m > *kẓam > krammu gives short vowel plus doubled labial; kraccu requires a different palatal formative. Syncope from *kaẓ-um before displacement is possible; final u is not automatically a contracting suffix.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The Tamil form supports the labial relationship but not exact geminate antiquity. Sparse distribution permits old contact, while no source establishes it. Kui garja is retained relative to the initial-order target despite separate affricate development.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatlong-free-root-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gondi, Konda, Pengo and Manda independently attest kāl, establishing both long quantity and a free-root shape.

Direction. k precedes the long vowel and l follows it throughout the independently compared branches. Toda ō and Parji ē are local vowel reflexes, not transferred vowels.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kāl > Telugu kālu, Kui kāḍu, Kuvi kāl retains original order; Kui l>ḍ is compatible with the same change in displaced lateral roots but here occurs without displacement. Toda kōl and compound kōs̱ show vowel change and conditioned final fricativization. Tulu kārɯ has the lateral/rhotic correspondence.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The long free root is doubly outside the canonical short bound-root domain. Brahui trikkal is a compound whose initial tr belongs to the numeral material, not a reversal of kāl; inherited status and quantity of its kal member need separate contact investigation. Markodi short kar versus kār preserves source quantity variation, which cannot establish Proto-Dravidian short quantity. No independent bare-root metathesis is present.

Mechanism scope. Retention with vowel and lateral correspondences.

Scholarly references. DEDR1479; PSS83 p.229 (oldDED1238)

Independent input evidence. Konda kaṛaŋ maran:kṛāŋ mrānu supplies a directly matching full versus clustered compound; Tulu korŋgi/korŋgu supplies retained r.

Direction. Both members of the Konda compound have independent full forms, establishing their order without privileging Telugu.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Botanical names can diffuse. Kannada kānagu has a different species identification (Dalbergia), so its semantic identity is uncertain. Exact Telugu medial -nu-gu versus Konda -ŋ needs nominal history; it is not supplied by a bare contraction.

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil cilai, Malayalam cila/cilekka, Kannada kele and Tulu kele-puni independently support a low-a formation with initial k/c-V-l. Tamil cil and Gondi kil also supply a bare root; reduplicative shrieking stems have different morphology.

Direction. Southern and Gondi full forms support k-V-l before Kui kl-. Palatalization in Tamil and some Kannada/Telugu forms is a separate initial k development; none requires reconstructing initial c in the common input.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kil-a-p > *klēp > klāpa is the K80 lowering analysis; an alternative lowers/assimilates before cluster creation. Kui klīri and Kuvi klīrinai show a different high-vowel expressive formation, not an exception to low-a-specific lowering. Telugu kilārucu/kelayu/celãgu retains initial vowel/l order.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Postconsonantal l lies outside the narrow Telugu r/ṟ/ẓ metathesis set, while Kui admits it. This supports a structural language contrast, not simply a difference in frequency. Exact ancient morphology of the long ā Telugu expressive stem and klīri is not recoverable from the bare *kil head alone. Toda kīl ik is explicitly a Badaga loan; initial-loss Kota iḍ and alternative-cognacy jelk remain uncertain. Toda kv-style processes elsewhere must not be generalized to this root.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 pp.497–499 item 6; PSS83 p.230 post-C sonorant restriction; DEDR 1574

Independent input evidence. Kannada kaẓal and Tamil kiẓāaṉ independently supply a medial approximant and a following low vowel, with distinct final l/n.

Direction. The full cross-language forms favor earlier k-V-ẓ before Telugu krānu; kānu can subsequently lose r.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kaẓ-an > *kẓān > krānu > kānu preserves final n. Tamil ki and long ā plus Kannada final l show that this exact immediate form is reconstructed, not simply copied from one modern cognate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Dairy vocabulary is geographically narrow and may diffuse. Vowel alternation and final n/l morphology remain unresolved; do not treat each differing ending as an independently confirmed contraction input.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Kannada kiṟi/kiṟa/kiṟu and Tulu kiri/kiru independently establish the velar and short vowel; Tamil ciṟu reflects palatalization rather than an originally universal c.

Direction. The full southern root supports earlier ki-apical order before Telugu kriyyu. Telugu ciṟu retains full order and palatalizes; kriyyu can block that context after reordering.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kiṟ-y > *kṟiy > kriyyu, with strengthening of the formative, or high-vowel syncope before movement. krēpu calf has a separate low/long formation or belongs to1123, so it is not a secure positive here.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The database mouse compound *kiṯṯ-eli is not an ancestor of all small/young derivatives. Palatalization chronology is plausible but initial k preservation alone is insufficient because borrowing or expressive formations can also preserve k. Strong ṟṟ/tt variants are distinct formations.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 1594; current comparative cluster panel

Independent input evidence. Tamil kiṟukiṟu/kiṟukku, Kannada giṟi/giṟu/giṟa and Tulu giriyuni independently establish k-i-apical order and several formations.

Direction. The comparative full stems agree with retained Brahui kirrefing, not an initial kr- stem.

Derivation and relative chronology. Intervocalic voicing and ṟ>r vary by language; expressive gemination gives giṟṟ-/girr- without initial displacement. Emeneau analyzes Brahui kirrefing as causative of hypothetical *kirreng, explicitly not an attested simplex.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a k-initial retention control for the very small Brahui t/p-heavy sample. Its expressive geminates and several suffix vowels prevent treating every form as one identical singleton formation. Telugu gīra has secondary or separate quantity; Badaga kiri moguḍu funeral object is semantically uncertain. Marathi girakṇẽ is a contact comparison, not an independent inherited Dravidian vote.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

PropertyAnnotation

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam kiẓakku and Kannada kiẓ/kiẓgu independently establish a short allomorph alongside long kīẓ. Parji kiṛi corroborates short vowel before apical. K03 p.128 uses immediate *kiẓ-nd for Telugu below.

Direction. Southern short and long forms establish k-V-apical order. Telugu krinda places the apical before the vowel; kinda can be connected to it by independently attested cluster simplification.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kiẓ-nd > *kẓind > krind > kind gives krinda/kinda. Displacement removes the front vowel from immediately after k, blocking Telugu k>c palatalization; later r-loss restores ki after that palatalization has ceased to act on this item. Long kīḍupaḍu retains the apical medially; krī may be a separate contraction or abbreviated derivative.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a relative chronology argument conditional on inheritance and the independently established palatalization environment, not proof from an isolated unpalatalized k. Do not shorten the citation root kīẓ ad hoc: a short allomorph is independently attested. Exact -nd and -nc history is less secure than initial order. Nilgiri/Brahui kī types admit medial-apical loss without displacement; they do not independently prove the Telugu route.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 p.128 Rule 14, p.158 Rule 21; DEDR 1619

Independent input evidence. Kannada guḍḍu and Tulu kuḍu establish a nonrhotic round-object stem. Konda gurḍu/gurzu supplies a real r-bearing comparison, unlike its explicitly Telugu-borrowed guḍu.

Direction. The extra r in Telugu gruḍḍu may correspond to Konda gurḍ, but the wider comparison does not uniquely establish its antiquity.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *gur-ḍ > gruḍḍu with strengthening; alternatively guḍḍu acquires literary r or interacts with blind1787, and Konda rhotic variants require their own source history. guḍḍu is not automatically evidence of later r loss.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Blind1787 has independent kuruḍu; egg does not share that reconstruction merely through homophony. Konda/Kuvi loan labels apply to guḍu, not automatically all rhotic variants. Earlier attestations of egg gruḍḍu/gurḍu would distinguish the alternatives.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not impose one identical suffix vowel on both languages. Manda grūc adds long ū/palatal formation not explained by that o-a derivation. Alternative related sink1826 supplies only clusters and is tested in family-merge sensitivity.

Direction. The full r-bearing monkey name favors earlier k-V-r before Telugu krō̃ti; exact dental versus velar suffix correspondence remains a separate question.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kor-ant > *krōnt > krō̃ti > kō̃ti; this is not direct transformation of Tamil kuraŋku into Telugu. A velar-to-dental suffix history or distinct formative must be justified.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Tamil kōnti is explicitly Telugu borrowing. Kannada/Tulu kōti and central kōti may also diffuse, but absent explicit source evidence remain uncertain transmission cases, not automatic independent metatheses. Species and monkey-name replacement need preservation.

Direction. Full southern stems favor Kui krusu as innovative; Telugu kruyyu also fits a displaced r-root but alternatively belongs to1851.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu kruyyu is ambiguous in both competing etymologies and contributes no secure D vote. Gondi kurumne has full r but expressive/adverbial morphology. IA kurumāṇa faded is a contact comparison, not evidence deciding direction.

d1787: blind

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd1787
Comparative input*kur-uṭ-V; immediate *kur-ḍ-V
Initial consonantk
V1 quality / quantityu / short
C2 identity / structurer / singleton
Following vowelu

Boundary evidenceWhole blindness stem supported independently; person endings do not add etyma; timing of V2 syncope remains inferential.
Input classshort-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencehigh
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam kuruṭu and Kannada kuruḍu independently supply high-u disyllabic input. Tulu kurḍu and Kota kurḍ independently support the syncopated medial cluster, while Kannada kuḍḍu shows its assimilated alternative.

Direction. The full and syncopated southern series establishes k-u-r ordering. Telugu gruḍḍi/gruḍḍu has the rhotic before u; guḍḍi is attested beside it but cannot be mechanically generalized to every language with guḍḍi.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kur-uḍ-V > *kur-ḍ-V > *kru-ḍḍ-V > gruḍḍi/gruḍḍu > guḍḍi, with initial k/g alternation and later r loss. Strengthening might precede displacement; *kurḍḍ > kruḍḍ yields the same result. Contraction followed by shortening is another possible route. Final i/u and gender formations remain separate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Identical u+u does not guarantee a long modern vowel: the independently attested consonantal branch is crucial. Initial g is not explained by naming the r/vowel exchange. Gondi/Kolami/Naikri guḍḍi could be Telugu loans or local medial assimilation; no observed cluster establishes independent metathesis there. Malto qoṭri may involve internal consonant reversal relative to kur-ṭ, but its precise morphology and quantity require separate study.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K61 §§1.142–154; K03 pp.130–131,157–162; DEDR 1787

PropertyAnnotation

Input classshort-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant

Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil kuẓi pit contrasts with kuẓal/kuẓai tube; Malayalam kuẓa/kuẓal and Kannada koẓal/koẓavi independently establish low-a tube formations. Gondi koṛi and Konda kuṛk corroborate initial k-V-apical order.

Direction. Independent full southern/central forms support k-V-ẓ before Telugu kr and old kẓ. Different high/low and consonantal formations must not be collapsed to a single convenient *koẓ-a input.

Derivation and relative chronology. Low-a *koẓ-al/av > *kẓōl/ōv > krōlu/krōvi, then kōlu. A consonantal *koẓ-cc > *kẓocc > kroccu explains short digging forms; old kẓōce has a distinct long variant. Kui kṛāu/Kuvi gṛāyu are displaced pit names with low outcome, but independently known pit *kuẓ-i is not the same low-a tube derivative. Exact pit-name -ay formation needs reconstruction.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. K80 explicitly contrasts Kui pit kṛāu and tube krōḍu; that semantic distinction describes distribution without itself explaining a sound condition. Kui krūpa has another vowel/formation. Telugu kukki/goppu could be direct medial assimilation; do not infer concealed metathesis merely from lost ẓ. Kannada kōvi is explicitly Telugu borrowing. The porridge *kūẓ reconstruction attached to this group is not evidence for a long pit input.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 pp.497–499 item 7; DEDR 1818; K61 pp.67–68 old kẓ clusters

Eligibility / caveatcore-formation-uncertain

Independent input evidence. Tamil kuẓai, Malayalam kuẓayuka and Kannada koẓe independently support a medial approximant. Exact lateral formative behind Telugu ḷḷ is not supplied by these low-ay verbs.

Direction. Full southern approximant stems favor promotion in kruḷḷu, but the extra final lateral needs morphology or redistribution.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *kuẓ-l > *kẓu-l > kruḷḷu, or a fuller derivative plus syncope, supplies a short consonantal route. kuḷḷu may lose cluster r or reflect direct medial assimilation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep distinct from truḷḷu3364 with no independent r/ẓ. Gondi kukk and Kannada kocce can develop by medial assimilation; no concealed initial cluster is required. Low-a source formation does not independently verify the assumed lateral suffix.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not count this as an independent secure metathesis root while its full input is missing. Treat merger with1767 in sensitivity; phonetic and semantic support are stronger than an invented output-based proto-vowel.

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil kuṟu:kuṟṟu, Kota kur:kut and Gondi kurkal independently establish an apical weak/strong family. Kannada gurdu provides a close r+d formation.

Direction. Kannada gurdu beside guddu and Telugu gruddu favors displacement of an earlier medial apical in at least the fist-striking formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kur-d > *krud > gruddu with initial/suffix voicing and strengthening is plausible; guddu can be direct rd assimilation or later cluster-r loss. Labial kummu/guppu formations must be analyzed separately.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The many expressive impact words and ṯṯ/tt changes do not all share one literal r root. Telugu krummu is embedded in a gloss, not a separately linked form in this annotation. Source-level extraction could recover it without adding a root. Marathi guddā could reflect diffusion but does not decide it.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 1850; current comparative cluster panel

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu retained kuṟu/kuṟuca and kundu must remain in the denominator; kruyyu is A in both entries. The head *kuṯ-ay is not the immediate source of every strong child/jackal formation. Source-corrupted Kota fragments are not separate phonological evidence.

Independent input evidence. Tamil kuṟai and Malayalam kuṟekka independently support low-ay cutting formation; Kannada koṟe and the shorter Tamil kuṟu support additional vowel histories. Central Dravidian kud/kut forms support medial apical but not identical suffixes.

Direction. Southern/Central k-V-apical order supports earlier unshifted root. Kui krāpa has moved r before V; Old Telugu kōṟa remains V-before-r and is a long nominal formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *koṯ-a-p > *krōp > krāp gives Kui krāpa under contraction then lowering; pre-contraction o>a is the competing order. Kannada korcu > koccu and Tulu koccu can arise by medial assimilation. Telugu kōṟa has a long vowel but no initial cluster and is not a displaced reflex.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. K80’s low-a comparison has independent southern support, but exact causative p formation and its vowel remain reconstructed. Do not apply the expected short-root change to the Old Telugu long noun without establishing its grade. Cutting, boring and fire-kindling meanings may converge with d2168; the source explicitly questions some Kannada comparisons.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 pp.497–499 item 8; DEDR 1859

Independent input evidence. Tamil kūlam and Konda/Kui/Kuvi/Pengo/Manda kūli independently support long ū before l, with distinct final formations.

Direction. The southern long root and eastern long forms agree on k-V-l order. No reconstructed short *kul is required by this set.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kūl-i > Kui kūḍi, Kuvi/Pengo/Manda kūli preserves order; l>ḍ does not depend on an earlier initial cluster. Brahui xōlum could match a different suffix and vowel history, but DEDR explicitly offers an Indo-Aryan alternative.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A long-vowel bound-formation control, unlike the doubly restricted free root kāl. Agricultural vocabulary can diffuse, so repeated eastern attestations do not alone prove inheritance; the relevant negative phonological observation remains long kūl rather than klū. Brahui xōlum is not a secure inherited vote because the source also compares Sanskrit godhūma through DBIA123. Do not confuse this entry with neighboring kūli wages1905.

Mechanism scope. Long-input retention; Brahui cognacy unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR1906; DEN1 1972 p.416 entryS278; PSS83 p.229

Independent input evidence. Konda ker independently supplies k-e-r order, but its stem notation ker- does not independently establish a following a. K80 reconstructs *ker-a from this comparison.

Direction. The full Konda root and initial gr in all other reflexes support displacement, with separate k>g. Direction of e/a quality change is an additional issue, not settled by consonant order.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *ker-a > *krē > grē, with Kui lowering to grā in one dialect; alternatively pre-contraction e>a before a yields grā. Kuvi grec, Pengo gre and Manda grepa preserve e. Exact labial/palatal formative and vowel quantities differ.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kui grāpa/grēpa is a valuable dialect contrast, but cannot independently validate the reconstructed low V2 which helps explain it. No Telugu cognate is supplied. Do not count each language’s suffix as an independent root. The regional proto-level is more defensible than a pan-Dravidian *grä already containing the outcome.

Independent input evidence. Tamil kiḷai ramify/kindred and Kannada keḷe/geḷe independently establish a short low-formative series alongside Tamil kēḷ friend. Short vowel cannot be rejected merely because the dictionary headword selects long kēḷ.

Direction. Southern short and long forms have V before lateral; Kui klāmbu has initial cluster and additional nominal morphology. Direction of displacement is plausible independently of the long ā outcome.

Derivation and relative chronology. *keḷ-a-mbu > *klēmbu > klāmbu is K80-type contraction then lowering; pre-contraction e>a is also possible. Plural klāpka has stem/number alternation with mb/pk, not a second independent metathesis root. Kannada geṇe/geṇiya and Tulu geṇe have medial lateral-to-nasal developments.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The exact -mbu formative should be checked against Kui nominal morphology; Tamil kiḷai alone does not supply it. K80 prints old DED 1628, but the correct old number is 1678 (modern2018); 1628 is do1957. Badaga kliūgidu is a plant name with a different Kannada comparison and is not evidence for lateral displacement in friend; its inclusion would manufacture an exception to southern distribution.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

PropertyAnnotation

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil koẓu/koẓuppu, Malayalam koẓu/koẓukka and Kannada korvu/korbu independently support o-ẓ and high-u/labial formations. Gondi koṛvinj and Konda koṛvu strengthen the short labial comparison; Tamil kōẓ is a separately attested long grade.

Direction. Southern, Gondi, Konda and central forms agree on k-o-apical. Telugu krovvu and Kui krōga instead place the apical next to k. The input labial versus velar extensions cannot be collapsed into one identical stem.

Derivation and relative chronology. *koẓ-w > *kẓow > krovvu > kovvu gives Telugu schematically, with labial gemination a separate issue. Kui *koẓ-(u)-k > krōg gives a long mid vowel without the low ā found after independently low-a formations. Pengo kṛō and Manda kṛuva preserve different quantity/suffix histories. Kannada korbu > kobbu permits medial assimilation without an initial kr stage.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a useful high-u comparison for eastern lowering, but exact u/zero in each immediate velar input is not supplied by the bare root alone. Toda kvāv/kvaḷp has initial k-v after loss/change of ẓ and a different vowel history; it is not evidence of the same k-r metathesis. Kuvi candle klōva is semantically plausible from fat/tallow yet requires source/contact scrutiny; kept uncertain. Related derivatives count as one family.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 2146; K80 low-a lowering hypothesis; K03 Rule 21

d2149 — new, sprout, young; kinship derivatives

d2149: new, sprout, young; kinship derivatives

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd2149
Comparative input*koẓ-utt-V; short *koẓ-V and long *kōẓ formations
Initial consonantk
V1 quality / quantityo / mixed by formation
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu/unknown
Root/formation shapeCVC-u-tt / CVC-V / CVVC
Grammatical categoryadjective/verb/noun
Boundary evidenceShort new adjective and short/long kinship formations must be separate input classes; exact tt extension is reconstructed, not identical to Tamil nt.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencehigh
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil koẓuntu, Malayalam koẓunnu, Gondi koṛs and Parji koṛ/koṛc independently establish k-V-apical order. K03 pp.159,198 distinguishes short *koẓ-utt-V new from short/long kinship formations.

Direction. Full southern and Central Dravidian forms support V before apical; Telugu krotta has changed order. Modern kotta is independently documented by K03 as the r-loss continuation, making concealed displacement demonstrable here.

Derivation and relative chronology. *koẓ-utt-V > *koẓ-tt-V > *kẓott-V > krott-V > kotta is the proposed short branch. The tt belongs to the formation before metathesis in K03, not automatic new gemination. Telugu koḍuku preserves medial *ẓ > ḍ; kōḍalu has a long root grade. Kui kuṛa/kṛua and Kuvi koṛgi/kṛōgi show different formations and dialect outcomes.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Tamil koẓuntu has nt, not the identical tt formation: do not invent nt>tt to derive Telugu from Tamil directly. Exact *-utt support is the comparative reconstruction, whereas high-u formation is independently visible. Kui kṛua preserves two vowels and need not represent contraction; Kuvi long ō needs its own vowel/quantity history. Some kinship/nasal forms may have assimilated medially; neither those nor the related crop and kinship derivatives count as independent roots. Konda kodma is explicitly Telugu borrowing.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.158–159 example 90, p.198 *koẓ-utt-V; DEDR 2149

Independent input evidence. Tamil kō:kōr and Kannada kō establish a long vowel-final root with variable extensions. Tamil/Malayalam kōrvai/kōrva have r and v, while kōvai lacks r.

Direction. Telugu krōva could promote derivative r, or add r to the kōva formation; the root is not independently a short CVr.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *kōr-v > krōv is long-vowel reordering; alternatively kōva > krōva by analogy. kōva may be retained r-less derivation or later r loss. The alternatives are observationally unresolved.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The productive-looking suffix alternants independently motivate a boundary, but not its age or order. This is excluded from secure D. Long nonrhotic derivatives across central languages cannot be read as concealed metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada and Konda kōl independently establish a long-vowel free root; Telugu kōla and eastern kōl/kōḍu continue that input.

Direction. The long vowel precedes the lateral across several branches. Toda initial kv contains a labial associated with the rounded vowel, not the displaced reflex of root-final l, whose fricative reflex remains after the vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. *kōl > kōla/kōlu retains order. Kui kōḍu and plural kōṭka change the medial/final lateral to a stop without promoting it. Toda kōl > kvɨ̄s̱ requires vowel breaking and lateral fricativization, not k-l metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A strong independent long/free-root control, including Kui/Kuvi plural formations that retain initial order. Short Gondi kola/Kolami kolā cannot establish original short V against the broad long comparison and may be local shortening. Many Badaga stick compounds and proper names are not independent etyma. The imported *kōy-il palace reconstruction is unrelated metadata, excluded.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 2237; PSS83 pp.229–230 long/free-root restriction

Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh for segment order; medium for exact common suffix
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Konda saras/sarasu and Gondi taras/taranj independently support initial s/t-a-r-a and a final s/nj alternation. Tamil ara/arā/aravu and Malayalam aravu agree in r following the first vowel but have lost initial c; they cannot alone reconstruct an originally vowel-initial root.

Direction. Konda and Gondi favor C-a-r before eastern Cr. Southern initial loss is independently comparable with broader c-loss correspondences, not evidence that Telugu added t. Tamil final ā is analyzed by K03 through -ac > -ah > ā, separately from first-syllable metathesis.

Derivation and relative chronology. K03 reconstructs *car-a-ncc > regional *tar-a-ncc > *trā-ncc > trā̃cu. Kui *sar-as > srāsu/srācu; Kuvi/Pengo *srāc > rāc with first-member loss. Manda trehe retains the initial cluster but changes final consonant/vowel. Nasal/geminate and simple-s variants require distinct immediate formations.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Direction is strongly comparative; exact shared innovation still depends on dating branch-specific s/t and suffix developments. Telugu nasal vowel and Gondi taranj support a nasal formation independently, while many cognates have no nasal. The Prakrit sarāhaya comparison in DEDR/K03 may reflect borrowing and is not an independent Dravidian denominator. Konda srāsu is quoted in K03 p.122 but absent from this database group; do not silently manufacture a database variant.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.122–123 n.5(1); DEDR 2359; DNM sarāhaya cited there

d2456 — incline, side; disputed eastern descend

d2456: incline, side; disputed eastern descend

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd2456
Comparative input*cāy; alternative eastern *i/eṟ-a (d516)
Initial consonantc
V1 quality / quantityā / long in southern root; short under alternative eastern etymology
C2 identity / structurey / singleton
Following vowelzero/a
Root/formation shapeCVVC / alternative VC-a
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceTwo competing roots are alternatives, not two independent eastern observations.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh southern; low eastern cognacy
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatalternative-cognacy-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil cāy, Malayalam cāyka and Telugu cāya independently support initial c with long ā and following glide. Eastern jāpa and Manda jē/hē can instead be compared with the descend root d516; their initial consonants and vowels do not settle cognacy by themselves.

Direction. The southern incline group has unambiguous c-ā-y order. K80 reassigns some eastern forms to *eṟ-a and a displacement/lowering history, while DEDR places them under cāy and cites Burrow1976 pp.40–41.

Derivation and relative chronology. Southern *cāy > cāy/cāya and Malayalam āyka/āñcuka involves initial c loss and stem/tense changes, not apical transfer. If eastern *cāy-p is right, jāpa need not metathesize. If the d516 comparison is right, *eṟ-a-p > *ṟēp > jāpa involves displacement, lowering and apical-to-j; Manda jē/hē preserves a nonlow vowel and needs its own vowel history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep the competing etymologies explicit; do not count the same Kui/Manda words once as retained incline and again as metathesized descend. Burrow1976 A sketch of Manda grammar in comparison with Pengo, Dravidian Linguistics V pp.39–56 has been identified, but pp.40–41 have not been read directly. Its argument is therefore not reconstructed from the citation. Needed: full Manda paradigm, comparative c/j versus ṟ/j correspondences and shared derivative morphology.

Mechanism scope. Southern retention; eastern cognacy determines whether any metathesis occurred.

Scholarly references. DEDR2456 and516; K80 pp.498–499; Burrow1976 pp.40–41 cited by DEDR, not directly consulted

Independent input evidence. Kolami sire/cīre, Naikri śīre and Parji cīr independently support c-V-r but mix short/long grades. Gondi serkā/sirkā and sarēkā/saṛēka support a velar tree formation; exact V1/V2 before metathesis remains uncertain.

Direction. Multiple central and Gondi forms favor s-V-r before Kui srēko. The imported *srēk-o reconstruction adopts the shifted cluster and cannot be used to claim that Gondi inserted its vowel without independent argument.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *ser-V-k > srēk gives Kui; *srēk > rēk gives Kuvi/Pengo/Manda and some Gondi lects. Alternative regional borrowing of srēko/rēko is plausible for a culturally salient tree name. Long cīr and short serk cannot be collapsed to assert unrestricted long-vowel metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No Telugu attestation in the linked corpus. The restricted geography and regional tree-name traffic weaken family-wide inheritance claims. Gondi full and r-initial variants preserve useful lect evidence, but distinct suffix vowels and quantity prevent a deterministic conditioning assignment. Latin B. latifolia is a parser fragment, not a Gondi word.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 2628; Burrow–Emeneau 1972 DEN1 p.407 entry 2160; Southworth 2006 *cir/cīr

d2674 — salt, brackish/astringent

d2674: salt, brackish/astringent

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd2674
Comparative input*cup; *cow-ar/*cov-ar > *ow-ar
Initial consonantc/zero
V1 quality / quantityu/o / short
C2 identity / structurep/w / singleton
Following vowela/zero
Root/formation shapeCVC / CVw-ar
Grammatical categorynoun/verb/adjective
Boundary evidenceBare *cup and low-a labial extension distinguished independently.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for full low-a extension; exact vowel grades differ
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatnonapical-contraction-control

Independent input evidence. Central sup/cup preserves an initial consonant also reflected by Gondi savvar/hovar, while southern uppu and uvar independently support a stop versus intervocalic labial alternation and the low-a extended formation. Tamil uvar and Gondi havar/savvar are independent of the eastern long-vowel outcomes.

Direction. Comparative evidence favors an earlier full labial-containing *cow-ar/*ov-ar, not treating modern long sōr/sār as an original root. The r is already final in the extension and never becomes pre-vocalic in eastern forms.

Derivation and relative chronology. *cow-ar > *cōr > Konda sōru, Pengo sōr, versus Kui sāru/Kuvi hāru/Manda jār involves intervocalic labial loss/contraction and eastern lowering. Lowering may precede contraction through *cawar or follow contraction of a low-a formation; the outputs alone do not determine which. Southern *ov-ar gives uvar/ogar, with Malayalam ōr showing an independent contraction parallel. Telugu vagaru may involve initial labial/prothetic or analogical restructuring, not established vowel-r metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is evidence about lowering in contracted roots, not an apical metathesis positive. It helps separate the two processes and avoids defining lowering by the presence of Cr. K80 p.498 prints Pengo hōr where DEDR gives sōr: preserve the source discrepancy, do not silently replace the database. Salt vocabulary can diffuse; the full southern/central contrast still independently establishes the earlier order. Nihali copo is a contact comparison, not a Dravidian language vote.

Mechanism scope. Labial loss/contraction; not initial apical metathesis.

Scholarly references. K80 p.498 item4; DEDR2674; K03 p.97 example10 (ogaru perhaps a Kannada loan; Gondi sawwor vowel metathesis)

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Brahui kurring retains postvocalic r and has a separately discussed irregular initial k; Emeneau1997 also queries kūžing with1876/2687, not a settled comparison. Marathi wrinkle vocabulary can show contact but is not an extra family vote.

d2698 — whirl, roll, revolve

d2698: whirl, roll, revolve

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd2698
Comparative input*cuẓ-i/a; initial-loss *uẓ-al and related formations
Initial consonantc/zero
V1 quality / quantityu/o / short
C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following voweli/a
Root/formation shapeCVC-i / CVC-a-l / VC-a-l
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceWhirl *cuẓ-i versus roll *uẓ-al; initial c loss and long grade separately annotated.
Input classuncertain-initial-order
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for uẓ-al order; medium for exact Telugu trajectory
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatconditional-displacement

Independent input evidence. Tamil cuẓi/cuẓal alongside uẓal, Malayalam cuẓaluka/uẓaluka, and Kannada suẓi/toẓal/uẓal independently support both c-initial and initial-loss families, with a second lateral in the roll formation. Telugu suḍi retains the first type; ḍollu is compared with the second.

Direction. Several branches establish vowel before ẓ and a following l in uẓal, giving a much stronger potential direction for roll ḍollu than for homophonous fall d2988. Initial c loss is independently attested, although whether it preceded displacement in Telugu itself is not directly dated.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *cuẓ-al > *uẓ-al > *oẓ-al > *ẓōl > ḍollu requires contraction followed by shortening/gemination, or an earlier syncope route with a consonantal derivative. K61 p.54 §1.127 discusses alternative suffix/quantity histories. Telugu suḍi continues *cuẓ-i without displacement. Kui ḍuṛi retains an apical after u and may have initial c>ḍ plus a medial rhotic; its initial ḍ is not sufficient evidence of the vowel-initial pathway.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu roll is a plausible displacement family, but exact input and collision with regional fall ḍollu d2988 prevent a strict mechanism claim. A pathway cẓ > ẓ after displacement would give the same surviving initial segment as c loss before displacement; chronology is not forced. Several Telugu fragments split ḍol(u)cu into bogus forms; restore only in source supplement, preserve raw data. Gondi uḍ/uḍḍ has medial change and retains initial u.

Mechanism scope. Plausible roll displacement with quantity alternatives and potential lexical convergence.

Scholarly references. DEDR 2698; K61 p.54 §1.127 (prior page verification); original DEDR SQL rows 63979–63999; compare DEDR 2988

Eligibility / caveatbrahui-displacement-comparison

Independent input evidence. Tamil cori/cura/cōr and tōr, Kannada suri/sōr/tore, Kota corv/toyr and Telugu torūgu/torāgu/toṟãgu establish full vowel-before-r order with several initial and quantity correspondences.

Direction. Brahui curring retains full order whereas trump/tramp have r before the vowel. PSS83 p.245 treats drop as a stronger metathesis example than simple aphaeresis, because output vowel is not the expected second i.

Derivation and relative chronology. A pre-Brahui full *tur/tor-V-mp > *tr-V-mp > trump/tramp is a displacement-family comparison. Exact V2, t/c development and a/u outcomes are not jointly established; the modern Telugu long suffix vowels are not automatically the Brahui input. Parji cōrp > cōp illustrates direct medial r loss. Toda tvar has a preceding glide but r remains after a.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The traditional seven-item Brahui sample calls most roots t-initial, but this family has independently attested c/t variants, so a categorical Proto-Dravidian c exclusion is not justified. Telugu jobbillu is opaque assimilation or questionable cognacy, not positive metathesis. Markodi cre blood beside core-like forms is a fresh possible local syncope/displacement comparison, not automatically the old Telugu change. Konda sō- has an alternative d2867 link. A compound torgi stranded in a gloss still needs original-page recovery.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR2883; PSS83 pp.244–245 citing Emeneau1971 pp.192–194

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil neruppu, Malayalam nerippu, Gondi nirvānā and Parji nir independently support n-V-r, with i/e and labial/velar formative variation. Neither imported *nijur nor **nirVvV is treated as uniquely established.

Direction. Several branches retain initial n-V-r. Telugu nippu lacks r; Kui drē instead has r immediately after a stop that may continue n through denasalization.

Derivation and relative chronology. Telugu *nir-pp > nipp via medial r-p assimilation is sufficient; a hidden *nripp > nipp trajectory remains possible but unproved. Kui *nir-V > *nrē > drē combines displacement/contraction and n>d, with exact ancient V2 unresolved. Kurux niyū̃r requires additional medial vowel/glide history and is not simple evidence for the same immediate input.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The geminate labial environment alone does not certify Telugu metathesis: nippu is opaque without an attested nr/dr intermediate. This is a crucial comparison with trippu and krovvu. Related burning eri d811 may involve nasal prothesis/loss, but that deeper union remains a sensitivity hypothesis. Initial n is independently recoverable here and must not be removed to make a vowel-initial metathesis case.

Mechanism scope. Opaque Telugu medial reduction; eastern displacement with denasalization.

Scholarly references. DEDR 2929; K03 Rule 21 denasalization; comparison DEDR 811

Independent input evidence. Gondi, Kolami and Kui/Kuvi independently have initial ḍ/d before the vowel and a following lateral or its loss. The lone Telugu ūḍu has a different shape and long vowel, insufficient to reverse the comparative direction for the whole family.

Direction. Broad regional agreement favors earlier ḍ-V-l for this set; there is no independently attested common *uḍal input here. Telugu ūḍu may be a related different formation, analogical associate or separate cognate hypothesis.

Derivation and relative chronology. *ḍol > ḍollu/ḍol, and *ḍol-p > ḍōpa with lateral loss/assimilation and compensatory quantity, are local candidate developments. Deriving all initial ḍ from vowel/apical exchange would require independent evidence not supplied by these reflexes.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Initial retroflexion is not a metathesis diagnosis. The near-homophonous rolling forms in d2698 may have converged with this fall/death set, but conflating them would falsely supply a southern unshifted cognate. Long ūḍu versus short ḍul- deserves dictionary/historical morphology work; for now code its direction uncertain. No confirmed metathesis count from this entry.

Mechanism scope. Initial-retroflex lookalike; no established earlier reversed order.

Scholarly references. DEDR 2988; compare DEDR2698 and K61 p.54 §1.127 alternative derivations (prior verified reading)

Independent input evidence. Tamil taŋku/takku, Malayalam taŋŋuka/takkuka, Kannada taŋgu/dakku and central tak independently establish initial t and a velar/nasal medial cluster. No postvocalic apical is reconstructed.

Direction. Initial t/d/ḍ precedes a in all relevant cognates. Telugu ḍakku does not show reversal of an independently reconstructible *aḍ input.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tak-k > takku/dakku/ḍakku involves initial voicing/retroflexion or lexical variant association; *taŋ-k > taŋgu/tagg involves nasal/velar developments. These are distinct from initial vowel/apical displacement.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A false-positive control for searching Telugu initial ḍ. K61 p.53 §1.126 proposes hyperstandard ḍ for d in ḍakku; this is an alternative to metathesis, not a demonstrated ancient sound law. The same discussion finds no evidence for an assumed lost nasal source. Uncertainty about this consonant is not positive metathesis evidence. Related takku/takkin(a) morphology and cognates support the original t-initial analysis.

Mechanism scope. Initial voicing/retroflexion, not metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR 3014; K61 p.53 §1.126 (prior verified reading)

Independent input evidence. Parji terip/terit independently gives full apical order; Telugu tari/tarucu/tarcu provides an internal full/consonantal series.

Direction. Full Parji and Telugu forms favor tar-c before traccu; a bare protoform alone contributes no extra evidence.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tar-c > *tra-c > traccu with strengthening is plausible; tarucu could be a fuller ancestor or a separately vocalized derivative. Parji labial p differs from Telugu palatal c.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A good directional comparison with uncertain exact suffix-vowel chronology. Churning milk and fire-drilling can share rotary motion, but their semantic extension does not itself explain which formation changed. Retained tarcu shows that a consonantal stem is not sufficient for obligatory movement.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Direction. Gondi taṛm favors earlier t-a-apical before Telugu trampi. Kui dlāva has a different labial vowel-bearing derivative and an explicitly proposed alternative aẓal etymology.

Derivation and relative chronology. *taẓ-m-p > *tẓa-mp > trampi, then possible r loss > tampi. Tamil taṇal/Kannada taṇalu involve medial nasalization/assimilation, not initial reversal. Kui *taẓ-av > dlāv is conditional on the root assignment.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The database Kui aṛ̆al, *c and *t are editorial comparison fragments, not lexical attestations. Kui alternative276 must not be counted twice; its outcome stays A here. Telugu tanuku requires a different nasal/velar history.

Independent input evidence. Tamil taṛ̆ai and Malayalam taṛ̆a/taṛ̆ekka plus Kannada taṛ̆e establish medial apical order; vowel alternants and strong extensions are independent of Brahui.

Direction. Full southern stems and Kui dalga favor earlier t-V-apical versus Brahui trikking/trikk. The exact Brahui suffix vowel is not independently recovered.

Derivation and relative chronology. *taẓ-V-kk > *tẓV-kk > trikk is a plausible displacement-family sequence, with apical merger to r. If V2 was i, simple loss of V1 would also yield trik-; if low a, additional vowel change is needed. The available data do not decide.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. PSS83 p.245 includes this among examples compatible with aphaeresis. Do not invent a high-i formative solely to derive the observed i. Brahui trikking is homophonous with d3244 wither but the two comparative roots and meanings remain separate pending evidence for a semantic bridge.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Gondi taṛānā/tark and Kuvi taṛj independently retain full order; Kuvi taṛj:tṛaj gives a close internal formation contrast. Other branches have long tāṛ grades.

Direction. The close Kuvi pair and full Gondi root favor t-V-apical before Telugu travvu; r-only eastern forms can lose the first cluster consonant.

Derivation and relative chronology. *taẓ-v > *tẓav > travvu > tavvu with labial strengthening and later r loss; Kuvi taṛj > tṛaj has the same directional relation with a palatal suffix. Konda ṟeb/Kuvi ṛev/Pengo ṛav can follow C1 loss, but e/o variants require distinct vowel histories.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A shared regional displacement pattern is plausible; exact v/b/j formation and long/short chronology are not one uniform word history. Kolami/Naikri tavv may reflect Telugu contact or internal apical loss; neither is independently demonstrated.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil short taṟi and long tāṟṟu/tāttu, Tulu sāruni and Telugu tālucu establish full t/s-a-apical order with independent quantity alternants. Newly reported Brahui tāring preserves that order.

Direction. Brahui tāring and southern full roots favor derivation of dranzing/drãzing within the same sift family; they do not independently attest the exact proposed short *tarañc stem.

Derivation and relative chronology. Emeneau proposes *tarañc- > *trañc- > dranz-/drāz-, with displacement-family contraction or aphaeresis, initial voicing and nasal/affricate changes. The long retained tāring is a different formation/grade, not necessarily the immediate input to dranz-.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Emeneau 1997 p.445 §12 removes the older query and rejects placement under d3402 *tūr as less economical. The original database drãzing spelling is preserved, not silently changed into drāzing. The -añc vowel is reconstructed, not independently supported by Tamil taṟi, so this does not prove a low-V2 law. Pengo dalŋgi ki has a different cluster/formative. Do not count the two Brahui derivatives as two roots.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil tiraŋku/tirakku/tirai and Malayalam tira independently establish i-r-a order. Kannada tere, Kodagu tere and Telugu tera agree with full order after vowel developments.

Direction. Brahui trikking retains i after r. Simple deletion of first i from independently supported *tirakk would give trakk, making this a stronger vowel-preservation argument than same-vowel cases.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tir-a-kk > *tri-a-kk > trikk is a possible literal-exchange plus vowel-loss derivation. Assimilation of the two vowels followed by loss of the first also remains possible; the comparison establishes displacement-family history more securely than its phonetic implementation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. PSS83 p.245 identifies wither and drop as stronger metathesis cases. The precise relation of nasal tiraŋku, strong tirakku and nominal tirai must remain morphological. Brahui trikking sprout d3119 is not counted as the same root solely on homophony.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes
