Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil tiri/tiruku/tiruppu/tirukku and Kannada tiri/tirugu independently establish high-vowel root and distinct singleton velar, geminate labial and geminate velar formations. Kannada tiragu/tirapa and Kodagu teraŋg additionally attest low-a formations; no one V2 fits all derivatives.

Direction. Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Gondi, Konda and central retained forms agree on t-i-r before Telugu tr-. Telugu itself contrasts retained tirugu and displaced trippu/trikku. The grammatical contrast is independently supported by Tamil intransitive and causative formations.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tir-upp > *tir-pp > *tri-pp > trippu; *tir-ukk > *tir-kk > *tri-kk > trikku, with equal-vowel syncope/reassociation not requiring a literal audible vowel swap. *tir-uk > tirugu retains order. Kui trēba and Kuvi rēnai involve a different formative and initial t loss in the latter; its exact low-a/ high-i input must not be inferred solely from ē. Manda trīmba matches a nasal formation with long quantity.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A strong independently formed Telugu contrast: singleton-velar turn is retained while geminate causative/twist forms displace. This is evidence for morphological/cluster conditioning within a family, not a universal rule until other geminate and singleton inputs are tested. Trimmaṭa/trimmaru wandering need exact derivational reconstruction and are flagged less certain than trippu. Central tipp may result directly from medial r-p assimilation; Telugu tipiri may be analogical or metathetically restructured but does not prove initial tr loss. Badaga Tirikōṇa is a proper name and should not be an extra inherited turn witness.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3246; K03 Rule 21; PSS83 p.229 nonautomatic application

d3259 — open

d3259: open

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd3259
Comparative input*ti/eṯ-a; velar, labial and palatal extensions
Initial consonantt
V1 quality / quantityi/e / short
C2 identity / structureṟ / singleton
Following vowela
Root/formation shapeCVC-a / CVC-a-C
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceLow-a root independently attested; local labial/palatal extensions and input grades separate.
Input classshort-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil tiṟa, Kannada teṟa/teṟe and Malayalam tuṟakka independently establish a low-a formative and t-V-apical order. Telugu teṟacu/teṟa retains that independently supported environment.

Direction. Full southern forms and Konda Gūṛi teṟe support t-V-apical before Konda ṟe. Initial loss alone from teṟa would give ṟa, so the mid vowel in ṟē/jē requires prior vowel interaction or a different independently established formation.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *teṯ-a > *tṟē > ṟē gives Konda; later apical change gives Pengo/Manda jē and Kuvi de. Kui dāpa adds low outcome (contraction then lowering or lowering then contraction). Telugu teṟacu retains initial order, and suffix cu requires its own historical morphology.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A clear low-a retained Telugu family versus broader eastern displacement. Gondi rehānā may show first-member loss, but its own suffix/vowel and donor history remain uncertain. Tulu jappuni/depp could involve medial assimilation plus initial t>j/d, not necessarily the same metathesis; Kurux/Malto tisg likewise preserves the first vowel despite loss/change of apical. Toda key tɨrp is explicitly alternatively compared with turn d3246 or Tamil borrowing and cannot be treated as an independent ordinary open reflex.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 p.160 example 94; K80 pp.497–499 item 10; DEDR 3259

Independent input evidence. Tamil tuṇi, Kannada tuṇuku and Telugu tuniya independently establish a nasal root; no rhotic is required by this core comparison.

Direction. Telugu truŋgu/truncu could have secondary r in nasal formations, or belong to3339 tura. The dictionary explicitly preserves that alternative.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tuṇ-i-C > tuniy/tunc by nasal-place and suffixal changes is nonmetathetic. A rhotic-root derivation of truŋgu/truncu belongs to the competing analysis, not a demonstrated ṇ>r metathesis here.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The long beam *tūṇ does not replace short cut-root quantity. Assign contested Telugu forms A under both entries; collapse for sensitivity if desired, but no double D vote. Kuvi tũrhali may have a secondary rhotic and remains uncertain.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil tura/turuvu, Kannada turi and Tulu turiyuni independently support full r order. The source head long **tūr does not erase these short forms.

Direction. Full southern and northern comparisons favor eastern tr-; Telugu disputed cut/break forms also occur under3305 tuṇi.

Derivation and relative chronology. Consonantal *tur-k > truk gives Konda tṟuk and Kui trupka after a separate k+p reversal. Kui trunga/trūva have distinct nasal/labial quantity histories. Telugu tuṟumu retains the full root; truŋgu/truncu remain alternative-cognacy cases.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not assign the same Telugu forms as secure D in two roots. Kui tuspa may follow r loss or direct simplification, not certain shared chronology. Long Kurux tūrnā is a regional grade, not evidence all short derivatives are secondary.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil tura/turattu, Malayalam turattuka and Parji turkip support full t-V-r independently of Telugu trō-.

Direction. The full southern/central order favors innovation of trōyu/trōcu/trōlu and Kui/Kuvi trō-.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *tor-a-y/c/l > trōy/c/l, with low-a root supported but exact suffixes distinct. *tor-b > trobb/drobb gives a short voiced-geminate derivative; dobbu can be later r loss or imported/assimilated form. Gondi ro- can lose C1 after a cluster.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kannada/Tulu dobbu and Naikri ḍʰobb make early contact plausible for the voiced-geminate subformation, not proven for every pushing word. The various Telugu suffixes and meanings remain one family, with a separate quantity test for each.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3340; current comparative cluster panel; K61 pp.65–66 probable early Kannada-loan class

Eligibility / caveatbrahui-displacement-comparison

Independent input evidence. Kurux tuṛᵘxnā and related forms supply a full t-u-r sequence independently of Brahui trukking.

Direction. The geographically separated Kurux full stem versus Brahui trukking favors reduction/displacement in Brahui. Superscript u in Kurux transcription must not automatically be treated as a full independent suffix vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tur-(u)-k > *tru-k > trukk is the comparison. Literal u/r exchange and loss of initial u from a two-u stem cannot be distinguished without establishing the status of the Kurux superscript vowel and the pre-Brahui stem.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. PSS83 p.245 lists this among cases compatible with aphaeresis. Only two northern branches attest the reviewed family; no Telugu denominator vote arises from their presence.

Independent input evidence. Tamil tuḷḷu, Malayalam tuḷḷuka, Kannada tuḷḷu, Kodagu tuḷḷ and Tulu tuḷḷuni independently establish a geminate lateral with no additional rhotic.

Direction. The widespread southern form and Telugu tuḷḷu favor earlier t-u-ḷḷ. Telugu truḷḷu retains that whole sequence and adds r, so ordinary transposition cannot derive it without an extra unsupported ancestral rhotic.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tuḷḷ-u > tuḷḷu; secondary literary r gives truḷḷu and its derivatives. K61 p.131 n.80 proposes hyperstandardization on the model of archaic Cr forms. This is a source proposal with strong segment-count evidence for addition, less direct evidence for its social mechanism.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A central negative control: initial tr does not guarantee metathesis. It is inappropriate to reconstruct **tur-uḷḷ solely from the Telugu outcome. Gondi tul could have simplified gemination or be related through contact; neither supplies the missing r. K61 citation was visually checked in the prior investigation; this run’s attempt to reopen p.131 reached the authorized preview limit and did not independently reverify the page.

Mechanism scope. Secondary r; hyperstandardization plausible, not metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR 3364; K61 p.131 n.80 (prior run page verification, reopened preview unavailable)

Independent input evidence. Tamil tuṟu/tuṟumu/tuṟumpu and strong tuṟṟu, Malayalam tuṟuka and Kannada tuṟugu/tuṟagu independently establish u before an apical and several following formations.

Direction. Full southern and central stems support derivation of Brahui trujjing from a fuller t-u-apical stem; the affricate formative does not have an exact independently matched full stem here.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tuṯ/ṟ-u-C > *tṯ/ṟu-C > trujj- is a displacement-family hypothesis; same-u aphaeresis remains possible. Telugu tuṟugu/turugu and tuṟumu/turumu retain order. Strong tukku/tuttu and eastern cuc/tuc can arise by medial assimilation and are not automatic evidence for concealed initial metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. PSS83 p.245 includes this among aphaeresis-compatible examples. ṯ versus ṟ and affricate development require independent correspondence reconstruction; assigning a unique apical from the outcome would overstate the data. Strong and weak formations are kept in one root family with mixed input structure.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR3367; PSS83 pp.244–245

Direction. Telugu truppuḍu has an initial r and final ḍ; simple adjacent V-r exchange from the closest Kannada form does not preserve the segment inventory.

Derivation and relative chronology. A longer-distance apical shift plus final suffix remodeling is possible, as is secondary r added to a tuppuḍu-type derivative. Gondi tōṛ offers an apical root but not the complete pp-ḍ formation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not suppress final ḍ or silently move the sole Kannada ẓ across pp while retaining a replacement. Direction. The full order is shared across southern, Gondi and eastern stems; no initial cluster requires exchange.

Derivation and relative chronology. Southern apical strong/weak alternants and eastern ṭūṭ have apical/initial stop assimilation or correspondence changes while ū stays between the consonants. Tulu tūpu can reflect medial cluster assimilation/loss. Telugu compound tūru-pettu > tūrpettu shows medial syncope.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Emeneau 1997 explicitly rejects deriving Brahui dranz- here; a cross-reference is not a Brahui attestation. Kolami tūrpet may be a Telugu compound loan but the source does not decide it. Badaga tūravare/purāvare bean names are not secure winnow cognates. The source query comparing Sanskrit śūrpa is not a settled borrowing direction.

Independent input evidence. Southern tēk/tēg and Gondi/Konda/Kolami dērk establish distinct velar versus rhotic-velar formations. The regional r is independently attested, but its origin is not resolved by this set.

Direction. Kuvi/Pengo dreb can plausibly continue regional der-b with reordering; Telugu trēnc needs a different nasal-palatal suffix. The southern root does not supply a simple inherited r.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional *der-b > dreb is plausible, while *tēr-nc > trēnc remains conditional on the regional r formation and suffix. Kui tēk-p > tēpka is separate velar-labial reversal without initial apical displacement.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Belching is expressive vocabulary with long/short and dental/rhotic variants. Do not reconstruct *ter-aŋ simply to obtain Telugu ē. Exact cognacy of the r-bearing subseries and original suffixes is the unresolved problem, not a general exceptionless metathesis.

Eligibility / caveatnorthern-medial-reduction-comparison

Independent input evidence. Malayalam tokku and Kurux tolᵒkʰ/tolokʰ are the complete attested database comparison. The southern form lacks l, so the immediate northern sequence is more secure than a common reconstructed lateral root.

Direction. Kurux directly supports t-o-l order, and external Kunha tolkhō preserves that same initial sequence. Moving a medial vowel to a final position is not the initial sonorant displacement found in Telugu.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional tolokʰ > *tolkʰ > tolkhō is possible through medial syncope and final vowel morphology/epenthesis; direct o/kʰ exchange plus lengthening is another description. Malayalam tokku could reflect lk assimilation if cognacy is valid, but no independent full southern tolok formation confirms that history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The dictionary itself queries the reconstructed *Tok root. Do not infer metathesis from a reconstructed l that only the northern branch has. Kunha source pairs an armpit term with Kurux side/flank; semantic continuity is plausible but exact polysemy needs elicitation. Full older forms, suffixal paradigms and additional southern cognates would resolve the alternatives.

Mechanism scope. Medial reduction/final-vowel alternation; literal exchange not demonstrated.

Scholarly references. DEDR3520, DEDS550; Kujur and Dash2025 p.119

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam tōl alongside tokku, Malayalam tukal, Kannada togal/toval and Tulu tugal independently motivate velar-bearing *tok-al and contracted long *tōl. Telugu tōlu is already a long-root control at the apical-metathesis stage, not an arbitrary long outcome.

Direction. Full togal/tugal retains k before a final l; lenition k>g/v and loss plus vowel contraction gives tōl without moving l. The separate tokka/tokku has no apical target.

Derivation and relative chronology. *tok-al > togal/toval > tōl is the comparative contraction analysis. *tōl > tōlu/ṭōḍu retains initial vowel/apical order; Toda tvɨ̄s̱ involves vowel breaking and final lateral fricativization. No l is promoted into the onset.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This distinguishes vowel contraction from metathesis and provides a long/free-root control across many branches. Gondi tolka and central compounds/plurals do not change the inherited long-root analysis without further evidence. Badaga dai wet is explicitly alternatively linked to d3555 and not skin evidence; Nihali ṭōl is marked borrowed and lies outside Dravidian rates. Short toli peeling may reflect another formation/grade, not a compulsory pre-metathesis shortening of every skin noun.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3559; K03 *tok-al/*tōl reconstruction; PSS83 long/free-root condition

d3754: moon, month, moonlight

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd3754
Comparative input*nel-a-nc/-ncc; *nel-V
Initial consonantn
V1 quality / quantitye/i / short
C2 identity / structurel / singleton
Following vowela

Input classshort-C-initial-other-apical

Input confidencehigh for order and formative family

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Kodagu nelaci, Gondi nelenj/nalenj and Parji neliñ independently support n-V-l followed by a palatal/nasal formation. Tamil nilā/nilavu and Malayalam nilā are linked through final *-ac > -ah > ā in K03, independently distinguishing later final ā from the first-syllable quantity.

Direction. Multiple branches establish n-V-l before eastern lēnj. Gondi/Konda retain full and l-initial variants; medial nasal/palatal material survives and supports cognacy beyond the initial resemblance.

Derivation and relative chronology. *nel-anc > *nlēnc > lēnj with initial nasal loss gives the standard eastern chain; Kui lēnj > lānj > ḍānju adds lowering and lateral-to-stop change. Gondi lelenj/lalenj may instead assimilate initial n to l before reduction, so precise segment exchange versus assimilation plus contraction is not uniquely fixed. Telugu nela retains original order. Thiyya Malayalam nilāvu > lāvu is simple initial-syllable loss, retaining the second vowel.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Telugu nonapplication accords with exclusion of post-C l from its narrow class. Kui ā versus Kuvi/Pengo/Manda ē supports language-specific lowering after, or during, contraction rather than one inherited identical vowel outcome. The exact extinct *nl cluster is reconstructed, not directly observed here. Gondi n/l assimilation supplies a concrete competing pathway, to be tested with dialect chronology and stress. Moon and month do not add independent roots.

Mechanism scope. Eastern displacement family; initial assimilation plus contraction remains an alternative in some Gondi forms.

Scholarly references. K03 pp.122–123 n.5(5), pp.159–160 Rule 21; DEDR 3754; K80 lowering examples

d3821 — green, fresh, moist; moss

d3821: green, fresh, moist; moss

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd3821
Comparative input*pac/pas; *pas-ir/ar extensions
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantitya / short
C2 identity / structurec/s / singleton
Following voweli/a/unknown
Root/formation shapeCVC / CVC-V-r
Grammatical categoryadjective/noun
Boundary evidenceExact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidenceComparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes

Eligibility / caveatalternative-cognacy-nonadjacent-process

Independent input evidence. Tamil pacu/paccai/pāci and Kannada pasu/pasir support a palatal/sibilant root with optional later r. Telugu pasaru is a full r-bearing extension, not a simple CVr base.

Direction. Telugu prā̃ci could involve longer-distance redistribution from a pasir-type formation, secondary r in pā̃ci, or the alternative stale4057; immediate apical exchange is not established.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *pas-ir > *prs... would require additional segment/vowel restructuring; no complete supported derivation follows. pāci may inherit a contracted sibilant root without any r.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not treat moss and green-gram protohead as the same exact noun input. The DEDR alternative4057 remains unresolved. Borrowed/compound green forms are not independent root evidence; Manda aphaeresis and Kuvi pāci have separate source notes.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3821; current comparative cluster panel

d3949 — spread, crawl, bed, expanse

d3949: spread, crawl, bed, expanse

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd3949
Comparative input*par-a; *par-a-k(k), *par-a-pp, *par-u-w; long *pār
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantitya / short and independent long grade
C2 identity / structurer/ṟ / singleton
Following vowela/u
Root/formation shapeCVC-a-K / CVC-a-PP / CVC-u-w / CVVC
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceLow-a velar, labial and high-u forms remain distinct; semantic classes alone cannot force regularity.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for broad formations; medium for exact velar quantity
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil para/parakku/parappu, Malayalam parakka/parattuka and Kannada pare/parapu independently support low-a formations. Tamil/Malayalam pār independently supports a long grade, and Telugu high-u paruvu is a distinct derivative.

Direction. Many branches establish p-a-r before Telugu prāku and Kui pr-. Telugu itself retains para-/paṟa- formations, so the head *para cannot be assigned one automatic outcome.

Derivation and relative chronology. *par-a-k > *prā-k > prāku, then r loss in pākul-āḍu, is the displaced crawl pathway; Tamil parakku supplies a matched velar formation but original gemination versus later simplification needs separate assessment. Telugu paracu/parapu/paragu retains order in other low-a formations. Kui prahpa/brāḍa and Kuvi pressali have distinct causative/voice extensions and vowel histories.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a genuine within-family lexical/morphological residual: low-a alone does not determine Telugu application, and the exact velar contrast cannot be repaired simply by assigning all crawl meanings to an invented class. Konda rēs metal plating may involve displaced *prēs with first-member loss, but e versus independently a requires another grade or contact and remains uncertain. Southern pammu/habbu/pabb and Gadaba pamp permit medial assimilation; do not invent hidden pr. Badaga initial p/h loss leaves r after a and is not metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3949; K03 *par-a reconstruction; K61 immediate-antecedent principle

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam parutti independently supplies a before r and high u before tt. Kannada/Tulu parti and Gondi part support a syncopated medial cluster.

Direction. Full and syncopated comparanda support par- as earlier than Telugu pra-. Telugu pratti and patti document the cluster and its rhotic-free outcome in the same language.

Derivation and relative chronology. *par-utti > *par-tti > *pra-tti > pratti > patti. The derivative already has tt; metathesis need not create it anew. Kannada parti > patti is also possible through direct medial r assimilation, without a pra stage.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Cotton vocabulary can travel, and Kuvi Sunkarametta pratti may be a Telugu loan; other Kuvi/Kui forms retain part-. Neither shared crop semantics nor a matching modern patti establishes inheritance. Kannada paẓti has an additional apical correspondence and should not override the robust r series. Long Tamil pāram is a separate formation, not the exact input to Telugu short a.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Eligibility / caveatvowel-input-uncertain

Independent input evidence. Gondi pere/perek/paṛem, Konda per/peru and central perku/peruk independently establish p-V-r. Tamil parukkai/poruku supplies a possible related grain formation but does not settle the exact vowel of the bare eastern rice root.

Direction. Several branches favor p-V-r before Telugu prālu, Kui prāu/prāma and Pengo/Manda preyi. The earlier order is clearer than the original V1/V2 qualities.

Derivation and relative chronology. A candidate *par-a > prā, with Telugu plural lu, gives prālu; a candidate *per-a > prē followed by eastern lowering gives Kui prāu. These are competing input assignments, not independently demonstrated steps for each language. Kui compound kōruvrau > kōruvau loses r after p>v in the compound, providing a directly attested local simplification pair.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The shared rice semantics and regional distribution permit inheritance or old agricultural borrowing. Telugu ā should not be used to reconstruct a-a while Kui ā is used to infer earlier e-a without independent evidence. Exact V2 and whether Telugu lu is synchronically/plausibly plural need historical lexical evidence. Gondi kuṭkī is an explanatory species name, not a cognate. Keep this case outside strict vowel-conditioning counts, while retaining secure order comparison.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3982; K80 rice/lowering comparison

d3986 — tooth; toothstick compounds

d3986: tooth; toothstick compounds

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd3986
Comparative input*pal; *pal#kar tooth-stick
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantitya / short
C2 identity / structurel / singleton
Following vowelzero
Root/formation shapeCVC free root / CVC#CVC

Boundary evidenceBare monosyllabic noun established across branches; added final vowel and toothstick compounding are independent of outcome.
Input classshort-C-initial-other-apical

Eligibility / caveatfree-root-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil pal, Malayalam pal, Kota pal, Gondi pal and Central Dravidian pal/pel independently establish a short closed free root, with no original second root vowel. Final u in some languages is not evidence for a formative *-u.

Direction. Agreement across southern, south-central, central and northern branches supports p-a-l. The toothstick compounds independently contain the second member kar/kaṟ wood (DEDR1389), so their internal liquid order must be examined separately.

Derivation and relative chronology. *pal > Telugu palu/pallu and eastern pal/palu retains order. Telugu plural paṇḍlu and singular pannu are a morphological/cluster problem: DEDR explicitly calls pannu a back-formation. Toda pas̱ is lateral fricativization, Tulu paru a rhotic correspondence. Gondi palkār > parkal and Parji perkal plausibly reverse the two compound liquids, without placing a lateral before the first vowel.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This supports a free-root restriction more directly than choosing only verbs with positive outcomes. The Telugu parser puts paṇḍlu/pannu in gloss text; those forms are source claims, not independent parsed lexical rows. Kuvi kaṟ/kar/kaṟal are pieces of an editorial cross-reference to1389, not additional tooth reflexes. The unrelated *pāl milk head is excluded. Compound liquid reversal could be shared or borrowed between neighboring Gondi/Parji; the dialect distribution alone does not date it.

Mechanism scope. Retention of initial order; compound liquid reversal tracked separately.

Scholarly references. DEDR3986 and1389; PSS83 p.229 free-root control (oldDED3288)

d3999: old, worn, stale

PropertyAnnotation

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada paẓa and Gondi paṛana independently establish low-a full input; Gondi paṛna also supplies a syncopated control.

Direction. Full paẓ-a favors Telugu prā̃ta and eastern prān/pṛāk; Kuvi pṇā has a secondary nasal next to initial p.

Derivation and relative chronology. *paẓ-ant > *pẓānt > prā̃ta > pā̃ta/pāta; *paẓ-an > prān in Pengo/Manda. Kuvi prāi > pṇāi may assimilate the promoted liquid to a nasal, but reverse order of assimilation/movement is also possible.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Suffix nt versus n versus k matters; do not count old-person and old-object derivatives separately. Konda pāta cloth is explicitly Telugu borrowing while paṛay retains native full order. Nasal loss and shortening/denasalization are later changes, not the original displacement.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 3999; current comparative cluster panel

Direction. Full southern approximant favors initial pr in Telugu prayi/prabbu, with separate formative histories.

Kota apṛ/ipṛ are explicitly onomatopoeic scolding elements, not automatic evidence of inherited initial apical displacement in that language. d4005: rib, side, armpit

PropertyAnnotation

Input confidencehigh

Eligibility / caveatcore-contact-convergence

Independent input evidence. Kannada paẓke, Konda paṛka and Kuvi paṛka independently support a medial approximant plus velar extension; Tamil paẓu supplies a shorter rib root.

Direction. The independent velar formations support pa-apical-k as earlier order. Kuvi paṛka/pṛaka demonstrates actual order variation, while Telugu prakka has promoted r and a strengthened velar.

Derivation and relative chronology. *paẓ-k > *pẓak(k) > prakka in Telugu; strengthening may precede or follow displacement. Kuvi paṛka > pṛaka is a separate local exchange without Telugu gemination. Later Telugu r-loss would produce pakka, but that modern form is not supplied as a standalone reflex in this corpus group.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. DEDR explicitly notes convergence with Middle Indo-Aryan pakkha, especially in Telugu. Thus a pure inherited account of every pakka/prakka token would be unjustified: inherited metathesis, borrowing and analogical mixing may all contribute. Exact corpus prakka retains the apical, but the formation’s loan history still needs independent textual evidence. Do not treat Tamil paẓu as proof of a vocalic suffix in the velar derivative.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 4005 and explicit DBIA 233a convergence note; Hume 2004 p.225

Independent input evidence. Tamil paṉṟi, Kannada/Kodagu/Telugu pandi, Konda panṟi and Pengo/Manda panji independently establish a nasal-apical cluster, not a singleton r.

Direction. The cross-branch nasal-plus-apical correspondences favor original p-a-nṯ order. Gondi paddi and Malayalam panni show assimilation of different parts of that cluster.

Derivation and relative chronology. *panṯi > pandi/panṟi retains cluster order; assimilation gives panni/paddi, and palatal developments give panji/pañji and paji. Later nasal loss or cluster simplification does not establish that an earlier singleton was eligible for metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A strong nasal-cluster control. The several Gondi records repeat dialect/source evidence, not independent roots. Badaga handi/andi shows p>h>zero, not apical transfer. Kui paji looks like a simple intervocalic consonant synchronically, but comparative evidence independently reconstructs the blocking cluster. The exact segmentation pan-ṯ versus lexical panṯ remains open and is not needed for the cluster classification.

Mechanism scope. Cluster assimilation/palatalization, not metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR4039; PSS83 p.229 oldDED3326

Independent input evidence. Tamil pirampu and Malayalam perampu independently establish full r order and low-a labial extension.

Direction. Agreement of full southern forms favors a cluster innovation in Telugu. Kannada prabbali may share regional transmission, not necessarily inherited metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Rattan names may travel with the object. Kannada prabbali cannot alone prove a Kannada sound law; its vowel, suffix and gemination pattern require source history. Long and short Telugu derivatives count as one family.

Independent input evidence. Tamil puri/piri, Malayalam puriyuka/piriyuka, Kannada puri and Kodagu piri independently establish a full apical root with high i formative; the root vowel varies independently.

Direction. Kui priu/prīpa have r before the vowel while Brahui pirɣẖing retains it after i. The latter is the explicit retention exception to the traditional Brahui closed-stem generalization.

Derivation and relative chronology. Kui *pir/pur-i-p > *pri-i-p > prīp is a possible contraction; priu has separate final morphology. Brahui *pir-k > pirɣ preserves the medial cluster, contrasting with the other t/p-initial Brahui cases. Telugu piri/puri and compounds retain full order.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. PSS83 p.245 acknowledges the Brahui exception despite a following consonant. It cannot be excluded from the class simply because it did not change. Root-vowel variation and different velar/labial formations may matter, but no demonstrated deterministic blocker is available. Winfield 1928 p.10 priu:prīnga plural morphology corroborates the Kui family without adding an independent root.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR4177; PSS83 pp.244–245; Winfield1928 p.10

Eligibility / caveatbrahui-displacement-comparison

Independent input evidence. Tamil piṛ̆i and Malayalam piṛ̆iyuka, Kannada piṛ̆i and Konda piṛs establish singleton piẓ order independently; piṇṭi/piṇḍu oilcake and squeeze formations separately establish nasal-stop derivatives.

Direction. Kui pṛihpa and Brahui princing have the apical before the vowel, whereas Brahui piṛ̆ẖing/bīṛing and Telugu piḍucu retain the full sequence. Nasal derivatives do not prove a primary nasal input for the displaced cluster.

Derivation and relative chronology. *piẓ-i-C > *pẓi-C > pri-C is the displacement-family comparison, with same-vowel contraction or aphaeresis underdetermined. Kui vṛīsa/bṛīc add initial voicing/frication and quantity; Kuvi ṛīsk could lose initial labial after a cluster, while vīskinai could lose the apical by another route. Telugu piṇḍu/piṇḍi involve medial assimilation, not initial reversal.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The red database piṇṭ head does not replace the independently supported singleton input of piẓi. Brahui bīṛing milk is a distinct long formation. Emeneau 1997 p.443 §7 prefers d4135 for pisfing; it is not counted here. DEDR frontmatter says 4135/4183 were repartitioned on phonological grounds, so their cognacy assignments are hypotheses to test, not independent confirmation of an exceptionless sound rule. Exact Brahui piṛ̆ẖ transcription still merits original-page checking.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR4183; DEDR frontmatter phonological repartition note; PSS83 pp.244–245; Emeneau1997 p.443 §7

Eligibility / caveatinput-cognacy-contested

Independent input evidence. Tamil piḷ/piḷa, Malayalam piḷakka/piḷaruka and Kannada piḷigu support a lateral root, with independently distinct i/a formations. Telugu prēlu has both r and l, not a simple one-liquid reflex. K61 instead compares a rhotic separate root in entry 898 and reconstructs *pir-al for prēlu.

Direction. Southern lateral forms establish p-V-ḷ for the DEDR group and support Kui pl-. They do not alone establish the two-liquid input required by Telugu prēlu. Gondi rhotics cannot settle r versus ḷ because ḷ has rhotic reflexes there independently.

Derivation and relative chronology. For the securely comparable eastern hatch stems, *piḷ-i/zero > plī/plin gives Kui plīva/pling(a), with stem-specific length and nasal morphology. Telugu alternatives: (1) K61 *pir-al > *per-al > prēlu > pēlu; (2) independently long/lengthened lateral pēlu with secondary literary r; (3) a two-liquid formation related to Malayalam piḷar- with a separate liquid-order change. None is established merely by fitting the modern form.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep Telugu uncertain, not an automatic exception to the narrow r/ṟ/ẓ restriction or a confirmed lateral metathesis. K61 p.437 entry 859 treats pēlu separately and allows derivation from prēlu; p.445 entry 901 supplies *per-al. Those page images were verified in the prior investigation, not reverified after this run hit preview limits. Kolami pēl could be independently lengthened or borrowed. Gadaba pēlsap is explicitly a Telugu loan. Homophonous prattle d4430 must remain distinct absent evidence of analogical transfer.

Mechanism scope. Eastern lateral displacement secure; Telugu root choice and possible secondary r unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR 4194; K61 p.437 entry 859, p.445 entry 901 and comparison entry 898 (prior verified reading)

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam puẓu, Kannada puẓu, Konda piṛvu and Telugu puruvu/purvu independently support full order and both vowel-bearing and consonantal branches.

Direction. Te purvu:pruvvu and Kui source piṛu:pṛiu provide direct directional comparisons; multiple full branches rule out assuming Telugu clusters ancestral.

Derivation and relative chronology. *puẓ-v > pruvvu after cluster reordering/strengthening; alternative *puẓ-uv > *pẓuuv with later shortening cannot be excluded. Kui piṛu > pṛiu > pṛīu provides a high-vowel displacement/coalescence comparison; Kuvi pliguli includes lateral outcome and separate morphology.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Short Telugu pruvvu is not proof of original zero V2 because puruvu exists. puccu/puppi can be internal assimilation or later r loss; classify A. Brahui pū and Kota pū can lose the apical without metathesis. Toda u· is explicitly a Badaga loan.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

d4335: anthill

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4335
Comparative input*puṯṯ / *punṯṯ-V; regional *puṭṭ
Initial consonantp

Eligibility / caveatroot-cluster-control

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam puṟṟu, Kannada puttu and Telugu puṭṭa support a strong apical cluster; Tulu puñca and Koraga huñca/huntu motivate an additional nasal reconstruction. Both alternatives are nonsingleton inputs.

Direction. Southern and central double-apical reflexes with nasal evidence establish original p-u-cluster order; eastern puci/pusi need not derive from a primitive singleton c.

Derivation and relative chronology. *pu(n)ṯṯV > puttu/puṭṭa and nasal/palatal puñca, with eastern pucci/puci/pusi after cluster simplification. Initial p>h>zero gives Kannada hutta/utta and Koraga huntu, independent of metathesis. Kuvi pūci may reflect local compensatory length from a strong cluster; no prior pr/pl onset is needed.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Geminate versus nasal-plus-geminate reconstruction is unresolved but does not affect exclusion from the singleton class. The database attaches a Kurumba pitti form to Malayalam because of an embedded heading; do not count it as a Malayalam outcome. Toda vɨt-xuḏy is independently explained as rising+pit in its newer dictionary, weakening its membership in this root and requiring an ambiguous code. North/central comparisons have possible lexical diffusion but no evidence of initial reversal. PSS old number was initially misread3556/3566; DEDR4335 is the verified mapping.

Mechanism scope. Cluster changes and uncertain Toda cognacy, no initial displacement.

Scholarly references. DEDR4335; K03 p.100 example16; PSS83 p.229

d4410 — name, name someone

d4410: name, name someone

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4410
Comparative input*pin-cc-Vr > *pic-ar / *pec-ar; regional pidir/peder
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantityi/e/ē / long produced by contraction in relevant southern forms
C2 identity / structurec/d with final r / singleton
Following vowela/i
Root/formation shapeCVC-a-r / CVVC
Grammatical categorynoun/verb
Boundary evidenceFinal r is an extension after earlier c/d; do not misread pēr as primitive short CVr.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for contraction family; low for eastern dental-initial history
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcontraction-and-secondary-apical-control

Independent input evidence. Kannada pesar, Tamil peyar, Tulu pudar, central pidir and northern pinj/pin independently support a medial palatal/dental plus a later final rhotic formation. K03 reconstructs *pic-ar and deeper *pin-cc-Vr; long pēr results from loss/contraction, not an originally short p-e-r root.

Direction. Southern pes-ar > pey-ar > pēr preserves final r while losing the medial consonant. Telugu pēru fits this contraction without moving r. Konda/Kuvi dōr and Pengo tōr promote or retain a dental-looking segment but differ in both onset and vowel; they are not straightforward r-metathesis.

Derivation and relative chronology. *pec-ar > *pey-ar > pēr gives Telugu and southern long forms. For eastern dōr/tōr, possible *peder > *pdēr > dēr with initial p loss would require secondary dental-cluster formation plus unexplained o; alternative medial assimilation or regional lexical replacement remains open. Do not present that schematic route as an attested intermediate.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A useful contraction control and possible different secondary-apical process. K03 p.104 explicitly treats Kolami/Naikri pēr as Telugu loans. Their forms therefore cannot independently reconstruct early long quantity. Badaga pēru may similarly involve southern contact, while hesaru provides its fuller comparison. The northern naming verb lacks the final rhotic extension and is not a retained instance of the same CVr input.

Mechanism scope. Medial consonant loss and contraction; eastern dental-initial variants unresolved.

Scholarly references. K03 p.104 example31 and discussion; DEDR 4410

d4411 — grow, increase, big; elder kin

d4411: grow, increase, big; elder kin

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4411
Comparative input*per-u-k(k); *per-V / *pēr; kinship derivatives
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantitye / mixed by formation
C2 identity / structurer / singleton
Following vowelu/i/unknown
Root/formation shapeCVC-u-K / CVC-V / CVVC
Grammatical categoryverb/adjective/noun
Boundary evidenceShort high-u grow formation independently matched; free/long big and elder compounds receive separate formation classes.
Input classmixed-or-uncertain-quantity
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil peruku/perukku, Malayalam perukuka and Telugu perugu independently share e-r-u-k. Konda pergi and Kolami perg corroborate consonantal derivatives. Long *pēr is independently distinct from the short grow verb.

Direction. Multiple branches support p-V-r, and Telugu perugu/pergu retains it even after medial syncope. Old Telugu perddaḷ supplies medial r before dd in a different elder formation, supporting an internal-assimilation history for pedda.

Derivation and relative chronology. *per-uk > perug(u) > pergu retains order; it does not become **preggu. *per-tt > perdd > pedd gives the elder series schematically, supported by inscriptional perddaḷ. Other penu/penn/pemme/peccu derivatives may involve nasal/labial/palatal assimilation. Kui prēnḍa elder male is displaced-looking but its exact input vowel and quantity are not independently identical to grow *peruku.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a genuine short-root high-u retained Telugu control, explicitly cited as nonapplication by PSS83 p.229. Loss of V2 alone is therefore insufficient to force metathesis. Elder kinship and person compounds add no independent roots. Telugu heccu/eccu, central pedda and Gondi peddal may involve borrowing or medial reduction; do not assert a hidden pr stage. Kui prēnḍa versus Kolami perendā supports a formation comparison, but ancient a versus e still requires independent reconstruction. The imported perl/peru HTML fragments are not extra Telugu forms.

Mechanism scope. Genuine retained grow formation; internal assimilation and uncertain kinship displacement elsewhere.

Scholarly references. PSS83 p.229 §16.1.2; DEDR 4411; K03 *per-V/*pēr

d4418 — bone, hard stone of fruit

d4418: bone, hard stone of fruit

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4418
Comparative input*peẓ/ṛ-V-n; plural -k
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantitye / short
C2 identity / structureẓ/ṛ / singleton
Following vowele/a/unknown
Root/formation shapeCVC-V-n
Grammatical categorynoun
Boundary evidenceSingular n versus plural k is morphological, not independent roots.
Input classshort-C-initial-other-apical
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for regional order; medium for segment, low for exact V2
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatregional-vowel-input-uncertain

Independent input evidence. Gondi peṛeŋka/peṛeka and Konda peṛen independently establish p-e-apical-V-n/k. No southern cognate in this group uniquely establishes underlying ẓ rather than another source of regional ṛ, or low a rather than e in V2.

Direction. Full Gondi/Konda forms support earlier p-V-ṛ before Kui/Kuvi/Pengo/Manda pṛēn. Kuvi pēṛnu retains postvocalic ṛ but has long quantity, whose age is not independently established.

Derivation and relative chronology. *peṛ-V-n > pṛēn by vowel loss/reassociation and contraction gives the eastern series. Kui/Kuvi plurals pṛēka replace/omit the singular nasal before number morphology; they are not additional metathesis etyma. Gondi peṛeŋka > penˀka/pɛnka permits medial apical loss; long Kuvi pēṛnu could reflect independent contraction, undoing of a cluster or an older grade.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A good regional order comparison, weaker exact input class. Kui ē without lowering cannot falsify the low-a rule unless V2 a is independently established; K03 *peẓ-an is a scholarly reconstruction to test, not independently observed a. Do not call Kuvi pēṛnu a certain reversal of metathesis or certain long-root exception. Nihali bone loans are not independent Dravidian languages or ancestral witnesses.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

d4430 — talk, prattle, command

d4430: talk, prattle, command

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4430
Comparative input*pēc / *pēẓ; short expressive variants distinct
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantityē / long independently established
C2 identity / structureẓ/c / singleton
Following vowelu/zero
Root/formation shapeCVVC / CVVC-V
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceDo not invent a short *peral prattle derivative; expressive formations separate.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for long input; low for Telugu added-r history

Eligibility / caveatlong-input-secondary-r-uncertain

Independent input evidence. Tamil pēcu/pēccu, Malayalam pēcuka, Kannada pēẓ and Kuvi pēl independently establish a long first vowel. The exact relationship between c and ẓ series is itself reconstructed, while Telugu prēlu retains l in addition to its initial r.

Direction. Long p-V-apical order is broadly supported. An ancestral short **per-al cannot be inferred from Telugu prēlu alone, and metathesis of a single ẓ does not by itself explain both r and l in prēlu.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *pēẓ > pēlu with lateral development, then secondary r > prēlu on literary Cr models; alternatively a distinct short derivative or analogical influence from homophonous burst prēlu d4194. These are hypotheses. Kota peṛc versus pe·c suggests internal cluster/quantity complexity but does not supply the exact two-liquid Telugu input.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A long-input and segment-count residual, not a secure case of long-vowel metathesis. The burst and prattle homophones cannot be merged or used to repair each other without historical semantic evidence. Toda is explicitly alternatively compared with d4003 and remains uncertain. Kurux short reduplicative prattle verbs may be expressive formations distinct from long command pēsnā.

Mechanism scope. Possible secondary r or analogical contamination, not established metathesis.

Scholarly references. DEDR 4430; K03 *pēc/*pēẓ; comparison DEDR 4194; K61 secondary-r model n.80

d4438: god, spirit, demon

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4438
Comparative input*pēy / regional *pēn; Kuvi plural pēn-ka
Initial consonantp
V1 quality / quantityē / long regional root; Pengo short
C2 identity / structuren/y / nasal in immediate Kuvi input; deeper n/y uncertain
Following vowelzero/u
Root/formation shapeCVVC + plural-k(a)
Grammatical categorynoun
Boundary evidenceIndependently attested singular nasal stem plus consonantal plural suffix; source retained and displaced plurals.

Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for immediate Kuvi nasal and length

Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-long-nasal-plural

Independent input evidence. Gondi pēn, Pengo pen and Kui pēnu independently establish a regional nasal stem; Kuvi itself has pēnu and retained plural pēṇka/pēnka. Tamil pēy and other southern y forms make the deeper nasal-versus-glide reconstruction uncertain, without undermining the immediate Kuvi nasal input.

Direction. The singular stem and retained plural supply vowel-before-nasal order inside the same paradigm. pṇēka has no inherited initial cluster in that paradigm.

Derivation and relative chronology. Kuvi pēn-u + -ka > pēn-ka > pṇē-ka, with the vowel and nasal changing order in the consonantal plural formation and n/ṇ place variation. The explicit pēṇka/pṇēka alternatives are especially useful. Kui pēnu:pēnga and Gondi pēn:-k keep the vowel before the nasal. Tamil pēcci involves a separate strong derivative.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This long-vowel nasal plural process falls outside the older narrow Telugu lexical domain. The data establish a morphological distribution, not a dated innovation or contemporary productivity. The surface plural can alternatively be modeled as stem allomorphy learned after a historical reordering; it is not eight independent etyma. DEDR parser truncates S. pēnka closing punctuation. No Telugu attestation in this entry is not a retained Telugu outcome. Possible pēy/pēn versus Parji vē̃d5530 connections and cult-term diffusion need separate reconstruction.

Mechanism scope. Direct paradigm supports long vowel–nasal reordering; stem allomorphy and phonetic implementation not independently dated.

Scholarly references. DEDR4438; PSS83 p.232 n.5; Hume2004 p.225

d4449: louse, flea

PropertyAnnotation

C2 identity / structuren / nasal
Following vowelzero/u

Input classnasal-or-nasal-cluster-input

Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-long-nasal-plural

Independent input evidence. Tamil pēṉ, Kannada pēn, Kota pe·n, Telugu pēnu and northern pēn forms independently support long ē before n. Kuvi retained pēnu:pēnka and Konda pēni:pēnku supply the plural formation directly.

Direction. The regional full singular and retained Bisamkatak plural independently establish pēn-ka before the Sunkarametta pṇēka order. This does not assume Telugu uniquely preserves the input.

Derivation and relative chronology. pēn-u + plural-ka > pēn-ka > pṇē-ka, with the nasal preceding the long vowel and n/ṇ place variation. The displaced and retained plurals have different source/dialect labels; their coexistence in an aggregated language is not evidence of free variation in one speaker. Telugu pēnu:pēlu changes plural n to l without moving either consonant before ē.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The louse and god4438 paradigms are segmentally similar but semantically distinct roots; do not merge them as derivatives. Gondi parki/purki louse belongs to4203, not this family. Pengo/Manda short pen has regional shortening but retains vowel-nasal order. Badaga hēnu:ēnu is initial labial weakening/loss, not nasal displacement. The long louse reconstruction also attached to4395 is a database crosslink error, not independent evidence. New unlinked Kurux/Kannada Kurumba cognate candidates remain in the separate candidate ledger, without adding etyma.

Mechanism scope. Direct paradigm supports long vowel–nasal reordering; phonetic implementation and date remain unknown.

Scholarly references. DEDR4449, DED(S)3643; Kujur and Dash2025 p.119 cites Kuvi louse via Steever2019

Independent input evidence. Konda por independently supports p-o-r and corresponds semantically to eastern prā/pro/pre. It does not itself attest a following low-a vowel; the K80 *por-a input remains a reconstruction requiring support beyond the outcome.

Direction. Konda favors p-V-r before the eastern clusters, but a single retained language plus restricted regional distribution gives less robust direction than a broad cross-branch set.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *por-a > *prō > prā gives Kui/Kuvi under K80 lowering. Pengo pro preserves o, Manda pre has another vowel outcome. Kuvi pār retains r after a long vowel and may reflect cluster anaptyxis, an independent grade or contact; no unique history follows from the modern pair.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. K80 separated sell from spread d3949 (old DED3255); preserve that editorial distinction and record a family-merge sensitivity rather than counting the separation as proof of independent roots. No Telugu reflex in the linked group. Imported PSD1 reconstructions misassign a source explicitly labeled PSDII; these are not South Dravidian I attestations. Exact low-a conditioning remains unverified here.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 pp.497–499 sell comparison; DEDR 4536 explicitly separated from DED3255

Independent input evidence. Kannada poẓal directly supplies medial approximant, short o and low a. Telugu archaic pẓōl/pẓōlu retains the same approximant in the newly formed initial cluster.

Direction. The consonant identity correspondence and fuller Kannada formation support po-ẓ-al earlier than p-ẓō-l. Only one unshifted language is attested, so wider ancestral level and loan direction remain less secure than local order.

Derivation and relative chronology. *poẓ-al > *pẓōl > prōl, with later Telugu ending u. Literal rearrangement+contraction and a>o assimilation followed by first-vowel loss are alternatives; pẓ precedes merger to pr under either mechanism.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Settlement vocabulary can be borrowed. Even if Telugu borrowed an uncontracted poẓal-type stem and changed it locally, it would still witness Telugu displacement but not inherited pan-Dravidian cognacy. The queried poẓil d4558 comparison needs separate review. A dated town-name spelling would bound its own form, not date the inception of the rule.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil poẓutu, Kannada poẓtu/portu and Gondi poṛdu independently establish full and consonantal orders. The database ap-pōẓ head is a compound, not the ancestor of every member.

Direction. Comparative full apical favors proddu innovation. Kannada portu:pottu independently demonstrates that internal assimilation can create pott without a pr stage.

Derivation and relative chronology. *poẓ-t > *pẓot > proddu with stop strengthening/voicing; high-u syncope may precede exchange. Telugu poddu may lose r; eastern pod forms could instead assimilate directly. appuḍu/ippuḍu/eppuḍu have deictic boundaries and a separate reduction history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Treat deictic compounds separately; their initial ap/ep sequence cannot be scored as retained plain por. No first-member-loss rule is required for Konda podu. Long pōtu elsewhere can be contraction without initial metathesis.

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam maram, Kannada/Kodagu/Tulu mara, Gondi mara and Gadaba marin independently establish ma-r-a order; Konda maran independently supplies final n. K03 pp.150,160–161 discusses nominal n/m and dialect stress.

Direction. Widespread uncontracted mar- and matching low second vowel make *mar-an earlier than mrān. A consonant-first ancestor would require multiple independent epentheses plus a low-vowel restoration without independent motivation.

Derivation and relative chronology. *mar-an > *mrān > Telugu mrānu > mānu. Literal *mraan contraction and *marán > *marān > mrān via stress and first-vowel loss are competing implementations. Konda Araku marán versus Sova mrānu supplies a synchronic phonetic analogue, not a directly observed prehistoric time series.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not derive Telugu n from modern Tamil m: both nominal suffix types have comparative support. Telugu mrā̃ku/mā̃ku has an additional velar formation whose source must be reconstructed separately. Kuvi marnu/mrānu/mārnu preserves dialect and paradigm variation; the long-vowel mārnu type is not a retained exact short input. Kolami/Naikri māk could reflect direct internal assimilation or a borrowed/reduced mrā-type, so its lost r alone cannot prove metathesis. Kurux mann/Malto manu similarly admit medial assimilation.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.107,150,160–162 n.16; DEDR 4711(a)

Eligibility / caveatcore-secondary-nasal-warning

Independent input evidence. Tamil malaŋku and Gondi malanji establish m-a-l-a-N, with Telugu malũgu/maluga and Konda malŋu confirming medial lateral; the immediate comparative input is not nasal.

Direction. The full lateral stems support an innovation in Kui mrāu/mrānga. Kuvi mṇiya may also descend from that family but does not itself establish a nasal proto-root.

Derivation and relative chronology. *mal-aŋ > *mlaaŋ > *mrāŋ with lateral-to-rhotic development and later final changes can account for Kui mrāu:mrānga. Kuvi mṇiya would need additional nasal assimilation and vowel/ending changes; these are not independently ordered. Kurux mińj may have lost the lateral in a cluster and changed vowel, rather than metathesizing it.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not count this as primary-nasal metathesis because the current cluster contains ṇ. Fish taxonomy and differences between eel, elongated fish and tambū require field/source checking. Tulu malejji has a different ending, and Kuvi i is not predicted by simple a+a contraction; these remain genuine uncertain comparisons. Telugu high u is secondary/variable relative to independently low-a forms, not proof of a unique high-suffix input.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR4737; DED(S,N)3877

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil maẓuku/maẓukku/maẓuŋku and Kannada maẓgu independently establish a short a root, approximant and high-u/velar formation. Kannada maẓa and Tamil maẓa separately attest a low-a nominal grade.

Direction. Southern full forms and Tulu marg support m-a-apical before Telugu mrakku/mraggu. Tamil makku and Kannada maggu also show that medial apical loss can produce plain velar forms independently.

Derivation and relative chronology. *maẓ-ukk > *maẓ-kk > *mẓa-kk > mrakku; voiced mraggu may involve voicing or a different consonantal history. Telugu mrakku > makku and mraggu > maggu are possible locally supported r-loss chains, but inherited/borrowed already assimilated forms can converge on the same outputs. Nasal forms maŋku need only medial assimilation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A high-u geminate formation supports the short displaced outcome. The paired plain forms cannot all be assigned exclusively to r loss because independently plain cognates exist. Source hypothesis of old Kannada borrowing for some voiced geminate Telugu formations is relevant but unproved for this individual root. Do not merge with alveolar turn d4761 or forget d4760 simply because Telugu collapses the apicals to r and meanings overlap.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 4750; K61 pp.65–66 §1.153 voiced-geminate loan hypothesis (general, not proof for this root)

Independent input evidence. Gondi maṛso/maṛsur/māṛsāl and Malto muṛse/muṛso establish an apical after the vowel; no nasal is required by these full regional forms. The K03 *maẓc-a reconstruction is a proposal, not direct evidence for every suffix vowel.

Direction. Gondi and Malto full stems versus Kui/Kuvi mṛeh-/mlēh-like forms support movement or displacement-family reduction of a nonnasal apical. Kuvi mneha/mṇēha is not independent evidence for primary nasal input.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional *maṛ/maẓ-s-V > *mṛ/ẓV-s/h is the displacement-family comparison, with s/c>h and apical rhotic/lateral/nasal outcomes requiring separate histories. Low a to e/ē and variable length cannot be derived from one unqualified a+a contraction; a different formative, vowel change or lexical restructuring remains necessary.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Gender endings in mṛehenju/mṛehali must be separated from the shared base, not counted as separate etyma. The sparse regional distribution and competing maṇ-s versus maẓc reconstructions leave deeper cognacy and order of apical assimilation unresolved. Gondi long māṛ- may be a separate grade; it is not proof the immediate displaced input was long. Nasal variants can reflect assimilation to initial m after displacement, but that chronology is a hypothesis.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR4756; K03 reconstruction records

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil maṟa/maṟai, Malayalam maṟakka/maṟayuka and Kannada maṟe/maṟagu establish m-a-apical-a independently. Gondi māraŋg/mareŋg and Konda marg support a nasal/velar lost/hide formation.

Direction. Full southern and Gondi/Konda forms support original m-V-apical. Telugu maṟacu/maṟũgu retains that order, while Kui mrāŋga promotes the apical into a cluster.

Derivation and relative chronology. *maṯ-aŋk > *mṟāŋg > Kui mrānga. Kuvi/Pengo jāŋg and Manda dāŋg are derived by DEDR through *mṟāŋg > *mjāŋg > jāŋg (with Manda apical d); these intermediate clusters are reconstructed, unlike attested Kui mr-. Separate causative mrāk-p > mrāp-k produces Kui mrāpka. Gondi ractāl is explicitly derived by the source from *mṟac with initial m loss.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Low-a does not compel Telugu displacement. Different maṟa-cu, maṟu-k and maṟa-ŋ formations must remain distinct before interpreting exact exceptions. Eastern j/d stems support shared development more strongly when nasal/velar morphology agrees, but do not by themselves prove every language inherited an identical completed sound change. Southern and central mak/maŋ/meŋ reductions may be medial assimilation; do not force hidden mr stages. Tamil source ṛ in maṛa is a transcription inconsistency beside its clear ṟ derivatives.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 4760 and explicit *mṟāŋg>*mjāŋg note; PSS83 p.229 lexical nonapplication principle

d4761 — turn over, return, be distressed, fall

d4761: turn over, return, be distressed, fall

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4761
Comparative input*maṯ-i/u; *maṯ-aŋk; *maṯ-al
Initial consonantm
V1 quality / quantitya / short
C2 identity / structureṟ / singleton
Following voweli/u/a
Root/formation shapeCVC-i / CVC-u-K / CVC-a-NK / CVC-a-l
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceHigh-i/u, low-a nasal and second-lateral formations separately reconstructed.
Input classshort-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh for root family; medium for exact Telugu formation
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil maṟi, maṟuku, maṟaŋku and Malayalam maṟiyuka/maṟukuka independently establish several formative vowels. Kannada maral/maraḷ and Telugu maralu support a second-lateral formation.

Direction. Full southern and eastern root forms establish m-a-apical before Telugu mraŋgu/mrandu. The meanings perish/decrease overlap other m-r roots, so exact linkage must be tested rather than inferred from spelling.

Derivation and relative chronology. A short high-u/zero nasal or stop formation *maṯ-NK/ND > mraŋgu/mrandu is possible. If the exact input is instead Tamil low-a *maṟaŋku, short Telugu a requires later shortening after contraction. Telugu maralu > maḷḷu can result from medial r-l assimilation, with no initial mr stage. Kui mag-b > mabg reverses suffix consonants after a separate medial apical loss.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The short Telugu nasal-cluster outcome is not a deterministic confirmation until its V2 is fixed independently. Mraŋgu/mraggu may reflect convergence with d4750; preserve separate lexical affiliations and flag double-count risk. Kannada malar beside maral reverses the two liquids internally, a different process from initial vowel/apical displacement. Tulu marakaṇɛ/maraŋkaṇɛ is explicitly alternatively linked to d4740 and remains uncertain.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 4761; DEN1 1972 p.413 entry3898; compare DEDR 4750 and 4740

d4806 — bamboo, thorny bamboo

d4806: bamboo, thorny bamboo

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4806
Comparative inputregional *māṇ/ṛ-i; Kuvi mṇāhu formation
Initial consonantm
V1 quality / quantityā / long independently established
C2 identity / structureṇ/ṛ / nasal/rhotic singleton; immediate suffixal s cluster inferred
Following voweli / unknown
Root/formation shapeCVVC-i / CVVC-s?
Grammatical categorynoun
Boundary evidenceKuvi singular h versus plural sk; full i-ending noun is a different formation.
Input classnasal-or-nasal-cluster-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for long vowel and full order; medium for segment and formation
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-long-apical-variable

Independent input evidence. Kui māṇi/māṛi and Kuvi Ḍ. māṛi, S. mādi independently support a long vowel before an apical. Their nasal/rhotic/dental correspondences do not determine one uniquely original apical identity.

Direction. The full Kui and Kuvi forms favor m-ā-apical before Isr. mṇāhu. The ṇ could reflect promotion of an older nasal or assimilation of a promoted liquid next to m; these are distinct analyses.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *māṇ-s > *mṇā-s > mṇāhu (plural mṇāska), with an h/s stem alternation, provides a displaced nasal formation. Alternatively *māṛ-s > *mṛā-s > mṇā-s adds liquid-to-nasal assimilation. The s-formative is inferred from the Kuvi paradigm, not directly matched to full māṛi.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The long input is independently supported, so this is outside the narrow short-vowel Telugu domain. Exact noun formation and nasal chronology remain uncertain. Thorny bamboo versus a generic bamboo bush could reflect lexical specialization or borrowing. The dictionary explicitly removes Kurux mās as a pronunciation of Indo-Aryan bā̃s; it cannot be used as a northern cognate.

Mechanism scope. Long apical displacement-family; nasal before/after reordering unresolved.

Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-mixed-quantity-secondary-nasal

Independent input evidence. Tamil māḷ and Kannada māḷ independently establish a long lateral root. Tamil maṭku, Telugu malugu/malãgu/manũgu and Kuvi maṇk support shorter and nasal formations independently; the short grade is not invented from the displaced outcome.

Direction. Southern m-V-lateral forms and retained Kuvi maṇk favor m-V-apical before mṇeŋg/mṇek. Nasal identity has independent regional support but cannot simply replace the deeper lateral.

Derivation and relative chronology. Short *maḷ-k > *maṇ-k > *mṇak, or *maḷ-k > *mḷak > *mṇak, are alternatives preceding Kuvi mṇek; the a>e quality remains unexplained. The intransitive nasal-velar mṇeŋg contrasts with stronger mṇek. F. mṛakʰali has r and a and may preserve a different assimilation/quality history. Telugu retains mal/man order through its short and long formations.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kuvi e is a genuine residual, not a reason to reconstruct unsupported *meṇ. DEDR assigns these forms to the same family; the exact short-grade derivation, semantics and source differences need a fuller paradigm. Badaga buru māle naked has insufficient semantic evidence and is not counted as a cognate. Nasal/stop alternation in Tamil māḷ:māṇṭ is a morphological control, not initial metathesis.

Mechanism scope. Displacement-family supported, with unresolved a/e quality and secondary nasal chronology.

Scholarly references. DEDR4831, DED3958; source labels in panel-030

Independent input evidence. Pengo and Manda miṇiya independently give short i before nasal and i after it; Kuvi mṇīya is the displaced comparison. The database *mṇīj head follows the outcome and is not accepted as the earlier order.

Direction. Two full regional forms support miṇ-i over an inherited initial mṇ followed by two separate identical epentheses; tree-name borrowing remains an alternative source of the geographical pattern.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible *miṇ-iya > *mṇiiya > mṇīya, consistent with same-vowel contraction after nasal reordering. Literal exchange versus first-vowel loss and compensatory length is not uniquely proven by this set.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is a nasal-input case, unlike eel4737 where independent full forms have l. The sparse regional botanical comparison needs better species/dialect records, and the Kuvi database gloss loses an independent F. full form if any existed: only the printed Pengo/Manda evidence is asserted here. No Telugu attestation is a missing cell, not retention.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR4855; PSS83 p.232 n.5, DEDS785

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil miẓuŋku and Malayalam miẓuŋŋuka independently give m-i-apical-u; Konda miṛiŋ supplies an independent high-i second-vowel variant. K03 p.161 explicitly uses *miẓ-u-ŋ.

Direction. Full southern and Konda forms establish m-V-apical order. Telugu mriŋgu is innovative, and its miŋgu variant can be traced through r loss because the cluster is independently attested in Telugu.

Derivation and relative chronology. *miẓ-u-ŋk > *miẓ-ŋk > *mẓiŋk > mriŋgu > miŋgu, with nasal-stop voicing and postconsonantal ẓ>r. Konda miṛiŋ > *mṛiŋ > ṛiŋ gives first-member loss under the displacement account. Tamil/Malayalam v-initial forms need a separate labial history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not replace all historical V2 values with u: the Konda i form is real and may involve assimilation. Kannada/Kota/central miŋ(g) can result directly from medial ẓ loss, or contact with Telugu, so matching modern Telugu miŋgu is not independent proof of concealed metathesis. Pengo ṛuggiŋga/ṛugginda is explicitly onomatopoeic and has different vowels/formation. Tamil English gloss words consume/devour are parser errors, not linguistic witnesses.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.161–162; K61 pp.61–64; DEDR 4866

Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule

Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-nasal-mixed-formation

Independent input evidence. Tamil miṉ/miṉuŋku, Malayalam minnuka and Kannada minugu establish a nasal root and short/long formation contrast independently. Kuvi miṇs, miṇig and mirsi coexist with mṇih/mṇīh and supply especially close regional input evidence.

Direction. The full nasal root across southern languages and retained Kuvi miṇs favor pre-vowel nasal promotion for mṇih. Gondi/Konda r/ḍ variants show that the apical may change identity before or after reordering; their existence does not prove all Kuvi nasals are secondary.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional miṇ-s > mṇi-s with h~st stem alternation can yield mṇih (mṇist-). The Isr. long mṇīh requires separate length or earlier vowel-coalescence history, not automatically the long star root. Telugu minuku:minku shows medial syncope retaining m-i-n order; miḍũgu versus miṇũgu involves nasal/stop change without metathesis. North bīnko/bínḍke has initial m>b and suffixal/cluster developments, not nasal promotion.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep short shine and long star formations separate. The fish reconstruction linked in this entry should not replace shine-root quantity; possible common origin with4885 is sensitivity only. Kuvi mrih has rhotic rather than nasal, and full mirsi could precede it by the ordinary nonnasal process; the exact order of n>r and reordering is not independently dated. mṇispu spelling lightening is the source gloss, not a different weather concept. Tulu broken HTML fragments miṇ&lt/kuni/&gt are not independent lexical forms.

Mechanism scope. Short nasal reordering supported; long variant and n/r chronology unresolved.

Scholarly references. DEDR4876 p.435 directly read; PSS83 p.232 n.5

d4885: fish

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4885
Comparative input*mīn; Kuvi mīn-ka
Initial consonantm
V1 quality / quantityī / long independently attested; Pengo/Manda short
C2 identity / structuren / nasal
Following vowelzero/u
Root/formation shapeCVVC + plural-k(a)
Grammatical categorynoun

Input classnasal-or-nasal-cluster-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatlate-kuvi-long-nasal-plural

Independent input evidence. Tamil mīṉ, Malayalam/Kannada mīn, Telugu mīnu and the Gondi/Konda/Kui forms independently establish long vowel before nasal. Kuvi singular mīnu and retained S. plural mīnka establish the immediate morphological input without relying on a reconstruction.

Direction. The full singular and alternative plural mīnka make m-n-ī in mnīka innovative. F. mrīka has secondary rhotic in the displaced cluster, not an independently primary r root.

Derivation and relative chronology. mīn-u + -ka > mīn-ka > mnī-ka, with dialectal mṇīka and mrīka requiring place/rhotic developments. Isr. singular mṇīnu retains the old postvocalic n as well as cluster ṇ: it is plausibly remodeled from the plural, or has nasal excrescence, rather than a literal one-for-one exchange. Kui mīnu:mīnga and Konda mīn:mīnga retain order.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The singular cluster variant must not count as independent confirmation of a swap because it contains two nasals. Distinguishing analogical backformation from phonetic excrescence needs chronology and paradigms across speakers. Fish4885 and shine/star4876 may be historically related through bright/scaly semantics, but this is not established; merge only in a sensitivity partition. DEDR main parser omits Gadaba/Gondi/Konda and strands Isr. forms in glosses; source-restored observations preserve the complete printed paradigms. Sanskrit mīna is a contact comparison, not a Dravidian language denominator.

Mechanism scope. Direct long vowel–nasal plural reordering; secondary cluster place change and possible singular analogy.

Scholarly references. DEDR4885 p.436 directly read; PSS83 p.232 n.5; Hume2004 p.225

d4968 — hare

d4968: hare

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd4968
Comparative input*muc/y-al; regional *mol/mor-Vl, K80 *moẓ-al
Initial consonantm
V1 quality / quantityu/o / short
C2 identity / structuresecondary l/r, earlier c/y / singleton
Following vowela/o
Root/formation shapeCVC-a-l
Grammatical categorynoun
Boundary evidenceTwo-liquid regional formation descends from a palatal/glide root; stages must precede a narrow-apical classification.
Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for broad order; medium for secondary-apical intermediate
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatsecondary-apical-regional

Independent input evidence. Tamil mucal/muyal and Malayalam muyal independently support a low-a final-l formation with medial c/y. Gondi molol/malol and Konda morol establish a regional two-liquid stage before initial clusters. K80 *moẓ-al is a scholarly intermediate, not a directly attested Proto-Dravidian root.

Direction. Full southern and Gondi/Konda forms favor m-V-C-V-l before Kui mṛāḍu and Kuvi mrālu. Regional apical identity is clearer than its exact relation to the southern palatal/glide.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional *mor-al/ol > *mrōl > mrālu gives Kui/Kuvi with lowering and Kui final l>ḍ; Pengo mrōl retains the mid vowel. The deeper *mucal > moyal > regional molol/morol requires palatal weakening plus assimilation/rhotacism, whose order relative to metathesis is not directly dated. Central/northern nasal forms reflect other c/nc developments.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. No Telugu attestation in this group. The independently low-a southern ending supports a historical formation, but reconstructing first-syllable o rather than u needs the umlaut/relative chronology argument. Do not classify this as ordinary inherited PDr apical metathesis without the secondary-apical stages. K80 p.498 additionally quotes Indi mnāl/mnōl, absent from this group; later nasal clusters need separate source annotation.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 p.498 item15; DEDR 4968; K03 *muc-Vl/*moy-al
