Independent input evidence. Tamil muraṭu, Malayalam muraṭu and Kannada moraḍu independently establish a full low-a dental formation; Telugu moraḍu retains the same order.

Direction. Full agreement favors Telugu mrōḍu innovation; Kui mrōjo independently has cluster order in the tree-base meaning.

Derivation and relative chronology. *mor-aḍ > mrōḍ by displacement/coalescence. Kui mrōjo adds dental-palatal correspondence. Nasal moṇḍi can reflect a separate assimilated derivative and is not proof of a previous mr stage.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Exact full/cluster Telugu pair supports direction and quantity, but coexistence requires lexical/formation history: the stump submeaning changes while broader rough derivatives retain r medially. Do not define a phonological class by that outcome. Gravel words have Indo-Aryan comparisons and need separate transmission study.

Independent input evidence. Tamil muraṟci and Tulu murajɛ independently supply a low-a formative; Gondi moros/moras/maronj gives matching regional rhotic and final s/nj formations. First-vowel u/o/a variation remains important.

Direction. Tamil/Tulu/Gondi establish m-V-r before Kui mrāsu. Kuvi database marcu preserves m-a-r, while K80 prints a long-vowel form in the same comparison.

Derivation and relative chronology. Regional *mor-a-s > *mrōs > mrās gives Kui under K80 lowering. K80’s deeper *mut-a/*mot-a > *mor-a requires a separate t/r correspondence argument. Kuvi marcu may retain order; the long form cited by K80 may reflect a different quantity grade or metathesis followed by vowel reinsertion, neither demonstrated.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Kui direction is plausible with strong suffix support, but not all branches share the same material or rope construction. The Kui leather rope versus Gondi tree fibre could reflect semantic specialization or contact. Telugu is unattested here. Preserve discrepancy between short database Kuvi marcu and long K80 spelling instead of silently normalizing it or counting two independent roots.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Telugu mola, Konda mola and Gondi molkī establish medial l; Kolami/Naikri mulke and Parji mulka preserve the cluster needed for the Brahui comparison.

Direction. Full regional l and lk support loss of cluster-initial l in Brahui mux, without requiring initial ml-.

Derivation and relative chronology. *mul-k > *muk > mux by lateral loss and velar frication is Emeneau 1997 p.441 §2.2. Regional o/u and Telugu malugu/malumu require vowel/derivational histories independent of metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Brahui mux is an opaque other development, not a retained-apical negative and not evidence for hidden metathesis. The independently attested lk cluster makes direct lateral loss economical. Duplicate DEDR and 1997 records of mux supply one family-language observation.

Mechanism scope. Medial l loss before k; no independent evidence of initial metathesis.

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil muẓuku, Malayalam muẓukuka, Kannada muẓuŋgu and Gondi muṛuŋg independently establish m-u-apical-u. Tulu murk and Konda muṛg/muṛk support a medial consonant-cluster branch.

Direction. Full SD I and Gondi/Konda forms establish earlier m-V-apical; Telugu bruŋgu has a moved apical and an additional initial m>b change. Full muḍũgu remains in Telugu itself.

Derivation and relative chronology. *muẓ-u-ŋk > *muẓ-ŋk > *mẓuŋk > *mruŋg > bruŋgu; the initial denasalization m>b is separate (K61 p.28 §1.69). Alternatively vowel contraction and later shortening before NK can give the same short output. Bruncu has a different stronger transitive formation. Telugu muṇugu/munũgu and southern muŋg/mukk can arise by medial assimilation without initial metathesis.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This is another independent same-u short outcome, contradicting obligatory surface ū but not uniquely deciding syncope versus contraction plus shortening. Kui bṛuḍga adds a retroflex stop whose origin cannot be read off the Telugu ŋg; Kuvi mrūkʰali differs in quantity and suffix/aspiration. The shared initial b in Telugu and Kui is suggestive but insufficient to choose inheritance, independent denasalization or contact. None of the surviving mu-initial assimilated forms can be labeled hidden metathesis without separate evidence.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K61 p.28 §1.69, pp.61–64; K03 *muẓ-u-nk/nkk; DEDR 4993

Independent input evidence. Tamil muṟi, Telugu muṟiki/muṟugu, Gondi murk and Tulu murguni independently support full apical order and consonantal variants.

Direction. Full and cluster comparanda favor Telugu mrukku innovation; r-less muggu has a direct internal assimilation alternative.

Derivation and relative chronology. *muṟ-k > mrukk with reordering/strengthening; *muṟ-ik > *muṟk by syncope is possible. mrukku > mukku is supported by the pair, while muggu could arise directly as in Kannada muggu.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Distinguish same-surface ripen mruggu5017/5046 from mouldy mrukku. Dirt and putrefaction meanings fit one family, but cannot fix vowel deletion chronology. Long mūri stench is a separate grade.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Independent input evidence. Tamil mel/meli/melku, Malayalam mel/meliyuka, Kannada mel/melu/melpu and Kota melg:melk independently support e-l and a velar formation.

Direction. Brahui bēɣ- can be derived directly from medial mel-k; Kui mṛērna has a cluster absent from the full comparanda but its exact formative is uncertain.

Derivation and relative chronology. Emeneau 1997 p.442 §4 derives *mel-k > *bel-k > bēɣ with front-vowel-conditioned m>b, e>ē and cluster lateral loss. The exact order of lengthening and loss is not proved. Kui *mel-V-r/n > *mlV-r/n > mṛērna is a possible displacement comparison, with suffix and long ē still underdetermined.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The database reconstruction *mēl high/west is a wrong homonymous association, excluded. Strong mell- adverbs are not independent root votes. Brahui ē is not proof of a long proto-root: Emeneau treats it as the reflex of earlier short e under a contact-affected vowel inventory. Gadaba mellaga may be a Telugu loan; source checking is needed.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR5078; Emeneau1997 pp.441–442 §§2.1–4

d5082: smear, plaster, wax

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd5082
Comparative input*meẓ-u-k; other *meẓ-V-nḍ/ŋk/w formations
Initial consonantm

C2 identity / structureẓ / singleton
Following vowelu / unknown

Eligibility / caveatvowel-input-uncertain

Independent input evidence. Tamil meẓuku, Malayalam meẓukuka and Konda miṛis independently establish an apical root and high-vowel formations. No compared form independently supplies the exact low-a formative required by K80 *meẓ-a for the Telugu/Kui long outputs.

Direction. Southern and Konda/Brahui full forms favor m-V-apical before Telugu mrē- and Kui mrānḍa. Thus order is firmer than exact quantity/formative conditioning.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *meẓ-a-ŋk > *mẓēŋk > mrē̃gu > mē̃gu gives Telugu if low a is justified; *meẓ-a-nḍ > *mẓēnḍ > mrānḍa adds Kui lowering. High-u/zero inputs could instead involve other contraction/lengthening routes. Telugu mrēvu has a different final labial development, not a free substitute for ŋg. Kuvi mrispi matches the high-i Konda form more closely.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A real quantity/formative residual: do not use long ē/ā to manufacture the a whose prediction is being tested. Telugu mēdu could be another formation or internal assimilation and is uncertain. Kolami mēg/Naikri mēgh may be old Telugu loans or independently medially reduced forms. Kuvi mṇek introduces a nasal not directly expected from ẓ, so its cognacy/assimilation needs separate evidence.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K80 p.498 item17; DEDR 5082; PSS83 parenthesized a reconstruction discussed in prior source audit

Eligibility / caveatcore-cluster-secondary-nasal

Independent input evidence. Tamil moḷ and Malto mulɣe independently establish vowel-before-lateral order across southern and northern branches. Malto also supports a velar extension independently of the eastern clusters.

Direction. The two separated full comparisons favor *mVḷ-k before eastern ml/mr/mṇ forms. A deeper nasal root is not independently supported by these witnesses.

Derivation and relative chronology. *mo/uḷ-k > *mḷo/uk > Kui mluk, Pengo/Manda mṛuk; Kuvi mṇok adds lateral-to-nasal assimilation before or after cluster formation. Kuvi mrokʰ-nai retains a rhotic alternative. Root o/u and the gloss merge in Schulze need separate scrutiny.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. This case cannot be counted as independent evidence that inherited nasals entered the original Telugu rule: the comparative input is lateral. Whether Kuvi assimilated a liquid after promotion or had a preexisting nasal allomorph is unresolved. DEDR3790 noḷ is an explicitly suggested comparison; initial m/n variation and semantics require review before merging families.

Mechanism scope. Consonantal apical displacement-family plus secondary nasal assimilation in Kuvi.

Scholarly references. DEDR5124, DED(S)4209; comparison3790 not merged

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible older *mVr-a > *mrā followed by rhotic/nasal variation is only a schematic hypothesis. Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Leave the earlier input and presence of historical reordering unresolved. Needed: an independently cognate full root, regular r/n correspondences and the semantics of the mouse compound. Do not infer borrowing simply to avoid the missing input, or use the already clustered proto-head as evidence of a Telugu-like change.

d5153 — year; this/last/next year compounds

d5153: year; this/last/next year compounds

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd5153
Comparative input*yĀṇṭ-u; K80 *nīt-yāṇṭ > *nir-ēṇḍ/*nir-ōṇḍ
Initial consonanty/zero; compound n
V1 quality / quantityā/ē/ō; compound i / long bare root; compound first-member quantity unresolved
C2 identity / structureṇṭ; compound r / singleton
Following vowelcompound boundary
Root/formation shape(C)VVNC / CVC#VVNC
Grammatical categorynoun/adverb

Input classnonapical-or-uncertain-input
Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidencehigh for year; low for exact completed-year compound stages
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatcompound-process-separate

Independent input evidence. Tamil yāṇṭu/āṇṭu, Kodagu āṇḍɨ and Telugu ēṇḍu independently establish the long year root. Last-year r-initial forms contain additional material; the year root itself has no r that could be simply transposed to its beginning.

Direction. K80 p.498 item18 proposes completed+year *nīt-yāṇṭ with regional nir-ēṇḍ/nir-ōṇḍ and quotes Konda nṛund. This supports a compound-based comparison, but the exact full compound and shortening are not independently attested in the present group.

Derivation and relative chronology. Bare *yĀṇṭ > āṇṭ/ēṇḍ/ōnḍ retains order after glide/vowel changes. Conditional *nir#ōṇḍ > *nrōṇḍ > ṛōnḍ and lowered ṛānḍ gives the last-year forms; merger, shortening and resegmentation at the compound boundary must be separately justified. Pengo/Manda ṛāṭihiŋ has further suffix and nasal-loss history.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not count last-year as ordinary metathesis of the bare year root or use its morphology-free head to test a vowel rule. Kui ṛānḍu last year versus ṛōnḍu previous year preserve a meaning distinction, potentially analogical rather than free phonetic variation. K80 prints Kui twice where the second set appears to be Kuvi; DEDR independently confirms Kuvi r-initial forms. Corpus-wide Konda gloss search last year returned zero; K80 nṛund is a source-only observation. Complete-root component remains to be independently linked.

Mechanism scope. Bare root retention; proposed compound metathesis requires separate denominator.

Scholarly references. K80 p.498 item18 directly visually checked; DEDR 5153

d5159 — river, water, thirst

d5159: river, water, thirst

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd5159
Comparative input*yĀṯ-u, oblique *yĀṯṯ-; regional *ēṯ
Initial consonanty/zero
V1 quality / quantityā/ē / long
C2 identity / structureṟ/ṯ / singleton
Following vowelu/zero
Root/formation shape(C)VVC / (C)VVCC

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil yāṟu/āṟu with oblique ṟṟ, Malayalam āṟu, Telugu ēṟu/ēṭi and Gondi yēr/yēt independently establish long quantity and an apical paradigm. The difference ā/ē is linked to the special initial-y vowel correspondence, not to metathesis.

Direction. Long vowel precedes the apical across branches. Loss of initial y in southern forms does not move the apical, and eastern j/y/z/s reflexes remain after the vowel.

Derivation and relative chronology. *yĀṯu > āṟu/ēṟu retains order after initial glide loss and regional vowel developments. Oblique fortition gives Tamil āṟṟu and Telugu ēṭi. Kui ēju/ēsu and Pengo ēz/ēs show apical changes without initial displacement.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. A strong long-vowel control across Telugu and eastern languages. Tulu tārɯ/sārɯ/hārɯ add or preserve initial material requiring separate local explanation, but final r stays postvocalic. Gondi and central big-river compounds combine this root with per/bere big; do not screen that compound-initial per as the river input. Badaga proper names are not independent basic reflexes. Imported goat reconstruction is erroneous metadata.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 5159; K03 initial *yĀ and apical-oblique correspondence

d5263: write, draw lines, scratch

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd5263
Comparative input*war-ay; *war-i and other scratching formations
Initial consonantw
V1 quality / quantitya / short
C2 identity / structurer / singleton
Following vowela/i
Root/formation shapeCVC-ay / CVC-i
Grammatical categoryverb/noun
Boundary evidenceLow-ay write versus high-i scratch/test formations independently attested; derivatives and recipient writing vocabulary not independent roots.
Input classshort-C-initial-r-rhotics-retroflex-approximant
Telugu hypothesiseligible; obligatory application predicts D
Input confidencehigh
Overall confidencehigh
Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil varai and Malayalam varayuka independently establish low-a drawing formation; Kannada bare and Tulu barepini corroborate labial-V-r order. Tamil vari independently establishes a high-i counterpart.

Direction. Multiple southern forms support var- before Telugu vrā-. The coexistence of vrāyu/rāyu directly supports subsequent loss of the first cluster member, unlike Telugu finger vrēlu>vēlu.

Derivation and relative chronology. *war-ay > *wrāy > vrāyu > rāyu. Writing nouns vrā̃ta/vrālu and causative vrāyincu have distinct suffix histories. Telugu variyu metal-testing preserves the high-i formation. Kui vrīsa/Kuvi brīnai has high ī and different suffix history, potentially *war-i versus a different earlier vowel grade.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. One first-member-loss word does not establish a universal low-vowel rule for wr clusters. Literacy vocabulary readily diffuses: Gondi/Konda/Kuvi rās/rāc and Gadaba rāyap may be Telugu exports or reflect local developments. Gondi varasānā retains full order, but its relation to a possible borrowed rās is uncertain. Telugu baruku and Parji varc have explicit alternative d5322 etymologies. Badaga finger/place-name homonyms attached to this group are not writing reflexes.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K61 pp.67–68; K03 pp.157–158; PSS83 pp.230–231; DEDR 5263

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil vaẓi and Kannada baẓi/baẓicu/baẓacu establish w/b-V-ẓ and different vowel-bearing extensions. Telugu vẓaccu preserves the identity of the promoted approximant before its merger with r.

Direction. Independent southern medial ẓ plus old Telugu cluster vẓ supports displacement before postconsonantal ẓ>r. The surviving cluster consonant is stronger direction evidence than a modern r alone.

Derivation and relative chronology. A consonantal *waẓ-cc > *wẓacc > vraccu accounts for short a with cc; alternatively high-i syncope could precede the consonantal stage. Kannada baẓacu has low a and cannot be mechanically chosen as the exact immediate Telugu input without explaining the short output. Telugu baḍiyu retains V before the apical in a different ritual sweeping formation.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The exact causative/input vowel remains a substantive uncertainty; old cluster spelling does not solve it. Inscriptional vẓ/vr dates need separate localization. Badaga bāku may have medial assimilation/loss and lengthening rather than initial metathesis. Toda poṛt ud contains the comparison in a compound; bare ud must not be counted as another independent reflex of waẓ.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 5295; K61 pp.67–68; K03 p.158 apical reflex table

Independent input evidence. Tamil vāẓ and Kannada bāẓ establish long root; Kannada barduku/barduŋku and baẓduŋku independently support a short expanded apical-dental formation.

Direction. Kannada barduku favors Telugu braduku reordering without projecting the long bare-root vowel onto this derivative. Possible early regional borrowing would still permit local displacement.

Derivation and relative chronology. *bar-d-uk > bra-d-uk, with initial w>b and apical development preceding or independent of the observed order change; bratuku has dental voicing variation. baduku/batuku can be direct apical loss or later cluster loss.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The apical is followed by d and a further u-k suffix: morphology is crucial. The apparent Telugu b&lt, br&lt and &gt are transcription/editorial fragments, not forms. Neither Arabic barkat cross-reference nor unrelated Badaga place names establish cognacy.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

d5409 — finger

d5409: finger

PropertyAnnotation
Primary familyd5409
Comparative input*wir/wer-al; distinct *wir-and/anj derivatives
Initial consonantw

C2 identity / structurer / singleton
Following vowela

Grammatical categorynoun

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil/Malayalam viral, Kannada beral/beraḷ and Tulu berel independently establish initial labial, V, rhotic, then a second vowel/liquid. Gondi varanj/virinj and regional *-and/anj forms are different formations. K03 pp.101–106 explains historical i/e ambiguity.

Direction. The full southern forms and retained Gondi/Konda variants support labial–vowel–rhotic order. Telugu vrēlu reverses the relative vowel/rhotic order, and vēlu is its documented cluster-reduced counterpart.

Derivation and relative chronology. Immediate *wer-al > *wrēl > vrēlu > vēlu. Deeper *wir-al > *wer-al lowering is one analysis; ancestral e is an alternative where southern vowel mergers obscure the contrast. Simple initial-vowel deletion from weral would give wral with wrong quality; prior a>e assimilation plus deletion gives wrēl without literal exchange.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. The exact mechanism remains underdetermined but plain deletion alone is inadequate. Konda veṛska versus ṛeska/ṛaska permits *vṛ- > ṛ- with first-member loss; exact a/e suffix history differs from Telugu -al. Kui vanju/Kuvi vansu and Central vande admit medial r assimilation in a nasal-stop formation; they are not secure concealed initial metathesis. Toda pēḷ can likewise arise by medial r loss and contraction. Badaga bēru index finger has a competing relation to full beralu or another finger-name root.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. K03 pp.101–106,483; K61 pp.61–62,67; PSS83 ch.15; DEDR 5409

Eligibility / caveatcore

Independent input evidence. Tamil viri, Malayalam viriyuka, Kannada biri and Konda viris/virs independently establish w-i-r and high-vowel formations. The extra lateral in Telugu vrīlu requires a derivative, and K61 explicitly says the proposed -il/-ul is unattested elsewhere.

Direction. Many branches agree on w-V-r before Telugu/Kui/Kuvi vr-. Telugu virugu/viriyu retains order alongside vrīlu. An earlier *vir-il is a published immediate antecedent, not an independently verified Proto-Dravidian word.

Derivation and relative chronology. Conditional *wir-il > *wrīl > vrīlu gives the long displaced Telugu form if the suffix is established. *wir-i-nk > *wriŋk gives Kui vringa, while labial vrīva has its own quantity/formative history. Gondi rīk can follow *wrīk with w loss; source suffix comparison remains needed. Telugu viccu/vippu/vikku permits direct medial assimilation, independently paralleled by Kannada biccu and Tulu biccuni.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Do not claim deterministic output conditioning from a suffix reconstructed only to yield ī. The broader displacement interpretation is stronger than the exact vowel/derivative chronology. Gondi rīk could involve regional borrowing or a distinct velar derivative; retain medium confidence. Kui birasakali is unshifted-looking but expressive/deverbal formation may differ. Sanskrit aravinda comparison concerns a compound and adds no independent root vote.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 5411; K61 p.67 §1.156 explicitly unattested derivative (prior verified reading); DEN1 1972 p.415 entry4438

d5555: throw, strike, discharge

PropertyAnnotation

Boundary evidenceExact formative correspondence discussed in derivation; not inferred from output.

Telugu hypothesisoutside narrow classical Telugu domain; no D prediction from that rule
Input confidenceComparative order and exact formation confidence distinguished in support and exception notes
Overall confidencemedium
Eligibility / caveatsecondary-r-input-unresolved

Independent input evidence. Konda vey and Kuvi ve/vēp independently supply a nonrhotic root. Telugu vēyu/vaicu likewise has no medial r.

Direction. Te vrēyu/vrēṭu adds r absent from the comparative input; neither the glide nor dental can simply exchange with a vowel to supply it.

Derivation and relative chronology. Possible analogical r in vēyu>vrēyu followed by derivative spread, or older fuller root/compound not yet identified. Labial/dental suffix alternations in eastern forms do not independently establish r.

Exceptions and discriminating evidence. Keep A, including vrēṭu strike noun and compound. Need early full rhotic witness or a demonstrable analogical model. Modern Telugu r-less variants cannot alone establish r loss as the first history.

Mechanism scope. Target initial-order comparison; literal exchange, assimilation and syncope distinguished in the derivation and language notes

Scholarly references. DEDR 5555; current comparative cluster panel
